Line 6865: C. Proposed Restructuring. The Members have carefully considered and determined that it is in the best interest of the Company and the Fund to undertake a comprehensive restructuring of the management company structure and a realignment of economics among the principals of the Ardent Capital platform (the "Restructuring"). The Restructuring has been developed in consultation with Calderwood & Harkness LLP, restructuring counsel for the Company, and involves four principal workstreams: (i) entity restructuring, including the formation of a parent holding company and an intermediate holding entity to create a more durable and scalable organizational architecture; (ii) economics realignment, including the reallocation of carried interest, management fee profit-sharing, and co-investment rights among continuing and next-generation principals; (iii) departing principal separations, including the negotiation and execution of separation and release agreements, carry retention arrangements, and restrictive covenant agreements with two departing principals; and (iv) LP consent and side-letter compliance, including LPAC notification and consent, limited partner notifications, and compliance with expanded key-person and management change provisions contained in the Fund's side letters.

C. Proposed Restructuring. The Members have carefully considered and determined that it is in the best interest of the Company and the Fund to undertake a comprehensive restructuring of the management company structure and a realignment of economics among the principals of the Ardent Capital platform (the "Restructuring"). The Restructuring has been developed in consultation with Calderwood & Harkness LLP, restructuring counsel for the Company, and involves four principal workstreams: (i) entity restructuring, including the formation of a parent holding company and an intermediate holding entity to create a more durable and scalable organizational architecture; (ii) economics realignment, including the reallocation of carried interest, management fee profit-sharing, and co-investment rights among continuing and next-generation principals; (iii) departing principal separations, including the negotiation and execution of separation and release agreements, carry retention arrangements, and restrictive covenant agreements with two departing principals; and (iv) LP consent and side-letter compliance, including LPAC notification and consent, limited partner notifications, and compliance with expanded key-person and management change provisions contained in the Fund's side letters.

G. LPAC Consent. In compliance with this requirement, LPAC notification and consent solicitation letters were sent to all four LPAC members on February 5, 2024, together with supporting documentation including the Restructuring Options Memorandum prepared by Calderwood & Harkness LLP. LPAC consent was obtained at a virtual meeting held on February 14, 2024, at which all four LPAC members were present and voted unanimously in favor of the Restructuring. **Searching asset management data**

I'm thinking about how to search for "Funds & Asset Management" and break it down by matter anchors. It seems like creating an index per matter could work well by extracting information from the corpus based on matter path boundaries. I could use Python to generate a .txt file for each matter and filter sections with regex. I’ll also want to build matter-index metadata, collecting filenames and analyzing counts of occurrences for relevant terms. Once that’s set up, I'll be able to output a compact index.

1: CONFIDENTIAL
2: 
3: **CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** **Attorneys at Law** 555 California Street, 40th Floor San Francisco, CA 94104 Telephone: (415) 392-7800 Facsimile: (415) 392-7801 www.calderwoodharkness.com
4: 
5: September 29, 2025
6: 
7: Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC 2400 Sand Hill Road, Suite 320 Menlo Park, CA 94025
8: 
9: > Attention: Rajesh Mehta, Co-Founder & Managing Partner
10: >
11: > Claire Dubois, Co-Founder & Managing Partner
12: 
13: **Re: Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP --- Side Letter Agreements and Most Favored Nation Election Framework for Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP**
14: 
15: Dear Mr. Mehta and Ms. Dubois:
16: 
17: **[1. Purpose and Confirmation of Engagement]{.underline}**
18: 
19: Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the \"GP\"), in its capacity as the general partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the \"Fund\"), in connection with the negotiation, preparation, and documentation of side letter agreements with certain anchor limited partners of the Fund and the structuring and documentation of the most favored nation (\"MFN\") election framework applicable to qualifying limited partners of the Fund, each as more fully described in Section 2 below.
20: 
21: The Fund was organized pursuant to a Certificate of Limited Partnership filed with the Office of the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on August 12, 2025, under File No. 7924813. The rights, obligations, and governance terms of the Fund and its limited partners will be set forth in the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of the Fund, to be dated as of the date of the Fund\'s initial closing (the \"First Close\") (as may be further amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"LPA\"). The side letters to be prepared in connection with this engagement will supplement and, solely as between the GP and the applicable limited partner, modify certain terms of the LPA in the manner described herein.
22: 
23: This letter (the \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions of our engagement, including the scope of the Firm\'s representation, the engagement team, our fee arrangements, and other matters relevant to the attorney-client relationship between Calderwood & Harkness and the GP. We ask that you review this Engagement Letter carefully and confirm your agreement to its terms by countersigning a copy of this letter as provided in Section 13 below.
24: 
25: **[2. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**
26: 
27: The scope of Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement in connection with the Fund\'s side letter program and MFN election framework shall encompass the following:
28: 
29: **(a) Anchor Limited Partner Side Letter Agreements**
30: 
31: Calderwood & Harkness will draft, negotiate, and finalize individual side letter agreements (each, a \"Side Letter\") with the following three anchor limited partners of the Fund (collectively, the \"Anchor LPs\"):
32: 
33: > \(i\) **Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System** (\"Cascadia PERS\"), a governmental pension plan organized under the laws of the State of Washington. Cascadia PERS has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000), representing approximately 12.5% of the Fund\'s target fund size of Six Hundred Million Dollars (\$600,000,000) (the \"Target Fund Size\").
34: >
35: > \(ii\) **Northstar Endowment Partners LLC** (\"Northstar\"), a limited liability company organized under the laws of the State of Delaware, serving as the dedicated investment vehicle for the endowment of Veltrano University. Northstar has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000), representing approximately 8.33% of the Target Fund Size.
36: >
37: > \(iii\) **Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP** (\"Brindoval\"), a limited partnership organized under the laws of the State of Delaware. Brindoval has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Forty Million Dollars (\$40,000,000), representing approximately 6.67% of the Target Fund Size.
38: 
39: The aggregate capital commitments of the Anchor LPs total One Hundred Sixty-Five Million Dollars (\$165,000,000), representing approximately 27.5% of the Target Fund Size. Given the significance of these commitments to the Fund\'s initial closing and overall capital formation, the Firm understands that the timely completion of Side Letter negotiations with each of the Anchor LPs is a priority for the GP.
40: 
41: **(b) Side Letter Terms and Provisions**
42: 
43: Each Side Letter will be structured to supplement and, solely as between the GP and the applicable Anchor LP, modify certain terms and conditions of the LPA. The specific provisions to be addressed in each Side Letter will vary based on the nature, regulatory status, and specific requirements of the applicable Anchor LP, but are expected to include, as applicable, the following categories of terms:
44: 
45: > \(i\) **Management fee concessions**, including reduced management fee rates, management fee offsets, and fee calculation methodologies applicable during the investment period and the post-investment period;
46: >
47: > \(ii\) **Co-investment rights**, including rights to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund, allocation priority, notification procedures, and minimum co-investment allocation amounts;
48: >
49: > \(iii\) **Excuse and opt-out rights**, including the right of certain limited partners to be excused from, or to opt out of, specific Fund investments on the basis of legal, regulatory, tax, or policy considerations applicable to such limited partner;
50: >
51: > \(iv\) **Reporting enhancements**, including supplemental reporting obligations of the GP, enhanced transparency regarding portfolio company performance, ESG-related reporting, and diversity and inclusion metrics;
52: >
53: > \(v\) **FOIA and public records protections**, particularly relevant to Cascadia PERS, including provisions addressing the treatment of Fund information in the event of a public records request, prior notice and consultation obligations of the limited partner, and the GP\'s right to seek protective relief;
54: >
55: > \(vi\) **Advisory committee seats**, including the right of certain Anchor LPs to designate a representative to serve on the Fund\'s advisory committee, as well as related governance provisions;
56: >
57: > \(vii\) **Key-person event notifications**, including enhanced notification rights in the event of a key-person event under the LPA, consultation rights, and accelerated information delivery timelines;
58: >
59: > \(viii\) **Transfer rights**, including any enhanced or modified transfer, assignment, or secondary sale rights negotiated with an Anchor LP, subject to the transfer restrictions and consent provisions of the LPA;
60: >
61: > \(ix\) **Fee netting provisions**, addressing the application and allocation of transaction fees, monitoring fees, break-up fees, and other fees received by the GP or its affiliates in connection with Fund investments;
62: >
63: > \(x\) **Information rights**, including the right to receive additional information from the GP regarding the Fund\'s investments, operations, or financial condition, beyond the standard reporting obligations set forth in the LPA; and
64: >
65: > \(xi\) **Other customary terms**, including provisions relating to indemnification, representations and warranties, sovereign immunity (if applicable), governing law modifications, and such other terms as may be customary for side letters in institutional venture capital fund formations.
66: 
67: The Firm will work closely with the GP to tailor each Side Letter to the specific requirements and negotiation objectives of each Anchor LP, while maintaining consistency across the side letter package and managing the GP\'s exposure under the MFN framework.
68: 
69: **(c) Most Favored Nation Election Framework**
70: 
71: Calderwood & Harkness will structure and document a comprehensive most favored nation election framework (the \"MFN Framework\") applicable to qualifying limited partners of the Fund. The MFN Framework will include the following components:
72: 
73: > \(i\) **MFN Eligibility Threshold.** The Firm will advise on and document the MFN eligibility threshold, which the GP has preliminarily determined shall be set at capital commitments of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) or greater. Limited partners whose capital commitments equal or exceed this threshold (each, an \"Eligible LP\") will be entitled to elect certain rights and benefits granted in Side Letters to other limited partners of the Fund, subject to the exclusions described below.
74: >
75: > \(ii\) **MFN Election Procedures Letter and Election Form.** The Firm will draft a template MFN election procedures letter (the \"MFN Procedures Letter\") to be delivered by the GP to each Eligible LP, together with a standardized MFN election form (the \"MFN Election Form\") to be completed and returned by any Eligible LP wishing to make an MFN election. The MFN Procedures Letter will set forth the procedures, timing, and conditions applicable to MFN elections, including the process for the GP\'s review and confirmation of elected provisions.
76: >
77: > \(iii\) **Excluded Provisions.** The Firm will define and categorize certain provisions that will not be available for election under the MFN Framework (collectively, \"Excluded Provisions\"). Excluded Provisions are expected to include, without limitation: (A) provisions granted to a limited partner in order to satisfy specific legal, regulatory, or tax requirements applicable to such limited partner by reason of its status, jurisdiction, or governing law; (B) advisory committee seats and related governance rights; (C) portfolio company board observer rights; and (D) any other terms that the GP reasonably determines are specific to the legal, regulatory, or organizational status of a particular limited partner and are not appropriate for general election by other limited partners.
78: >
79: > \(iv\) **Redacted MFN Side Letter Compilation.** The Firm will prepare a redacted compilation of the Side Letters entered into by the Fund (the \"MFN Side Letter Compilation\"), from which the identities of the limited partners party thereto and all Excluded Provisions shall be redacted. The MFN Side Letter Compilation will be delivered by the GP to each Eligible LP within fifteen (15) business days following the final closing of the Fund (the \"Final Close\"), which is currently targeted to occur on or before July 15, 2026.
80: >
81: > \(v\) **MFN Election Period.** Following delivery of the MFN Side Letter Compilation, each Eligible LP shall have a period of thirty (30) calendar days (the \"MFN Election Period\") in which to review the MFN Side Letter Compilation and submit a completed MFN Election Form to the GP indicating which provisions, if any, such Eligible LP elects to receive. The Firm will advise the GP on the review, confirmation, and administration of MFN elections following the close of the MFN Election Period.
82: 
83: **(d) Coordination with Counterparty Counsel**
84: 
85: Calderwood & Harkness will serve as lead counsel to the GP in all negotiations with the Anchor LPs and will coordinate directly with the legal counsel representing each of the Anchor LPs during the negotiation period. The Firm understands that the following law firms will serve as counterparty counsel:
86: 
87: > \(i\) **Whitfield & Gage LLP** (Portland, Oregon), with Sandra Okafor as lead partner, serving as counsel to Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System;
88: >
89: > \(ii\) **Hollander McKee & Stone LLP** (Boston, Massachusetts), with David Tannenbaum as lead partner, serving as counsel to Northstar Endowment Partners LLC; and
90: >
91: > \(iii\) **Prescott & Langley LLP** (Chicago, Illinois), with Angela Ferris as lead partner, serving as counsel to Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP.
92: 
93: The Firm will coordinate the distribution of initial Side Letter drafts to each counterparty counsel, manage the negotiation process, track open issues, and seek to resolve negotiation points in a manner consistent with the GP\'s objectives and the Fund\'s overall commercial terms. The Firm will also facilitate, as appropriate, the scheduling and conduct of negotiation calls between the parties and their respective counsel.
94: 
95: **(e) Internal Analyses and Negotiation Support**
96: 
97: In support of the Side Letter negotiations and the MFN Framework, Calderwood & Harkness will prepare the following internal analyses and work product for the GP\'s use:
98: 
99: > \(i\) **Redline Comparison Chart.** A comprehensive redline comparison chart setting forth, on a term-by-term and LP-by-LP basis, the specific provisions granted in each Side Letter, highlighting differences among the Anchor LP Side Letters and identifying areas of potential MFN exposure.
100: >
101: > \(ii\) **MFN Exposure Analysis.** An analysis of the GP\'s exposure under the MFN Framework resulting from the provisions included in the Anchor LP Side Letters, including an assessment of the likelihood and potential impact of Eligible LP elections with respect to specific provisions, and recommendations for mitigating MFN risk through the designation of Excluded Provisions or the structuring of Side Letter terms.
102: >
103: > \(iii\) **Negotiation Issues Tracker.** A running issues tracker to be maintained throughout the negotiation period, cataloging open negotiation points, counterparty positions, the GP\'s responses, and the resolution status of each issue.
104: 
105: These materials will be prepared for the GP\'s internal use and will be subject to the attorney-client privilege and work product protections, as applicable.
106: 
107: **(f) Closing Checklist --- First Close Deliverables**
108: 
109: Calderwood & Harkness will prepare a closing checklist identifying all deliverables and conditions related to Side Letter execution that must be completed in connection with the First Close, including the execution and delivery of each Anchor LP Side Letter, the GP\'s execution of any related certificates, confirmations, or ancillary documents, and the distribution of any required notices or disclosures to the Anchor LPs or other limited partners of the Fund.
110: 
111: **[3. Matters Outside the Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**
112: 
113: The GP and the Firm acknowledge and agree that the following matters are expressly outside the scope of this engagement and are not included in the services to be provided by Calderwood & Harkness hereunder:
114: 
115: > \(a\) The drafting, negotiation, or review of the LPA itself, or any amendments or restatements thereto;
116: >
117: > \(b\) The preparation, drafting, or review of the Fund\'s private placement memorandum, confidential offering memorandum, subscription agreements, investor questionnaires, or other offering or subscription documents;
118: >
119: > \(c\) Any filings with, or submissions to, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the \"SEC\") or any state securities regulator, including Form D filings, Form ADV amendments, or blue sky filings;
120: >
121: > \(d\) Tax structuring, tax planning, or the rendering of any tax opinion or tax advice in connection with the Fund, the GP, or any limited partner, including any analysis under Subchapter K of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, or any state or local tax regime;
122: >
123: > \(e\) Analysis of compliance with the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), or the plan asset regulations thereunder, except to the extent of any ERISA-related representations, warranties, or acknowledgments that may be included in the Side Letters as a matter of standard drafting practice;
124: >
125: > \(f\) Any representation of, or advice to, the GP or the Fund in connection with the Fund\'s placement agent arrangements with Greystone Capital Advisors LLC, including the negotiation, review, or interpretation of any placement agent agreement; and
126: >
127: > \(g\) Any litigation, arbitration, mediation, or other dispute resolution proceeding, whether arising out of or related to the Side Letters, the LPA, the Fund, or otherwise.
128: 
129: In the event that the GP wishes to expand the scope of Calderwood & Harkness\'s representation to include any of the foregoing matters or any other matter not described in Section 2 above, such expansion of scope shall be confirmed in a separate engagement letter or in a written amendment to this Engagement Letter, setting forth the additional scope, engagement team, fee arrangements, and other applicable terms.
130: 
131: **[4. Engagement Team]{.underline}**
132: 
133: The following attorneys will comprise the Calderwood & Harkness engagement team for this matter:
134: 
135:   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
136:   **Team Member**     **Role**              **Practice Group**         **Primary Responsibilities**
137:   ------------------- --------------------- -------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
138:   Nicholas Stern      Responsible Partner   Funds & Asset Management   Primary point of contact for strategic matters and client relationship management; overall supervision of the engagement; participation in key negotiation sessions with counterparty counsel
139: 
140:   Graham Sutherland   Billing Partner       Funds & Asset Management   Billing administration and fee monitoring; periodic review of engagement progress and work product
141: 
142:   Owen Fischer        Lead Associate        Funds & Asset Management   Day-to-day management of the engagement; principal drafter of all Side Letters, MFN Framework documents, and internal analyses; primary liaison with counterparty counsel; coordination of negotiation schedules and issue resolution
143: 
144:   Stephen Adler       Working Associate     Funds & Asset Management   Supporting drafting and research; preparation of the MFN exposure analysis, redline comparison charts, and negotiation issues tracker; assistance with closing checklist preparation
145:   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
146: 
147: The GP\'s primary day-to-day contact for the engagement will be Owen Fischer. For strategic and client relationship matters, the GP may contact Nicholas Stern directly. The Firm may, from time to time, assign additional attorneys or professional staff to the engagement as circumstances warrant, and will inform the GP of any material changes to the composition of the engagement team.
148: 
149: **[5. Fees and Billing]{.underline}**
150: 
151: **(a) Billing Rates**
152: 
153: Services rendered in connection with this engagement will be billed on an hourly basis at the Firm\'s standard 2025 billing rates, which are as follows:
154: 
155:   -----------------------------------------------------------------------
156:   **Timekeeper**          **Rate Category**       **Hourly Rate**
157:   ----------------------- ----------------------- -----------------------
158:   Nicholas Stern          Partner                 \$1,450
159: 
160:   Graham Sutherland       Partner                 \$1,450
161: 
162:   Senior Associates       Senior Associate        \$950
163: 
164:   Owen Fischer            Associate               \$750
165: 
166:   Stephen Adler           Associate               \$750
167:   -----------------------------------------------------------------------
168: 
169: The foregoing billing rates are the Firm\'s standard rates in effect as of January 1, 2025. Billing rates are subject to annual adjustment, which typically takes effect on January 1 of each calendar year. The Firm will notify the GP in advance of any changes to the billing rates applicable to this engagement. In the event that senior associates are assigned to the engagement in a supporting capacity, the applicable senior associate rate set forth above will apply.
170: 
171: **(b) Fee Estimate**
172: 
173: Based on the scope of services described in Section 2 above, and on the Firm\'s experience with comparable side letter programs for venture capital and private equity fund formations, Calderwood & Harkness estimates that total professional fees for the engagement will be in the range of **\$185,000 to \$225,000**. This estimate is based on an anticipated total of approximately **170 to 210 hours** of attorney time across the engagement team, and assumes a negotiation process involving a customary number of drafting rounds and negotiation sessions with each of the three Anchor LPs.
174: 
175: The foregoing estimate is provided solely for the GP\'s budgeting and planning purposes and **does not constitute a cap on fees or a fixed fee arrangement**. Actual fees may be higher or lower than the estimate depending on a number of factors, including the complexity and duration of negotiations with each Anchor LP, the number and scope of negotiation rounds, the extent of LP-specific requirements or unusual provisions, and the responsiveness of counterparty counsel. The Firm will provide the GP with monthly updates on accrued fees relative to the estimate and will promptly notify the GP if the Firm believes that fees are likely to materially exceed the estimated range.
176: 
177: **(c) Disbursements and Expenses**
178: 
179: In addition to professional fees, the GP will be responsible for the reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket disbursements incurred by the Firm in connection with this engagement. **CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** **Attorneys at Law** 555 California Street, 40th Floor San Francisco, CA 94104 Telephone: (415) 392-7800 Facsimile: (415) 392-7801 www.calderwoodharkness.com
September 29, 2025
Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC 2400 Sand Hill Road, Suite 320 Menlo Park, CA 94025
> Attention: Rajesh Mehta, Co-Founder & Managing Partner
> Claire Dubois, Co-Founder & Managing Partner
**Re: Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP --- Side Letter Agreements and Most Favored Nation Election Framework for Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP**
Dear Mr. Mehta and Ms. Dubois:
**[1. Purpose and Confirmation of Engagement]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the \"GP\"), in its capacity as the general partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the \"Fund\"), in connection with the negotiation, preparation, and documentation of side letter agreements with certain anchor limited partners of the Fund and the structuring and documentation of the most favored nation (\"MFN\") election framework applicable to qualifying limited partners of the Fund, each as more fully described in Section 2 below.

The Fund was organized pursuant to a Certificate of Limited Partnership filed with the Office of the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on August 12, 2025, under File No. 7924813. The rights, obligations, and governance terms of the Fund and its limited partners will be set forth in the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of the Fund, to be dated as of the date of the Fund\'s initial closing (the \"First Close\") (as may be further amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"LPA\"). The side letters to be prepared in connection with this engagement will supplement and, solely as between the GP and the applicable limited partner, modify certain terms of the LPA in the manner described herein.

This letter (the \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions of our engagement, including the scope of the Firm\'s representation, the engagement team, our fee arrangements, and other matters relevant to the attorney-client relationship between Calderwood & Harkness and the GP. We ask that you review this Engagement Letter carefully and confirm your agreement to its terms by countersigning a copy of this letter as provided in Section 13 below.
**[2. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**
The scope of Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement in connection with the Fund\'s side letter program and MFN election framework shall encompass the following:
**(a) Anchor Limited Partner Side Letter Agreements**

Calderwood & Harkness will draft, negotiate, and finalize individual side letter agreements (each, a \"Side Letter\") with the following three anchor limited partners of the Fund (collectively, the \"Anchor LPs\"):

> \(i\) **Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System** (\"Cascadia PERS\"), a governmental pension plan organized under the laws of the State of Washington. Cascadia PERS has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000), representing approximately 12.5% of the Fund\'s target fund size of Six Hundred Million Dollars (\$600,000,000) (the \"Target Fund Size\").

> \(ii\) **Northstar Endowment Partners LLC** (\"Northstar\"), a limited liability company organized under the laws of the State of Delaware, serving as the dedicated investment vehicle for the endowment of Veltrano University. Northstar has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000), representing approximately 8.33% of the Target Fund Size.

> \(iii\) **Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP** (\"Brindoval\"), a limited partnership organized under the laws of the State of Delaware. Brindoval has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Forty Million Dollars (\$40,000,000), representing approximately 6.67% of the Target Fund Size.

The aggregate capital commitments of the Anchor LPs total One Hundred Sixty-Five Million Dollars (\$165,000,000), representing approximately 27.5% of the Target Fund Size. Given the significance of these commitments to the Fund\'s initial closing and overall capital formation, the Firm understands that the timely completion of Side Letter negotiations with each of the Anchor LPs is a priority for the GP.
**(b) Side Letter Terms and Provisions**

Each Side Letter will be structured to supplement and, solely as between the GP and the applicable Anchor LP, modify certain terms and conditions of the LPA. The specific provisions to be addressed in each Side Letter will vary based on the nature, regulatory status, and specific requirements of the applicable Anchor LP, but are expected to include, as applicable, the following categories of terms:

> \(i\) **Management fee concessions**, including reduced management fee rates, management fee offsets, and fee calculation methodologies applicable during the investment period and the post-investment period;

> \(ii\) **Co-investment rights**, including rights to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund, allocation priority, notification procedures, and minimum co-investment allocation amounts;

> \(iii\) **Excuse and opt-out rights**, including the right of certain limited partners to be excused from, or to opt out of, specific Fund investments on the basis of legal, regulatory, tax, or policy considerations applicable to such limited partner;

> \(iv\) **Reporting enhancements**, including supplemental reporting obligations of the GP, enhanced transparency regarding portfolio company performance, ESG-related reporting, and diversity and inclusion metrics;

> \(v\) **FOIA and public records protections**, particularly relevant to Cascadia PERS, including provisions addressing the treatment of Fund information in the event of a public records request, prior notice and consultation obligations of the limited partner, and the GP\'s right to seek protective relief;
> \(vi\) **Advisory committee seats**, including the right of certain Anchor LPs to designate a representative to serve on the Fund\'s advisory committee, as well as related governance provisions;

> \(vii\) **Key-person event notifications**, including enhanced notification rights in the event of a key-person event under the LPA, consultation rights, and accelerated information delivery timelines;

> \(viii\) **Transfer rights**, including any enhanced or modified transfer, assignment, or secondary sale rights negotiated with an Anchor LP, subject to the transfer restrictions and consent provisions of the LPA;

> \(ix\) **Fee netting provisions**, addressing the application and allocation of transaction fees, monitoring fees, break-up fees, and other fees received by the GP or its affiliates in connection with Fund investments;

> \(x\) **Information rights**, including the right to receive additional information from the GP regarding the Fund\'s investments, operations, or financial condition, beyond the standard reporting obligations set forth in the LPA; and

> \(xi\) **Other customary terms**, including provisions relating to indemnification, representations and warranties, sovereign immunity (if applicable), governing law modifications, and such other terms as may be customary for side letters in institutional venture capital fund formations.

The Firm will work closely with the GP to tailor each Side Letter to the specific requirements and negotiation objectives of each Anchor LP, while maintaining consistency across the side letter package and managing the GP\'s exposure under the MFN framework.
**(c) Most Favored Nation Election Framework**

Calderwood & Harkness will structure and document a comprehensive most favored nation election framework (the \"MFN Framework\") applicable to qualifying limited partners of the Fund. The MFN Framework will include the following components:

> \(i\) **MFN Eligibility Threshold.** The Firm will advise on and document the MFN eligibility threshold, which the GP has preliminarily determined shall be set at capital commitments of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) or greater. Limited partners whose capital commitments equal or exceed this threshold (each, an \"Eligible LP\") will be entitled to elect certain rights and benefits granted in Side Letters to other limited partners of the Fund, subject to the exclusions described below.

> \(ii\) **MFN Election Procedures Letter and Election Form.** The Firm will draft a template MFN election procedures letter (the \"MFN Procedures Letter\") to be delivered by the GP to each Eligible LP, together with a standardized MFN election form (the \"MFN Election Form\") to be completed and returned by any Eligible LP wishing to make an MFN election. The MFN Procedures Letter will set forth the procedures, timing, and conditions applicable to MFN elections, including the process for the GP\'s review and confirmation of elected provisions.

> \(iii\) **Excluded Provisions.** The Firm will define and categorize certain provisions that will not be available for election under the MFN Framework (collectively, \"Excluded Provisions\"). Excluded Provisions are expected to include, without limitation: (A) provisions granted to a limited partner in order to satisfy specific legal, regulatory, or tax requirements applicable to such limited partner by reason of its status, jurisdiction, or governing law; (B) advisory committee seats and related governance rights; (C) portfolio company board observer rights; and (D) any other terms that the GP reasonably determines are specific to the legal, regulatory, or organizational status of a particular limited partner and are not appropriate for general election by other limited partners.

> \(iv\) **Redacted MFN Side Letter Compilation.** The Firm will prepare a redacted compilation of the Side Letters entered into by the Fund (the \"MFN Side Letter Compilation\"), from which the identities of the limited partners party thereto and all Excluded Provisions shall be redacted. The MFN Side Letter Compilation will be delivered by the GP to each Eligible LP within fifteen (15) business days following the final closing of the Fund (the \"Final Close\"), which is currently targeted to occur on or before July 15, 2026.

> \(v\) **MFN Election Period.** Following delivery of the MFN Side Letter Compilation, each Eligible LP shall have a period of thirty (30) calendar days (the \"MFN Election Period\") in which to review the MFN Side Letter Compilation and submit a completed MFN Election Form to the GP indicating which provisions, if any, such Eligible LP elects to receive. The Firm will advise the GP on the review, confirmation, and administration of MFN elections following the close of the MFN Election Period.
**(d) Coordination with Counterparty Counsel**

Calderwood & Harkness will serve as lead counsel to the GP in all negotiations with the Anchor LPs and will coordinate directly with the legal counsel representing each of the Anchor LPs during the negotiation period. The Firm understands that the following law firms will serve as counterparty counsel:
> \(i\) **Whitfield & Gage LLP** (Portland, Oregon), with Sandra Okafor as lead partner, serving as counsel to Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System;
> \(ii\) **Hollander McKee & Stone LLP** (Boston, Massachusetts), with David Tannenbaum as lead partner, serving as counsel to Northstar Endowment Partners LLC; and
> \(iii\) **Prescott & Langley LLP** (Chicago, Illinois), with Angela Ferris as lead partner, serving as counsel to Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP.

The Firm will coordinate the distribution of initial Side Letter drafts to each counterparty counsel, manage the negotiation process, track open issues, and seek to resolve negotiation points in a manner consistent with the GP\'s objectives and the Fund\'s overall commercial terms. The Firm will also facilitate, as appropriate, the scheduling and conduct of negotiation calls between the parties and their respective counsel.
**(e) Internal Analyses and Negotiation Support**
In support of the Side Letter negotiations and the MFN Framework, Calderwood & Harkness will prepare the following internal analyses and work product for the GP\'s use:

> \(i\) **Redline Comparison Chart.** A comprehensive redline comparison chart setting forth, on a term-by-term and LP-by-LP basis, the specific provisions granted in each Side Letter, highlighting differences among the Anchor LP Side Letters and identifying areas of potential MFN exposure.

> \(ii\) **MFN Exposure Analysis.** An analysis of the GP\'s exposure under the MFN Framework resulting from the provisions included in the Anchor LP Side Letters, including an assessment of the likelihood and potential impact of Eligible LP elections with respect to specific provisions, and recommendations for mitigating MFN risk through the designation of Excluded Provisions or the structuring of Side Letter terms.

> \(iii\) **Negotiation Issues Tracker.** A running issues tracker to be maintained throughout the negotiation period, cataloging open negotiation points, counterparty positions, the GP\'s responses, and the resolution status of each issue.
These materials will be prepared for the GP\'s internal use and will be subject to the attorney-client privilege and work product protections, as applicable.
**(f) Closing Checklist --- First Close Deliverables**

Calderwood & Harkness will prepare a closing checklist identifying all deliverables and conditions related to Side Letter execution that must be completed in connection with the First Close, including the execution and delivery of each Anchor LP Side Letter, the GP\'s execution of any related certificates, confirmations, or ancillary documents, and the distribution of any required notices or disclosures to the Anchor LPs or other limited partners of the Fund.
**[3. Matters Outside the Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**

The GP and the Firm acknowledge and agree that the following matters are expressly outside the scope of this engagement and are not included in the services to be provided by Calderwood & Harkness hereunder:
> \(a\) The drafting, negotiation, or review of the LPA itself, or any amendments or restatements thereto;

> \(b\) The preparation, drafting, or review of the Fund\'s private placement memorandum, confidential offering memorandum, subscription agreements, investor questionnaires, or other offering or subscription documents;

> \(c\) Any filings with, or submissions to, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the \"SEC\") or any state securities regulator, including Form D filings, Form ADV amendments, or blue sky filings;

> \(d\) Tax structuring, tax planning, or the rendering of any tax opinion or tax advice in connection with the Fund, the GP, or any limited partner, including any analysis under Subchapter K of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, or any state or local tax regime;

> \(e\) Analysis of compliance with the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), or the plan asset regulations thereunder, except to the extent of any ERISA-related representations, warranties, or acknowledgments that may be included in the Side Letters as a matter of standard drafting practice;

> \(f\) Any representation of, or advice to, the GP or the Fund in connection with the Fund\'s placement agent arrangements with Greystone Capital Advisors LLC, including the negotiation, review, or interpretation of any placement agent agreement; and
> \(g\) Any litigation, arbitration, mediation, or other dispute resolution proceeding, whether arising out of or related to the Side Letters, the LPA, the Fund, or otherwise.

In the event that the GP wishes to expand the scope of Calderwood & Harkness\'s representation to include any of the foregoing matters or any other matter not described in Section 2 above, such expansion of scope shall be confirmed in a separate engagement letter or in a written amendment to this Engagement Letter, setting forth the additional scope, engagement team, fee arrangements, and other applicable terms.
**[4. Engagement Team]{.underline}**
The following attorneys will comprise the Calderwood & Harkness engagement team for this matter:
**Team Member**     **Role**              **Practice Group**         **Primary Responsibilities**

Nicholas Stern      Responsible Partner   Funds & Asset Management   Primary point of contact for strategic matters and client relationship management; overall supervision of the engagement; participation in key negotiation sessions with counterparty counsel
Graham Sutherland   Billing Partner       Funds & Asset Management   Billing administration and fee monitoring; periodic review of engagement progress and work product

Owen Fischer        Lead Associate        Funds & Asset Management   Day-to-day management of the engagement; principal drafter of all Side Letters, MFN Framework documents, and internal analyses; primary liaison with counterparty counsel; coordination of negotiation schedules and issue resolution

Stephen Adler       Working Associate     Funds & Asset Management   Supporting drafting and research; preparation of the MFN exposure analysis, redline comparison charts, and negotiation issues tracker; assistance with closing checklist preparation

The GP\'s primary day-to-day contact for the engagement will be Owen Fischer. For strategic and client relationship matters, the GP may contact Nicholas Stern directly. The Firm may, from time to time, assign additional attorneys or professional staff to the engagement as circumstances warrant, and will inform the GP of any material changes to the composition of the engagement team.
**[5. Fees and Billing]{.underline}**
**(a) Billing Rates**
Services rendered in connection with this engagement will be billed on an hourly basis at the Firm\'s standard 2025 billing rates, which are as follows:
**Timekeeper**          **Rate Category**       **Hourly Rate**
Nicholas Stern          Partner                 \$1,450
Graham Sutherland       Partner                 \$1,450
Senior Associates       Senior Associate        \$950
Owen Fischer            Associate               \$750
Stephen Adler           Associate               \$750

The foregoing billing rates are the Firm\'s standard rates in effect as of January 1, 2025. Billing rates are subject to annual adjustment, which typically takes effect on January 1 of each calendar year. The Firm will notify the GP in advance of any changes to the billing rates applicable to this engagement. In the event that senior associates are assigned to the engagement in a supporting capacity, the applicable senior associate rate set forth above will apply.
**(b) Fee Estimate**

Based on the scope of services described in Section 2 above, and on the Firm\'s experience with comparable side letter programs for venture capital and private equity fund formations, Calderwood & Harkness estimates that total professional fees for the engagement will be in the range of **\$185,000 to \$225,000**. This estimate is based on an anticipated total of approximately **170 to 210 hours** of attorney time across the engagement team, and assumes a negotiation process involving a customary number of drafting rounds and negotiation sessions with each of the three Anchor LPs.

The foregoing estimate is provided solely for the GP\'s budgeting and planning purposes and **does not constitute a cap on fees or a fixed fee arrangement**. Actual fees may be higher or lower than the estimate depending on a number of factors, including the complexity and duration of negotiations with each Anchor LP, the number and scope of negotiation rounds, the extent of LP-specific requirements or unusual provisions, and the responsiveness of counterparty counsel. The Firm will provide the GP with monthly updates on accrued fees relative to the estimate and will promptly notify the GP if the Firm believes that fees are likely to materially exceed the estimated range.
**(c) Disbursements and Expenses**

In addition to professional fees, the GP will be responsible for the reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket disbursements incurred by the Firm in connection with this engagement. Disbursements may include, without limitation, travel expenses (airfare, ground transportation, lodging, and meals incurred in connection with in-person negotiation sessions or meetings), document production and reproduction costs, filing fees, courier and overnight delivery charges, long-distance telephone charges, and similar expenses. All disbursements will be billed at the Firm\'s actual cost, without markup.
**(d) Billing and Payment**

Calderwood & Harkness will render invoices for professional fees and disbursements on a monthly basis, in arrears. Each invoice will include a summary of the services rendered and the disbursements incurred during the applicable billing period, together with a detail of hours billed by each timekeeper.

Amounts not paid within the thirty-day period will bear interest at the rate of **1.0% per month** (or, if less, the maximum rate permitted by applicable law), calculated from the due date until the date of payment. The Firm reserves the right to suspend or terminate its services in the event of a material delinquency in payment, subject to the Firm\'s ethical obligations and the provisions of Section 12 below.
**[6. Key Timeline and Milestones]{.underline}**

**Milestone**                                                     **Target Date**
Engagement opened                                                 September 29, 2025
Distribution of initial Side Letter drafts to Anchor LP counsel   October 20, 2025

Final Close (deadline)                                            July 15, 2026
Delivery of MFN Side Letter Compilation to Eligible LPs           Within 15 business days after Final Close
MFN Election Period                                               30 calendar days following delivery of the MFN Side Letter Compilation

Calderwood & Harkness will use commercially reasonable efforts to meet the foregoing timeline and milestones; however, the Firm notes that the actual schedule will depend on a number of factors outside the Firm\'s control, including the responsiveness of counterparty counsel and the Anchor LPs, the complexity and scope of LP-specific negotiation requests, and any changes to the GP\'s fundraising timeline or closing schedule. The Firm will keep the GP regularly informed of progress against the timeline and will promptly communicate any anticipated delays or scheduling issues.
**[7. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will maintain the confidentiality of all information provided by the GP and the Fund in connection with this engagement, in accordance with the Firm\'s professional obligations under the California Rules of Professional Conduct and applicable law. The Firm will not disclose confidential information to any third party except as authorized by the GP, as required by law or court order, or as necessary to carry out the Firm\'s responsibilities under this engagement (including, for the avoidance of doubt, communications with counterparty counsel in the course of Side Letter negotiations, as directed by the GP).

Based on a conflicts check conducted by the Firm as of the date of this Engagement Letter, Calderwood & Harkness is not aware of any current conflict of interest that would preclude the Firm from undertaking this engagement in accordance with applicable rules of professional conduct.

The Firm confirms that Calderwood & Harkness does not currently represent, and has not within the past twenty-four (24) months represented, any of the three Anchor LPs --- Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System, Northstar Endowment Partners LLC, or Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP --- or any of their respective legal counsel --- Whitfield & Gage LLP (Portland, Oregon), Hollander McKee & Stone LLP (Boston, Massachusetts), or Prescott & Langley LLP (Chicago, Illinois) --- in any matter, whether related or unrelated to the subject matter of this engagement.

> \(b\) the Fund itself as a separate legal entity, except to the extent that the interests of the Fund are aligned with, and directed by, the GP in the GP\'s capacity as the general partner and manager of the Fund; or
> \(c\) any individual managing partner, officer, member, or employee of the GP in his or her personal capacity, including Rajesh Mehta and Claire Dubois.

Co-investment allocations shall be offered to CPERS on a pro rata basis relative to its commitment to the Fund, subject to the General Partner\'s discretion regarding allocation among all co-investment-eligible limited partners.

> \(f\) **Most Favored Nation Election Right.** Right to elect to receive the benefit of any more favorable terms granted to any other limited partner in the Fund (subject to certain Excluded Provisions as described in Section IX of this Checklist), in accordance with the MFN election procedures established in the side letters and the procedures letter to be delivered following the Final Close.
> \(g\) **Tax-Exempt Status Representations.** Representations by CPERS regarding its status as a tax-exempt entity under Section 115 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.
**Commitment Amount:** \$75,000,000
**Responsible Party:** C&H (prepare final execution version); GP (execute on behalf of the Fund); LP Counsel --- Whitfield & Gage LLP (Sandra Okafor) (obtain LP execution)
**Number of Originals Required:** Two (2) --- one original for the General Partner\'s files and one original for CPERS\'s files.
**Status:** \[   \]
**Date Last Updated:** **\_\_\_**
**Item 2: Side Letter --- Northstar Endowment Partners LLC**

**Description:** Execution copy of the Side Letter (the \"Northstar Side Letter\") between Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC, in its capacity as general partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, and Northstar Endowment Partners LLC, dated as of the First Close (January 15, 2026). The Northstar Side Letter sets forth certain rights, obligations, and modifications to the LPA that are applicable solely as between the General Partner and Northstar.
**Key Provisions Covered:**

> \(a\) **Management Fee Reduction.** Reduction of the management fee payable by Northstar to 1.85% per annum on committed capital during the Investment Period (representing a 15 basis point discount from the standard 2.00% management fee set forth in Section 6.1 of the LPA). Following the expiration of the Investment Period, Northstar will pay the management fee at the standard rate of 2.00% per annum on invested capital, consistent with the LPA.

> \(b\) **Advisory Committee Seat.** Right to designate one (1) representative to serve on the Fund\'s Advisory Committee established under Section 9.1 of the LPA. Northstar\'s initial designee is expected to be Helen Bancroft, Director of Private Investments, or such other individual as Northstar may designate from time to time upon written notice to the General Partner.

> \(c\) **Key-Person Event Notification.** Right to receive prompt written notification (and in any event within five (5) business days) in the event that either Rajesh Mehta or Claire Dubois ceases to devote substantially all of his or her business time and attention to the affairs of the Fund (a \"Key Person Event\"), together with a description of the General Partner\'s plan to address the Key Person Event. This notification right is in addition to, and does not limit, the Key Person Event provisions set forth in Section 8.3 of the LPA.

> \(d\) **Co-Investment Rights.** Right to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund on terms substantially similar to those described in the CPERS Side Letter (Item 1, clause (e) above).

> \(e\) **Transfer Rights.** Right to transfer all or a portion of Northstar\'s limited partnership interest in the Fund to one or more affiliated endowment investment vehicles of Veltrano University, without the prior written consent of the General Partner that would otherwise be required under Section 10.2 of the LPA, provided that (i) such transfer complies with all applicable securities laws, (ii) the transferee executes such documents as the General Partner may reasonably require (including a joinder to the LPA and, if applicable, a counterpart to the Northstar Side Letter), and (iii) such transfer would not cause the Fund to be treated as a \"publicly traded partnership\" for U.S. federal income tax purposes.

> \(f\) **ERISA Representation Waiver.** Representation by Northstar that it is not, and the assets being contributed by it to the Fund do not constitute \"plan assets\" of, an \"employee benefit plan\" as defined in Section 3(3) of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), nor is Northstar subject to the provisions of ERISA. The standard ERISA representations in the subscription agreement shall be modified accordingly.

> \(g\) **Most Favored Nation Election Right.** Right to elect to receive the benefit of any more favorable terms granted to any other limited partner in the Fund (subject to certain Excluded Provisions as described in Section IX of this Checklist), in accordance with the MFN election procedures established in the side letters and the procedures letter to be delivered following the Final Close.
**Commitment Amount:** \$50,000,000
**Responsible Party:** C&H (prepare final execution version); GP (execute on behalf of the Fund); LP Counsel --- Hollander McKee & Stone LLP (David Tannenbaum) (obtain LP execution)
**Number of Originals Required:** Two (2) --- one original for the General Partner\'s files and one original for Northstar\'s files.
**Status:** \[   \]
**Date Last Updated:** **\_\_\_**
**Item 3: Side Letter --- Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP**

**Description:** Execution copy of the Side Letter (the \"Brindoval Side Letter\") between Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC, in its capacity as general partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, and Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP, dated as of the First Close (January 15, 2026). The Brindoval Side Letter sets forth certain rights, obligations, and modifications to the LPA that are applicable solely as between the General Partner and Brindoval.
**Key Provisions Covered:**

> \(a\) **Opt-Out Rights.** Right of Brindoval to elect not to participate in any Fund investment in a portfolio company that the General Partner determines, in good faith and after consultation with Brindoval, to be directly competitive with any software-as-a-service (\"SaaS\") business owned or controlled by the Raines family or any of its affiliated entities. The General Partner shall provide Brindoval with reasonable prior written notice of any proposed investment that it believes may trigger this opt-out right, together with a summary description of the proposed portfolio company\'s business sufficient for Brindoval to make an informed determination, and shall afford Brindoval a period of not less than ten (10) business days to exercise such right. For the avoidance of doubt, Brindoval\'s exercise of this opt-out right shall not reduce its unfunded commitment to the Fund.

> \(b\) **Co-Investment Rights.** Right to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund on terms consistent with those made available to other co-investment-eligible limited partners, subject to the General Partner\'s discretion regarding allocation.

> \(c\) **Management Fee / Carried Interest Netting.** Right to have management fees paid by Brindoval netted against distributions of carried interest otherwise payable to the General Partner with respect to Brindoval\'s interest in the Fund. This netting mechanism applies at the time of each distribution and effectively reduces the General Partner\'s carried interest allocation attributable to Brindoval\'s interest by the aggregate amount of management fees previously paid by Brindoval.

> \(d\) **Information Rights.** Entitlement to enhanced information rights aligned with the Institutional Limited Partners Association (\"ILPA\") best practices, including (i) annual audited financial statements delivered within 90 days following the end of each fiscal year, (ii) unaudited quarterly financial statements delivered within 45 days following the end of each fiscal quarter, (iii) capital account statements, and (iv) annual meeting or investor update access.

> \(e\) **Most Favored Nation Election Right.** Right to elect to receive the benefit of any more favorable terms granted to any other limited partner in the Fund (subject to certain Excluded Provisions as described in Section IX of this Checklist), in accordance with the MFN election procedures established in the side letters and the procedures letter to be delivered following the Final Close.

> \(f\) **Management Fee Rate.** Standard management fee of 2.00% per annum on committed capital during the Investment Period (no discount from the standard rate set forth in Section 6.1 of the LPA). Post-Investment Period management fee at the standard rate of 2.00% per annum on invested capital.
**Commitment Amount:** \$40,000,000
**Responsible Party:** C&H (prepare final execution version); GP (execute on behalf of the Fund); LP Counsel --- Prescott & Langley LLP (Angela Ferris) (obtain LP execution)
**Number of Originals Required:** Two (2) --- one original for the General Partner\'s files and one original for Brindoval\'s files.
**Status:** \[   \]
**Date Last Updated:** **\_\_\_**
**[III. SIGNATURE PAGES]{.underline}**
**Item 4: GP Signature Pages --- All Side Letters**

**Description:** Signature pages executed by Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC, in its capacity as general partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, for each of the three anchor LP side letters described in Section II of this Checklist. Each signature page should reflect the execution by the General Partner of the applicable side letter and should be dated as of the First Close (January 15, 2026).

**Authorized Signatories:** The following individuals are authorized to execute the side letters on behalf of the General Partner, and any one of them acting alone shall have full authority to bind the General Partner:
> • Rajesh Mehta, Co-Founder & Managing Partner
> • Claire Dubois, Co-Founder & Managing Partner
**Number Required:** Three (3) sets --- one executed GP signature page for each of the following side letters:
> \(i\) CPERS Side Letter (Item 1)
> \(ii\) Northstar Side Letter (Item 2)
> \(iii\) Brindoval Side Letter (Item 3)
**Responsible Party:** GP

**Notes:** C&H will provide the form of signature page for each side letter. The GP should review and confirm that the name, title, and capacity lines are correct before execution. Signature pages may be executed in counterpart and delivered by PDF or other electronic transmission, with originals to follow by overnight courier.
**Status:** \[   \]
**Date Last Updated:** **\_\_\_**
**Item 5: LP Signature Page --- Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System**

**Description:** Signature page executed by a duly authorized representative of Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System, evidencing CPERS\'s execution of and agreement to be bound by the terms and conditions of the CPERS Side Letter (Item 1).

**Expected Signatory:** Martin Albrecht, Chief Investment Officer, Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System, or such other duly authorized officer of CPERS as may be identified in the incumbency certificate delivered pursuant to Item 8 of this Checklist.
**Responsible Party:** LP Counsel --- Whitfield & Gage LLP (Sandra Okafor)

**Notes:** C&H will provide the form of LP signature page. Whitfield & Gage LLP should confirm the identity and title of the authorized signatory and ensure that all requisite internal approvals (including any board or investment committee approvals required under CPERS\'s governing documents and applicable Washington State law) have been obtained prior to execution. An executed copy of the signature page should be delivered to Owen Fischer at C&H by PDF, with originals to follow.
**Status:** \[   \]
**Date Last Updated:** **\_\_\_**
**Item 6: LP Signature Page --- Northstar Endowment Partners LLC**

**Description:** Signature page executed by a duly authorized representative of Northstar Endowment Partners LLC, evidencing Northstar\'s execution of and agreement to be bound by the terms and conditions of the Northstar Side Letter (Item 2).

**Expected Signatory:** Helen Bancroft, Director of Private Investments, Northstar Endowment Partners LLC, or such other duly authorized officer or manager of Northstar as may be identified in the incumbency certificate or manager\'s certificate delivered pursuant to Item 9 of this Checklist.
**Responsible Party:** LP Counsel --- Hollander McKee & Stone LLP (David Tannenbaum)

**Notes:** C&H will provide the form of LP signature page. Hollander McKee & Stone LLP should confirm the identity and title of the authorized signatory and ensure that all requisite internal approvals (including any approvals required under Northstar\'s operating agreement and any oversight or governance requirements of Veltrano University\'s Board of Trustees or investment committee) have been obtained prior to execution. An executed copy of the signature page should be delivered to Owen Fischer at C&H by PDF, with originals to follow.
**Status:** \[   \]
**Date Last Updated:** **\_\_\_**
**Item 7: LP Signature Page --- Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP**

**Description:** Signature page executed by a duly authorized representative of Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP, acting through its general partner or other authorized signatory, evidencing Brindoval\'s execution of and agreement to be bound by the terms and conditions of the Brindoval Side Letter (Item 3).

**Expected Signatory:** Jonathan Raines, Principal, Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP (or, if Brindoval executes through its general partner, such authorized representative of the general partner as may be identified in the incumbency certificate delivered pursuant to Item 10 of this Checklist).
**Responsible Party:** LP Counsel --- Prescott & Langley LLP (Angela Ferris)

**Notes:** C&H will provide the form of LP signature page. Prescott & Langley LLP should confirm the signatory capacity (i.e., whether execution is by Brindoval directly through an authorized representative or through its general partner) and provide the appropriate form of signature block. An executed copy of the signature page should be delivered to Owen Fischer at C&H by PDF, with originals to follow.
**Status:** \[   \]
