25: Dear Dr. Yeung and Ms. Dasgupta:
26: 
27: Calderwood & Harkness LLP is pleased to confirm the terms of our engagement to serve as fund counsel to Cobalt Ventures LP in connection with the matters described below. We very much look forward to partnering with you and the Cobalt team on this important initiative, and we appreciate the confidence you have placed in our firm. This engagement letter (this \"Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions under which Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness,\" the \"Firm,\" \"we,\" or \"us\") will provide legal services to Cobalt Ventures LP (\"Cobalt\" or the \"Client\").
28: 
29: We ask that you review this Letter carefully and, if the terms are acceptable, execute and return a copy to us as described in Section 12 below.
30: 
31: **[1. Purpose and Introduction]{.underline}**
32: 
33: Calderwood & Harkness LLP is pleased to confirm its engagement by Cobalt Ventures LP to serve as fund counsel in connection with the structuring, formation, and fund-raising for Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP (the \"Fund\" or \"CLSO Fund I\"), a proposed Delaware limited partnership. We understand that the Fund will be Cobalt\'s inaugural dedicated opportunistic life-sciences investment vehicle, and that Cobalt is targeting aggregate committed capital of Seven Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$750,000,000), with a hard cap of One Billion Dollars (\$1,000,000,000).
34: 
35: By way of background, Cobalt is a California-headquartered venture capital sponsor focused on the biotechnology and life-sciences sectors. Founded in 2018 by Dr. Marcus Yeung and Priya Dasgupta, Cobalt currently manages approximately \$420 million in assets under management across two prior vintage vehicles --- Cobalt Ventures Fund A, LP (vintage 2019) and Cobalt Ventures Fund B, LP (vintage 2022). The launch of CLSO Fund I represents a significant strategic milestone for the Cobalt platform, expanding the firm\'s investment mandate into opportunistic life-sciences investments across stage, geography, and modality.
36: 
37: This Letter sets forth the terms under which Calderwood & Harkness will provide legal services in connection with the structuring, formation, and fund-raising of the Fund and related entities, and it supersedes any prior oral or written understandings between the parties regarding the scope and terms of this engagement.
38: 
39: **[2. Client Identification]{.underline}**
40: 
41: The Client for purposes of this engagement is **Cobalt Ventures LP**, a Delaware limited partnership (Delaware LP File No. 7824931; California Secretary of State File No. 202118412387; EIN: 83-2947561), with its principal place of business at 3400 Sand Hill Road, Suite 220, Menlo Park, California 94025, and its registered agent for service of process in Delaware at Hollowell Technologies, 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801.
42: 
43: In addition to Cobalt Ventures LP, Calderwood & Harkness\'s representation under this engagement extends to the following entities, each of which is to be formed in connection with the Fund:
44: 
45: > \(a\) **Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership, to be formed, which will serve as the main investment vehicle for the Fund;
46: >
47: > \(b\) **Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC** --- a Delaware limited liability company, to be formed, which will serve as the general partner of the Fund;
48: >
49: > \(c\) **Cobalt Life Sciences Management I, LLC** --- a Delaware limited liability company, to be formed, which will serve as the management company and will be party to the management agreement with the Fund; and
50: >
51: > \(d\) **Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I (Blocker), Inc.** --- a Delaware C-Corporation, to be formed if and when determined to be necessary or advisable for purposes of establishing a taxable blocker structure for certain categories of investors, including tax-exempt and non-U.S. limited partners.
52: 
53: The foregoing entities are collectively referred to herein as the \"Fund Entities.\" As formation documents are prepared and filed for each Fund Entity, such entity shall be deemed a client of the Firm under the terms of this Letter without the need for a separate engagement letter, unless the Firm and the Client agree otherwise in writing.
54: 
55: **Important Clarification Regarding Scope of Representation.** Calderwood & Harkness does not represent, and will not represent in connection with this engagement, any individual limited partner or prospective limited partner of the Fund, any placement agent engaged by the Fund (including sagebrush Capital Partners LLC), or any other third-party service provider to the Fund. Each such party should retain and rely upon its own independent legal counsel with respect to its interests in or obligations to the Fund.
56: 
57: **[3. Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**
58: 
59: The scope of Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement encompasses the following workstreams, each of which is described in greater detail below. To the extent the Client requests legal services that fall outside the scope described in this Section 3, such services will be provided only upon mutual written agreement and may be subject to a separate engagement letter or an amendment to this Letter.
60: 
61: **3.1 Fund Structuring and Entity Formation**
62: 
63: Calderwood & Harkness will advise the Client on the optimal legal and organizational structure for the Fund and will be responsible for the formation of each Fund Entity. This workstream will include the following:
64: 
65: > \(a\) **Structural Analysis.** Analysis of fund structure alternatives, including a single-tier Delaware limited partnership, parallel fund structures (including for non-U.S. investors or investors requiring a separately managed account), blocker corporation arrangements, alternative investment vehicle (\"AIV\") structures, and master-feeder options. Our analysis will take into account the anticipated investor base, the Client\'s investment strategy, tax efficiency, regulatory considerations, and administrative complexity.
66: >
67: > \(b\) **Fund Structuring Memorandum.** Preparation and delivery of a comprehensive Fund Structuring Memorandum setting forth Calderwood & Harkness\'s analysis and recommendations regarding the recommended fund architecture, including a diagram of the proposed entity structure, a summary of the principal advantages and disadvantages of each structural alternative considered, and our recommended approach. The target delivery date for the Fund Structuring Memorandum is **April 30, 2026**.
68: >
69: > \(c\) **Delaware Formation Filings.** Preparation and filing of the Certificate of Limited Partnership for Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP, and the Certificates of Formation for Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC and Cobalt Life Sciences Management I, LLC, with the Delaware Division of Corporations. If the blocker corporation is determined to be necessary, Calderwood & Harkness will also prepare and file the Certificate of Incorporation for Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I (Blocker), Inc.
70: >
71: > \(d\) **EIN Applications.** Preparation and submission of IRS Form SS-4 (Application for Employer Identification Number) for CLSO Fund I, CLSO GP I, and CLSO Management I.
72: >
73: > \(e\) **Registered Agent Coordination.** Coordination with Hollowell Technologies, the Client\'s designated registered agent in Delaware, to ensure that each Fund Entity is properly set up for service of process and annual compliance filings.
74: 
75: **3.2 Tax Structuring**
76: 
77: Calderwood & Harkness will provide tax structuring advice in connection with the formation and operation of the Fund, including the following:
78: 
79: > \(a\) **Tax Structuring Memorandum.** Preparation and delivery of a Tax Structuring Memorandum addressing the following topics, among others: (i) unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") and effectively connected income (\"ECI\") planning for tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors; (ii) the application of IRC §1061 to carried interest allocations, including holding period analysis and the implications of the three-year holding period requirement; (iii) state income tax nexus considerations for the Fund, the general partner, and the management company, with a particular focus on Delaware, California, Oregon, Connecticut, and Massachusetts; (iv) blocker corporation structuring, including the use of a Delaware C-Corporation to mitigate UBTI and ECI for certain categories of investors; and (v) carry escrow implications, including the tax treatment of amounts held in escrow and the timing of income recognition. The target delivery date for the Tax Structuring Memorandum is **April 30, 2026**.
80: >
81: > \(b\) **Coordination with Tax Advisor.** Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with Greystone Tax Advisors LLC (Kenneth Liu, Managing Director), the Client\'s independent tax advisor, on all tax structuring matters. We understand that Greystone will be responsible for the preparation of the Fund\'s annual tax returns (Forms 1065 and Schedules K-1) and for providing ongoing tax compliance advice, and that Calderwood & Harkness\'s role is limited to tax structuring and tax-related provisions of the fund documents.
82: 
83: **3.3 Fund Documentation Drafting**
84: 
85: Calderwood & Harkness will prepare the principal fund documents for the Fund, including the following:
86: 
87: > \(a\) **Agreement of Limited Partnership.** Drafting of the Agreement of Limited Partnership of Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP (the \"LPA\"), including all schedules and exhibits thereto. The first draft of the LPA is targeted for delivery on or about **May 31, 2026**. The LPA will address, among other things, the following key economic and governance terms:
88: >
89: > *Economic Terms:*
90: >
91: > • Management Fee: 2.00% per annum of committed capital during the investment period, stepping down to 2.00% of invested capital (or net invested capital, as determined) thereafter;
92: >
93: > • Carried Interest: 20% of net profits, subject to the preferred return and GP catch-up described below;
94: >
95: > • Preferred Return: 8% per annum, compounded annually;
96: >
97: > • GP Catch-up: 100% of distributions after the preferred return has been achieved, until the general partner has received 20% of cumulative net profits;
98: >
99: > • Carry Escrow: 30% of carried interest distributions to be held in escrow pending final liquidation of the Fund to secure the general partner\'s clawback obligation;
100: >
101: > • Clawback: Standard general partner clawback obligation, net of taxes, to be triggered upon final liquidation of the Fund to the extent the general partner has received carried interest distributions in excess of amounts to which it is entitled on a cumulative basis;
102: >
103: > • Recycling Allowance: 15% of aggregate committed capital may be recycled (i.e., proceeds from realized investments may be recalled for reinvestment during the investment period);
104: >
105: > • Concentration Limit: No more than 15% of aggregate committed capital may be invested in any single portfolio company, measured at the time of investment;
106: >
107: > • Organizational Expense Cap: Organizational expenses in excess of \$1,500,000 shall be borne by the general partner or the management company;
108: >
109: > • Broken-Deal Expense Cap: Broken-deal expenses in excess of \$500,000 per unconsummated transaction shall be borne by the general partner or the management company.
110: >
111: > *Governance Provisions:*
112: >
113: > • Key Person Event provisions, identifying Dr. Marcus Yeung and Priya Dasgupta as key persons, with suspension of the investment period upon a key person event and reinstatement mechanics;
114: >
115: > • Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") provisions, including composition, authority, and procedures for the resolution of conflicts of interest;
116: >
117: > • Removal rights, including removal of the general partner for cause and no-fault removal by a supermajority in interest of the limited partners;
118: >
119: > • Default provisions, including the consequences of a limited partner\'s failure to fund a capital call;
120: >
121: > • Excuse and exclusion provisions, permitting limited partners to be excused or excluded from particular investments under specified circumstances (e.g., legal, regulatory, or tax impediments).
122: >
123: > *Regulatory Provisions:*
124: >
125: > • ERISA compliance provisions, including the Fund\'s election to qualify as a \"venture capital operating company\" (\"VCOC\") under Department of Labor Regulation §2510.3-101(d), and the related covenants and operating requirements necessary to maintain VCOC status.
126: >
127: > \(b\) **GP LLC Agreement.** Drafting of the Limited Liability Company Agreement of Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC (the \"GP LLC Agreement\"), setting forth the rights, obligations, and economic arrangements of the members of the general partner entity.
128: >
129: > \(c\) **Management Company LLC Agreement.** Drafting of the Limited Liability Company Agreement of Cobalt Life Sciences Management I, LLC (the \"Management Company LLC Agreement\"), setting forth the organizational and operational terms of the management company.
130: >
131: > \(d\) **Subscription Agreement and Investor Questionnaire.** Preparation of the form Subscription Agreement and Investor Questionnaire to be executed by each limited partner at the time of its commitment to the Fund, including representations and warranties regarding accredited investor and qualified purchaser status, ERISA status, tax status, OFAC compliance, and beneficial ownership.
132: 
133: **3.4 Private Placement Memorandum**
134: 
135: Calderwood & Harkness will prepare the confidential Private Placement Memorandum (the \"PPM\") for the Fund. The PPM will be the principal marketing and disclosure document used in connection with the offering of limited partnership interests in the Fund to prospective investors. We anticipate delivering an outline and first draft of the PPM on or about **June 30, 2026**. The PPM will include, among other things, the following:
136: 
137: > \(a\) An executive summary of the terms of the offering;
138: >
139: > \(b\) A description of the Fund\'s investment strategy, investment process, and target sectors within the life-sciences space;
140: >
141: > \(c\) A comprehensive discussion of risk factors associated with an investment in the Fund, including market risks, strategy-specific risks, regulatory risks, and structural risks;
142: >
143: > \(d\) Regulatory disclosures, including disclosures required under applicable federal and state securities laws;
144: >
145: > \(e\) Biographies of the principals and key investment professionals of Cobalt;
146: >
147: > \(f\) A summary of the material U.S. federal income tax considerations applicable to an investment in the Fund, including considerations for taxable U.S. investors, tax-exempt U.S. investors, and non-U.S. investors; and
148: >
149: > \(g\) Appendices containing the form of LPA and Subscription Agreement, or summaries thereof.
150: 
151: **3.5 Placement Agent Agreement**
152: 
153: Calderwood & Harkness will negotiate and draft the exclusive global placement agent agreement (the \"Placement Agent Agreement\") between the Client (or the general partner of the Fund, as applicable) and sagebrush Capital Partners LLC (\"Sagebrush\") (CRD No. 298714; primary contact: Jonathan Mercer, Managing Director). We understand that sagebrush will serve as the exclusive global placement agent for the Fund, subject to certain carve-outs for the Client\'s existing investor relationships. The principal commercial terms of the Placement Agent Agreement are expected to include the following:
154: 
155: > \(a\) Placement fee of 1.50% of committed capital sourced by sagebrush from third-party investors;
156: >
157: > \(b\) 100% offset of placement fees against the management fee payable by the Fund, such that placement fees are economically borne by the general partner and the management company rather than the limited partners;
158: >
159: > \(c\) A retainer of \$150,000, payable upon execution of the Placement Agent Agreement, to be credited against earned placement fees;
160: >
161: > \(d\) A tail period of 24 months following the termination of the Placement Agent Agreement, during which sagebrush will be entitled to placement fees on commitments received from investors introduced by sagebrush during the term of the engagement.
162: 
163: Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with Ashworth & Lyle LLP (Sara Phan, Partner), counsel to sagebrush, in connection with the negotiation and finalization of the Placement Agent Agreement. The target execution date for the Placement Agent Agreement is **July 15, 2026**. The Placement Agent Agreement will be governed by the laws of the State of New York.
164: 
165: **3.6 Side Letter Framework**
166: 
167: Calderwood & Harkness will prepare a Side Letter Framework Memorandum (the \"Side Letter Memo\") analyzing standard concessions and investor-specific terms that the Client may expect to negotiate with anticipated anchor investors and other significant limited partners. The Side Letter Memo will address, among other things, the following:
168: 
169: > \(a\) Fee discounts and co-investment rights;
170: >
171: > \(b\) Most favored nation (\"MFN\") mechanics, including the scope of MFN elections, carve-outs for certain investor-specific provisions, and the procedures for MFN notification and election;
172: >
173: > \(c\) Reporting and transparency requirements;
174: >
175: > \(d\) Key person and LPAC participation;
176: >
177: > \(e\) Excuse and exclusion rights;
178: >
179: > \(f\) Transfer and secondary market provisions; and
180: >

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP**

Dear Dr. Yeung and Ms. Dasgupta:

Calderwood & Harkness LLP is pleased to confirm the terms of our engagement to serve as fund counsel to Cobalt Ventures LP in connection with the matters described below. We very much look forward to partnering with you and the Cobalt team on this important initiative, and we appreciate the confidence you have placed in our firm. This engagement letter (this \"Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions under which Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness,\" the \"Firm,\" \"we,\" or \"us\") will provide legal services to Cobalt Ventures LP (\"Cobalt\" or the \"Client\").
We ask that you review this Letter carefully and, if the terms are acceptable, execute and return a copy to us as described in Section 12 below.
**[1. Purpose and Introduction]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP is pleased to confirm its engagement by Cobalt Ventures LP to serve as fund counsel in connection with the structuring, formation, and fund-raising for Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP (the \"Fund\" or \"CLSO Fund I\"), a proposed Delaware limited partnership. We understand that the Fund will be Cobalt\'s inaugural dedicated opportunistic life-sciences investment vehicle, and that Cobalt is targeting aggregate committed capital of Seven Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$750,000,000), with a hard cap of One Billion Dollars (\$1,000,000,000).

By way of background, Cobalt is a California-headquartered venture capital sponsor focused on the biotechnology and life-sciences sectors. Founded in 2018 by Dr. Marcus Yeung and Priya Dasgupta, Cobalt currently manages approximately \$420 million in assets under management across two prior vintage vehicles --- Cobalt Ventures Fund A, LP (vintage 2019) and Cobalt Ventures Fund B, LP (vintage 2022). The launch of CLSO Fund I represents a significant strategic milestone for the Cobalt platform, expanding the firm\'s investment mandate into opportunistic life-sciences investments across stage, geography, and modality.

This Letter sets forth the terms under which Calderwood & Harkness will provide legal services in connection with the structuring, formation, and fund-raising of the Fund and related entities, and it supersedes any prior oral or written understandings between the parties regarding the scope and terms of this engagement.
**[2. Client Identification]{.underline}**

The Client for purposes of this engagement is **Cobalt Ventures LP**, a Delaware limited partnership (Delaware LP File No. 7824931; California Secretary of State File No. 202118412387; EIN: 83-2947561), with its principal place of business at 3400 Sand Hill Road, Suite 220, Menlo Park, California 94025, and its registered agent for service of process in Delaware at Hollowell Technologies, 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801.
In addition to Cobalt Ventures LP, Calderwood & Harkness\'s representation under this engagement extends to the following entities, each of which is to be formed in connection with the Fund:
> \(a\) **Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership, to be formed, which will serve as the main investment vehicle for the Fund;
> \(b\) **Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC** --- a Delaware limited liability company, to be formed, which will serve as the general partner of the Fund;

> \(c\) **Cobalt Life Sciences Management I, LLC** --- a Delaware limited liability company, to be formed, which will serve as the management company and will be party to the management agreement with the Fund; and

> \(d\) **Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I (Blocker), Inc.** --- a Delaware C-Corporation, to be formed if and when determined to be necessary or advisable for purposes of establishing a taxable blocker structure for certain categories of investors, including tax-exempt and non-U.S. limited partners.

The foregoing entities are collectively referred to herein as the \"Fund Entities.\" As formation documents are prepared and filed for each Fund Entity, such entity shall be deemed a client of the Firm under the terms of this Letter without the need for a separate engagement letter, unless the Firm and the Client agree otherwise in writing.

**Important Clarification Regarding Scope of Representation.** Calderwood & Harkness does not represent, and will not represent in connection with this engagement, any individual limited partner or prospective limited partner of the Fund, any placement agent engaged by the Fund (including sagebrush Capital Partners LLC), or any other third-party service provider to the Fund. Each such party should retain and rely upon its own independent legal counsel with respect to its interests in or obligations to the Fund.
**[3. Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**

The scope of Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement encompasses the following workstreams, each of which is described in greater detail below. To the extent the Client requests legal services that fall outside the scope described in this Section 3, such services will be provided only upon mutual written agreement and may be subject to a separate engagement letter or an amendment to this Letter.
**3.1 Fund Structuring and Entity Formation**

Calderwood & Harkness will advise the Client on the optimal legal and organizational structure for the Fund and will be responsible for the formation of each Fund Entity. This workstream will include the following:

> \(a\) **Structural Analysis.** Analysis of fund structure alternatives, including a single-tier Delaware limited partnership, parallel fund structures (including for non-U.S. investors or investors requiring a separately managed account), blocker corporation arrangements, alternative investment vehicle (\"AIV\") structures, and master-feeder options. Our analysis will take into account the anticipated investor base, the Client\'s investment strategy, tax efficiency, regulatory considerations, and administrative complexity.

> \(b\) **Fund Structuring Memorandum.** Preparation and delivery of a comprehensive Fund Structuring Memorandum setting forth Calderwood & Harkness\'s analysis and recommendations regarding the recommended fund architecture, including a diagram of the proposed entity structure, a summary of the principal advantages and disadvantages of each structural alternative considered, and our recommended approach. The target delivery date for the Fund Structuring Memorandum is **April 30, 2026**.

> \(c\) **Delaware Formation Filings.** Preparation and filing of the Certificate of Limited Partnership for Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP, and the Certificates of Formation for Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC and Cobalt Life Sciences Management I, LLC, with the Delaware Division of Corporations. If the blocker corporation is determined to be necessary, Calderwood & Harkness will also prepare and file the Certificate of Incorporation for Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I (Blocker), Inc.
> \(d\) **EIN Applications.** Preparation and submission of IRS Form SS-4 (Application for Employer Identification Number) for CLSO Fund I, CLSO GP I, and CLSO Management I.

> \(e\) **Registered Agent Coordination.** Coordination with Hollowell Technologies, the Client\'s designated registered agent in Delaware, to ensure that each Fund Entity is properly set up for service of process and annual compliance filings.
**3.2 Tax Structuring**
Calderwood & Harkness will provide tax structuring advice in connection with the formation and operation of the Fund, including the following:

> \(a\) **Tax Structuring Memorandum.** Preparation and delivery of a Tax Structuring Memorandum addressing the following topics, among others: (i) unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") and effectively connected income (\"ECI\") planning for tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors; (ii) the application of IRC §1061 to carried interest allocations, including holding period analysis and the implications of the three-year holding period requirement; (iii) state income tax nexus considerations for the Fund, the general partner, and the management company, with a particular focus on Delaware, California, Oregon, Connecticut, and Massachusetts; (iv) blocker corporation structuring, including the use of a Delaware C-Corporation to mitigate UBTI and ECI for certain categories of investors; and (v) carry escrow implications, including the tax treatment of amounts held in escrow and the timing of income recognition. The target delivery date for the Tax Structuring Memorandum is **April 30, 2026**.

> \(b\) **Coordination with Tax Advisor.** Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with Greystone Tax Advisors LLC (Kenneth Liu, Managing Director), the Client\'s independent tax advisor, on all tax structuring matters. We understand that Greystone will be responsible for the preparation of the Fund\'s annual tax returns (Forms 1065 and Schedules K-1) and for providing ongoing tax compliance advice, and that Calderwood & Harkness\'s role is limited to tax structuring and tax-related provisions of the fund documents.
**3.3 Fund Documentation Drafting**
Calderwood & Harkness will prepare the principal fund documents for the Fund, including the following:

> \(a\) **Agreement of Limited Partnership.** Drafting of the Agreement of Limited Partnership of Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP (the \"LPA\"), including all schedules and exhibits thereto. The first draft of the LPA is targeted for delivery on or about **May 31, 2026**. The LPA will address, among other things, the following key economic and governance terms:
> *Economic Terms:*
> • Management Fee: 2.00% per annum of committed capital during the investment period, stepping down to 2.00% of invested capital (or net invested capital, as determined) thereafter;
> • Carried Interest: 20% of net profits, subject to the preferred return and GP catch-up described below;
> • Preferred Return: 8% per annum, compounded annually;
> • GP Catch-up: 100% of distributions after the preferred return has been achieved, until the general partner has received 20% of cumulative net profits;
> • Carry Escrow: 30% of carried interest distributions to be held in escrow pending final liquidation of the Fund to secure the general partner\'s clawback obligation;

> • Clawback: Standard general partner clawback obligation, net of taxes, to be triggered upon final liquidation of the Fund to the extent the general partner has received carried interest distributions in excess of amounts to which it is entitled on a cumulative basis;
> • Recycling Allowance: 15% of aggregate committed capital may be recycled (i.e., proceeds from realized investments may be recalled for reinvestment during the investment period);
> • Concentration Limit: No more than 15% of aggregate committed capital may be invested in any single portfolio company, measured at the time of investment;
> • Organizational Expense Cap: Organizational expenses in excess of \$1,500,000 shall be borne by the general partner or the management company;
> • Broken-Deal Expense Cap: Broken-deal expenses in excess of \$500,000 per unconsummated transaction shall be borne by the general partner or the management company.
> *Governance Provisions:*
> • Key Person Event provisions, identifying Dr. Marcus Yeung and Priya Dasgupta as key persons, with suspension of the investment period upon a key person event and reinstatement mechanics;
> • Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") provisions, including composition, authority, and procedures for the resolution of conflicts of interest;
> • Removal rights, including removal of the general partner for cause and no-fault removal by a supermajority in interest of the limited partners;
> • Default provisions, including the consequences of a limited partner\'s failure to fund a capital call;
> • Excuse and exclusion provisions, permitting limited partners to be excused or excluded from particular investments under specified circumstances (e.g., legal, regulatory, or tax impediments).
> *Regulatory Provisions:*

> • ERISA compliance provisions, including the Fund\'s election to qualify as a \"venture capital operating company\" (\"VCOC\") under Department of Labor Regulation §2510.3-101(d), and the related covenants and operating requirements necessary to maintain VCOC status.

> \(b\) **GP LLC Agreement.** Drafting of the Limited Liability Company Agreement of Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC (the \"GP LLC Agreement\"), setting forth the rights, obligations, and economic arrangements of the members of the general partner entity.

> \(c\) **Management Company LLC Agreement.** Drafting of the Limited Liability Company Agreement of Cobalt Life Sciences Management I, LLC (the \"Management Company LLC Agreement\"), setting forth the organizational and operational terms of the management company.

> \(d\) **Subscription Agreement and Investor Questionnaire.** Preparation of the form Subscription Agreement and Investor Questionnaire to be executed by each limited partner at the time of its commitment to the Fund, including representations and warranties regarding accredited investor and qualified purchaser status, ERISA status, tax status, OFAC compliance, and beneficial ownership.
**3.4 Private Placement Memorandum**

Calderwood & Harkness will prepare the confidential Private Placement Memorandum (the \"PPM\") for the Fund. The PPM will be the principal marketing and disclosure document used in connection with the offering of limited partnership interests in the Fund to prospective investors. We anticipate delivering an outline and first draft of the PPM on or about **June 30, 2026**. The PPM will include, among other things, the following:
> \(a\) An executive summary of the terms of the offering;
> \(b\) A description of the Fund\'s investment strategy, investment process, and target sectors within the life-sciences space;
> \(c\) A comprehensive discussion of risk factors associated with an investment in the Fund, including market risks, strategy-specific risks, regulatory risks, and structural risks;
> \(d\) Regulatory disclosures, including disclosures required under applicable federal and state securities laws;
> \(e\) Biographies of the principals and key investment professionals of Cobalt;

> \(f\) A summary of the material U.S. federal income tax considerations applicable to an investment in the Fund, including considerations for taxable U.S. investors, tax-exempt U.S. investors, and non-U.S. investors; and
> \(g\) Appendices containing the form of LPA and Subscription Agreement, or summaries thereof.
**3.5 Placement Agent Agreement**

Calderwood & Harkness will negotiate and draft the exclusive global placement agent agreement (the \"Placement Agent Agreement\") between the Client (or the general partner of the Fund, as applicable) and sagebrush Capital Partners LLC (\"Sagebrush\") (CRD No. 298714; primary contact: Jonathan Mercer, Managing Director). We understand that sagebrush will serve as the exclusive global placement agent for the Fund, subject to certain carve-outs for the Client\'s existing investor relationships. The principal commercial terms of the Placement Agent Agreement are expected to include the following:
> \(a\) Placement fee of 1.50% of committed capital sourced by sagebrush from third-party investors;

> \(b\) 100% offset of placement fees against the management fee payable by the Fund, such that placement fees are economically borne by the general partner and the management company rather than the limited partners;
> \(c\) A retainer of \$150,000, payable upon execution of the Placement Agent Agreement, to be credited against earned placement fees;

> \(d\) A tail period of 24 months following the termination of the Placement Agent Agreement, during which sagebrush will be entitled to placement fees on commitments received from investors introduced by sagebrush during the term of the engagement.

Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with Ashworth & Lyle LLP (Sara Phan, Partner), counsel to sagebrush, in connection with the negotiation and finalization of the Placement Agent Agreement. The target execution date for the Placement Agent Agreement is **July 15, 2026**. The Placement Agent Agreement will be governed by the laws of the State of New York.
**3.6 Side Letter Framework**

Calderwood & Harkness will prepare a Side Letter Framework Memorandum (the \"Side Letter Memo\") analyzing standard concessions and investor-specific terms that the Client may expect to negotiate with anticipated anchor investors and other significant limited partners. The Side Letter Memo will address, among other things, the following:
> \(a\) Fee discounts and co-investment rights;
> \(b\) Most favored nation (\"MFN\") mechanics, including the scope of MFN elections, carve-outs for certain investor-specific provisions, and the procedures for MFN notification and election;
> \(c\) Reporting and transparency requirements;
> \(d\) Key person and LPAC participation;
> \(e\) Excuse and exclusion rights;
> \(f\) Transfer and secondary market provisions; and
> \(g\) Regulatory, tax, and ERISA-specific accommodations.
As investor commitments are received and side letter negotiations are initiated, Calderwood & Harkness will draft, negotiate, and finalize individual side letters on behalf of the Client.
**3.7 Regulatory Compliance**

Calderwood & Harkness will prepare and maintain a comprehensive Regulatory Compliance Checklist to track the Fund\'s compliance obligations throughout the formation and fund-raising process. The Regulatory Compliance Checklist will address, among other things, the following:

> \(a\) **SEC Form D Filing.** Preparation and filing of SEC Form D in connection with the offering of limited partnership interests in the Fund under Regulation D of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, under either Rule 506(b) or Rule 506(c), as determined in consultation with the Client;

> \(b\) **Blue Sky Filings.** Preparation and filing of state securities notice filings (blue sky filings) in each jurisdiction in which limited partnership interests are offered or sold, as required;

> \(c\) **Form ADV Amendment / Registration Evaluation.** Amendment of Cobalt\'s existing Form ADV filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission in connection with the Fund launch. We understand that Cobalt currently maintains Exempt Reporting Adviser status under SEC File No. 802-11934. Calderwood & Harkness, in coordination with Fielding & O\'Hara PLLC (Brian Liddell, Partner), the Client\'s regulatory counsel for SEC investment adviser compliance, Advisers Act exemptions, and Form ADV matters, will evaluate whether the launch of CLSO Fund I and the anticipated increase in regulatory assets under management will require Cobalt to transition from Exempt Reporting Adviser status to full registration as an investment adviser under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940;
> \(d\) **ERISA/VCOC Compliance.** Monitoring and advising on compliance with ERISA plan asset rules, including the maintenance of VCOC status as described in Section 3.3(a) above;

> \(e\) **OFAC/AML/KYC Requirements.** Advising on the anti-money laundering, know-your-customer, and OFAC screening procedures to be implemented in connection with the acceptance of investor subscriptions; and
> \(f\) **State-Specific Notice Filings.** Preparation of any additional state-specific notice filings required in connection with the Fund\'s activities.

Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with Fielding & O\'Hara PLLC on all matters relating to SEC investment adviser registration, Advisers Act compliance, and Form ADV filings, as Fielding & O\'Hara serves as the Client\'s primary regulatory counsel for those matters.

Cobalt Ventures LP is organized as a Delaware limited partnership (DE LP File No. 7824931; California Secretary of State File No. 202118412387; EIN: 83-2947561). The firm\'s registered agent in Delaware is Hollowell Technologies, 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801.
52: 
53: Cobalt currently manages approximately **\$420 million** in assets under management across two prior vintage vehicles: Cobalt Ventures Fund A, LP and Cobalt Ventures Fund B, LP. The Sponsor\'s historical strategy has centered on single-fund venture investments in the range of \$5 million to \$25 million, targeting early- and growth-stage biotechnology companies. The launch of CLSO Fund I represents a significant evolution in the Sponsor\'s strategy, as discussed in Section II.B below.
54: 
55: In addition to the co-founders, **Alan Whitford** serves as Partner, Head of Research. Mr. Whitford holds a PhD in Molecular Biology from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and previously served as Chief Scientific Officer at Meridian Therapeutics. He joined Cobalt in 2021 and plays a critical role in scientific diligence, portfolio company monitoring, and strategic advisory. Mr. Whitford will participate in the Fund\'s carried interest allocation as described in Section III.
56: 
57: **[B. Investment Strategy for CLSO Fund I]{.underline}**
58: 
59: CLSO Fund I represents a material step-up in the Sponsor\'s investment strategy, transitioning from venture-stage investments with smaller check sizes to larger, concentrated positions in later-stage life-sciences companies. The Fund\'s investment strategy is defined by the following parameters:
60: 
61: **Sector Focus.** The Fund will target investments in three primary sub-sectors within life sciences:
62: 
63: > \(i\) *Clinical-stage therapeutics* --- companies with drug candidates in Phase II clinical trials or later, where meaningful clinical data exists or is expected within the Fund\'s investment horizon and where regulatory pathways to approval are identifiable;
64: >
65: > \(ii\) *Medical devices* --- companies pursuing FDA 510(k) clearance or Premarket Approval (PMA) pathways, with a preference for devices addressing large, underserved markets with demonstrable clinical utility; and
66: >
67: > \(iii\) *Platform biotechnology* --- companies developing enabling technologies in gene editing, synthetic biology, and AI-enabled drug discovery, where the platform has the potential to generate multiple product candidates or licensing opportunities.
68: 
69: **Geographic Focus.** The Fund will invest primarily in North American companies. Up to twenty-five percent (25%) of aggregate commitments may be deployed in companies headquartered or principally operating in Western Europe and Israel, reflecting the maturity and depth of the life-sciences ecosystems in those regions. This geographic allocation is an investment-level parameter and does not, standing alone, necessitate an offshore fund vehicle, although it may inform AIV considerations for specific transactions (for example, investments requiring a local holding entity in a European jurisdiction).
70: 
71: **Check Size.** The Fund targets initial investments in the range of **\$30,000,000 to \$100,000,000** per portfolio company, with capital reserved for follow-on investments in existing portfolio companies. This represents a significant increase from the Sponsor\'s historical check sizes of \$5 million to \$25 million, consistent with the Fund\'s focus on later-stage, larger-capitalization opportunities.
72: 
73: **Control and Governance.** The Fund will target board seats or contractual governance rights (such as board observer seats, information rights, protective provisions, and consent rights) in one hundred percent (100%) of its portfolio companies. This governance focus is not only central to the Fund\'s value-creation strategy but is also essential for the Fund\'s intended qualification as a \"venture capital operating company\" under the Department of Labor\'s plan asset regulations, as discussed in Section VII below.
74: 
75: **Concentration and Reserves.** The Fund\'s Limited Partnership Agreement (the \"LPA\") will include a concentration limit of fifteen percent (15%) of aggregate commitments per investment, and the Fund will maintain a recycling allowance of fifteen percent (15%) of aggregate commitments to permit redeployment of certain realized proceeds during the investment period.
76: 
77: **[C. Anticipated Investor Base]{.underline}**
78: 
79: The diversity and composition of the Fund\'s anticipated investor base is a primary driver of the structural analysis in this memorandum. Cobalt has identified three prospective anchor or seed investors whose investment parameters, tax status, and regulatory requirements inform the structural flexibility that the Fund must accommodate:
80: 
81: **1. Ironwood Public Employees\' Retirement System (\"Ironwood PERS\")**
82: 
83: Ironwood PERS is a state government pension fund organized under the laws of the State of Oregon, with approximately \$62 billion in assets under management. The anticipated commitment from Ironwood PERS is **\$100,000,000**. The primary contact is Helen Tsao, Director of Private Markets, whose offices are located at 900 Capitol Way NE, Suite 400, Salem, Oregon 97301.
84: 
85: Ironwood PERS\'s investment committee approval is tentatively scheduled for June 2026. Ms. Tsao has communicated the following key requirements for Ironwood PERS\'s investment in the Fund:
86: 
87: > • **Most Favored Nation (\"MFN\") side letter** --- Ironwood PERS expects to receive an MFN provision entitling it to elect any material economic or governance terms granted to other limited partners in side letters, subject to customary carve-outs.
88: >
89: > • **Advisory committee seat** --- Ironwood PERS has specifically requested a seat on the Fund\'s LP Advisory Committee (the \"LPAC\").
90: >
91: > • **Co-investment rights at no fee/no carry** --- Ironwood PERS expects the right to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund on a no-management-fee, no-carried-interest basis.
92: >
93: > • **Annual in-person reporting** --- Ironwood PERS requires that the Sponsor provide an annual in-person report to Ironwood PERS\'s investment staff, either in Salem, Oregon or at a mutually agreed location.
94: 
95: As a state government pension fund, Ironwood PERS is generally exempt from federal income tax and is typically not subject to unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") in most investment scenarios. However, UBTI treatment should be confirmed for debt-financed income scenarios, as discussed in the Tax Structuring Memorandum. Ironwood PERS\'s status as a governmental plan means it is generally not subject to ERISA, although it may be treated as a \"benefit plan investor\" for purposes of the Department of Labor\'s plan asset regulations under certain analyses. The pay-to-play implications of Ironwood PERS\'s status as a state pension fund are discussed in Section VIII.C below.
96: 
97: **2. Northgate Endowment Management LLC (\"Northgate\")**
98: 
99: Northgate Endowment Management LLC is the investment management arm of a major university endowment with approximately \$8.5 billion in assets under management. Northgate is organized as a Delaware limited liability company. The anticipated commitment is **\$50,000,000**. The primary contact is David Park, Senior Portfolio Manager -- Life Sciences Allocation, whose offices are located at 77 Brattle Street, 4th Floor, Cambridge, Massachusetts 02138.
100: 
101: Northgate has communicated the following key requirements:
102: 
103: > • **ERISA-compliant carve-out structure** --- Northgate has requested a structure that ensures compliance with ERISA to the extent applicable. This request likely reflects concerns about the university endowment\'s potential status as a benefit plan investor and the need to ensure that the Fund qualifies for an exception from plan asset treatment (such as the VCOC exception), or alternatively, that Northgate\'s participation is structured through a separate vehicle that independently satisfies ERISA requirements.
104: >
105: > • **Co-investment rights** --- Northgate expects the right to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund.
106: >
107: > • **Annual detailed portfolio analytics** --- Northgate requires comprehensive annual portfolio-level reporting, including detailed valuation methodologies, attribution analysis, and clinical milestone tracking for each portfolio company.
108: 
109: As a university endowment, Northgate is likely tax-exempt under IRC §501(c)(3), which means it may be subject to UBTI on certain categories of investment income, including debt-financed income and income from the conduct of an unrelated trade or business. Northgate may therefore wish to participate in certain investments through a blocker entity, as discussed in Section IV.E below.
110: 
111: **3. Pinnacle Insurance Group, Inc. (\"Pinnacle\")**
112: 
113: Pinnacle Insurance Group, Inc. is a life and annuity insurance company organized under the laws of the State of Connecticut, with a general account of approximately \$28 billion. The anticipated commitment is **\$75,000,000**. The primary contact is Rachel Stein, Senior Vice President -- Alternative Investments, whose offices are located at 500 Asylum Avenue, Hartford, Connecticut 06103.
114: 
115: Pinnacle has communicated the following key requirements:
116: 
117: > • **Insurance regulatory compliance provisions** --- Pinnacle requires that the Fund\'s structure and documentation comply with applicable Connecticut insurance regulations governing permissible investments by insurers, including limitations on asset concentration, investment-grade and below-investment-grade allocations, and derivative instrument restrictions. Pinnacle may also require specific reporting formats for insurance regulatory filings.
118: >
119: > • **blocker entity for certain tax-exempt structures** --- Pinnacle has specifically requested access to a blocker entity for investments generating income that creates adverse tax, reserve, or risk-based capital treatment under Connecticut insurance accounting rules.
120: >
121: > • **Quarterly NAV statements** --- Pinnacle requires quarterly net asset value statements for financial reporting and regulatory compliance purposes.
122: 
123: As a taxable insurance company, Pinnacle\'s tax considerations differ from those of tax-exempt investors, but Pinnacle may nonetheless prefer blocker participation for investments generating debt-financed income, certain operating company income, or income with adverse insurance regulatory accounting characteristics. The blocker entity analysis is addressed in Section IV.E.
124: 
125: **4. Aggregate Anticipated Anchor Commitments and Remaining Capital to Raise**
126: 
127: The aggregate anticipated commitments from the three identified anchor investors total **\$225,000,000** (\$100 million from Ironwood PERS, \$50 million from Northgate, and \$75 million from Pinnacle). The General Partner\'s commitment will be a minimum of two percent (2%) of aggregate commitments, which at the target fund size of \$750 million equals **\$15,000,000**. Accordingly, the remaining capital to be raised from additional institutional investors to reach the target fund size is approximately **\$510,000,000** (\$750 million minus \$225 million minus \$15 million).
128: 
129: **5. Placement Agent**
130: 
131: Cobalt has engaged **sagebrush Capital Partners LLC** (Jonathan Mercer, Managing Director) as the exclusive global placement agent for the Fund. Sagebrush is a registered broker-dealer with the Securities and Exchange Commission (CRD No. 298714). The placement agent engagement is described in further detail in Section X.E.
132: 
133: **6. Structural Implications of Investor Base Diversity**
134: 
135: The diversity of the anticipated investor base --- encompassing a state pension fund, a university endowment, a life and annuity insurance company, and additional institutional investors yet to be identified by sagebrush --- drives the need for significant structural flexibility in the Fund\'s architecture. Each investor category presents distinct tax, regulatory, and governance requirements that the Fund\'s structure must accommodate. The structural analysis in Section IV is informed by these investor-specific considerations.
136: 
137: **[III. KEY FUND ECONOMIC TERMS (SUMMARY)]{.underline}**
138: 
139: The following table summarizes the core economic and governance terms that inform the structural decisions analyzed in this memorandum. These terms are preliminary and will be set forth in detail in the LPA, the first draft of which is targeted for circulation to the principals on May 31, 2026. The terms presented here reflect our discussions with the Cobalt principals to date and are subject to further refinement during the LPA drafting process and in response to investor feedback during the marketing period.
140: 
141:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
142:   **Parameter**                               **Term**
143:   ------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
144:   Target Fund Size                            \$750,000,000
145: 
146:   Hard Cap                                    \$1,000,000,000
147: 
148:   First Close Minimum                         \$250,000,000
149: 
150:   GP Commitment                               Minimum 2% of aggregate commitments (\$15,000,000 at \$750M target)
151:

153: 
154:   Management Fee --- Post-Investment Period   2.00% per annum on invested capital (net of write-offs/write-downs and realized proceeds)

161:

163:

185: 
186:   Key Person                                  Dr. Marcus Yeung and Priya Dasgupta; trigger upon either ceasing to devote substantially all business time to Fund

189:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
190: 
191: **Carried Interest Allocation Among Principals.** The carried interest entitlement will be allocated among the principals of the General Partner as follows: Dr. Marcus Yeung --- 55%; Priya Dasgupta --- 35%; Alan Whitford --- 10%. The specific mechanics of this allocation, including vesting schedules, forfeiture provisions, and treatment upon departure of a principal, will be governed by the GP LLC Agreement and any ancillary carried interest allocation agreements, the drafting of which is a separate workstream targeted for completion concurrently with the first draft LPA.
192: 
193: **[Fee Waterfall Illustration (at \$750M Target)]{.underline}**
194: 
195: To illustrate the interplay between the management fee, placement fee, and fee offset mechanics, we present the following simplified calculations at the target fund size of \$750 million:
196: 
197: **Annual Management Fee During Investment Period:**
198: 
199: > \$750,000,000 × 2.00% = **\$15,000,000** per annum
200: 
201: **Aggregate Management Fees Over 5-Year Investment Period:**
202: 
203: > \$15,000,000 × 5 = **\$75,000,000**
204: 
205: **Illustrative Placement Fee (Assuming sagebrush Sources Entire Third-Party Capital):**
206: 
207: > Total third-party commitments (excluding GP commitment): \$750,000,000 − \$15,000,000 = \$735,000,000
208: >
209: > \$735,000,000 × 1.50% = **\$11,025,000** (fully offset against management fee over the Fund\'s life)
210: 
211: **Net Management Fee to CLSO Management After Full Placement Fee Offset:**
212: 
213: > \$75,000,000 − \$11,025,000 = **\$63,975,000** over the five-year investment period
214: >
215: > This represents an effective net management fee rate of approximately 1.71% per annum on aggregate commitments during the investment period, after giving effect to the placement fee offset.
216: 
217: We note that these calculations are illustrative only. The actual placement fee will be based on the commitments actually sourced by sagebrush (as opposed to commitments obtained directly by the Cobalt principals), and the offset will be applied on a pro rata basis over the Fund\'s life in accordance with the offset mechanics to be specified in the LPA. Additionally, transaction and monitoring fees received by the Management Company from portfolio companies will be subject to an eighty percent (80%) offset against the management fee, further reducing the effective management fee borne by limited partners. The post-investment period management fee, calculated on invested capital rather than aggregate commitments, will decline as portfolio companies are realized, resulting in a naturally declining fee base during the harvest period of the Fund.
218: 
219: **[IV. FUND STRUCTURE ALTERNATIVES ANALYSIS]{.underline}**
220: 
221: This Section IV presents our analysis of six structural alternatives for the Fund. For each alternative, we describe the structure, evaluate its advantages and disadvantages in the context of the Fund\'s specific circumstances, and provide our recommendation. We note that these alternatives are not mutually exclusive --- our recommended approach combines elements of several alternatives to achieve the optimal structure for the Fund.
222: 
223: **[A. Option 1: Single-Tier Delaware Limited Partnership (Recommended)]{.underline}**
224: 
225: **1. Description.** Under this alternative, the Fund would be organized as a **single Delaware limited partnership**: Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP. The Fund would be formed under the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act, 6 Del. C. §§17-101 *et seq.* (the \"DRULPA\"), and would be governed by a limited partnership agreement entered into by the General Partner and all limited partners.
226: 
227: **Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company, would serve as the general partner of the Fund. The General Partner would be managed by Dr. Marcus Yeung and Priya Dasgupta as managing members. The General Partner would hold the carried interest entitlement and would be responsible for all fund management and investment decisions, subject to the terms of the LPA.
228: 
229: **Cobalt Life Sciences Management I, LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company, would serve as the management company. The Management Company would employ the Fund\'s investment professionals (including Dr. Yeung, Ms. Dasgupta, Mr. Whitford, and future hires), receive the management fee from the Fund, and bear organizational expenses in excess of the \$1,500,000 cap set forth in the LPA.
230: 
231: Under this single-tier structure, all limited partners would invest directly into the Fund LP. Each limited partner would subscribe for a limited partnership interest in the Fund by executing a subscription agreement and the LPA (or a joinder thereto), and would be subject to capital calls and entitled to distributions in accordance with the terms of the LPA.
232: 
233: This core structure would be supplemented by ancillary mechanisms --- including AIV provisions, a blocker corporation, and parallel fund enabling provisions --- as described in Sections IV.C through IV.F below, to address the specific needs of particular investors or transactions.
234: 
235: **2. Advantages.** The single-tier Delaware limited partnership offers several significant advantages for the Fund:
236: 
237: **Simplicity and Transparency.** A single fund entity reduces administrative complexity, audit costs, and investor confusion. All limited partners participate in a common pool of investments and are subject to a single waterfall calculation, which simplifies reporting, valuation, and distribution mechanics. Institutional investors and their investment consultants are highly familiar with single-tier Delaware LP structures and can efficiently evaluate the Fund\'s terms and governance.
238: 
239: **Market Standard.** The single-tier Delaware LP is the market-standard structure for U.S. domestic life-sciences, venture capital, and growth equity funds at the Fund\'s target size. Based on our experience advising on fund formations in the life-sciences sector, approximately seventy-five to eighty percent of U.S.-sponsored life-sciences funds with target sizes between \$500 million and \$1 billion employ a single-tier Delaware LP as their primary vehicle, supplemented by ancillary structures as needed.
240: 
241: **Straightforward Waterfall Mechanics.** With a single pool of capital, the distribution waterfall --- including the return of capital, preferred return, GP catch-up, and carried interest --- can be calculated across the entire fund on a unified basis. This avoids the complexities of cross-entity waterfall aggregation that arise in master-feeder and multi-vehicle structures.
242: 
243: **Familiarity to Existing Investor Base.** Cobalt\'s existing investor base in Fund A and Fund B is familiar with single-tier Delaware LP structures. Maintaining structural consistency across the Sponsor\'s fund family reduces investor due diligence burden and facilitates re-ups by existing limited partners.
244: 
245: **Lower Formation and Ongoing Costs.** A single-tier structure requires the formation of fewer entities (the Fund LP, the GP LLC, and the Management Company LLC) compared to a master-feeder or multi-vehicle architecture. Ongoing costs --- including audit fees, tax return preparation, fund administration, and legal compliance --- are correspondingly lower.
246: 
247: **Clear Governance Framework.** A single fund entity permits a single LPAC, a single set of LP consent mechanisms, and a single LPA. Governance provisions are applied uniformly to all limited partners, and the GP\'s authority and obligations are defined in a single governing document (subject to side letter modifications for individual investors).
248: 
249: **3. Disadvantages and Limitations**
250: 
251: The single-tier Delaware LP structure has certain limitations that should be acknowledged:
252: 
253: **Tax-Exempt and Non-U.S. Investor Considerations.** A single-tier LP does not inherently address UBTI or ECI concerns for tax-exempt or non-U.S. investors. Income generated by the Fund flows through to all limited partners on a pro rata basis, including categories of income (such as debt-financed income or operating company income) that may give rise to UBTI for tax-exempt investors or ECI for non-U.S. investors. This limitation is addressed through the blocker corporation (Section IV.E) and AIV mechanics (Section IV.D) described below.
254: 
255: **Non-U.S. Investor Demand.** If significant non-U.S. investor demand materializes during the fundraising process, a single-tier Delaware LP may not be the optimal vehicle for all investor constituencies. Non-U.S. investors may prefer to invest through an offshore vehicle to avoid potential U.S. tax filing obligations and withholding tax complexities. This concern is addressed through the parallel fund option described in Section IV.C.
256: 
257: **Insurance Regulatory Considerations.** Pinnacle Insurance Group, as a Connecticut-domiciled life and annuity insurer, may require blocker entity participation for certain investments that generate income with adverse insurance regulatory accounting characteristics. A single-tier LP does not, standing alone, address these concerns, but the blocker mechanism described in Section IV.E provides the necessary accommodation.
258: 
259: **4. Recommendation. The single-tier Delaware limited partnership is our recommended primary fund vehicle.** Based on the Fund\'s target investor base (which is predominantly U.S. institutional), the Fund\'s target size (\$750 million), the Fund\'s investment strategy (clinical-stage therapeutics, medical devices, and platform biotechnology), and prevailing market practice for life-sciences opportunistic funds, the single-tier Delaware LP provides the optimal combination of simplicity, cost-efficiency, and institutional acceptability.
260: 
261: The limitations identified above --- primarily relating to UBTI/ECI planning for tax-sensitive investors and potential non-U.S. investor demand --- are effectively addressed through the ancillary structures described in Sections IV.C through IV.E below. These ancillary structures are additive to the core single-tier architecture and do not require any modification to the primary fund vehicle.
262: 
263: **[B. Option 2: Dual Master-Feeder Structure]{.underline}**
264: 
265: **1. Description.** Under a dual master-feeder structure, investment activity would be conducted through a **master fund** --- organized either as a Delaware limited partnership or as an offshore entity (such as a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership) --- that receives capital through one or more **feeder funds**. The typical architecture involves two feeder vehicles:
266: 
267: > \(a\) A *domestic feeder* --- organized as a Delaware limited partnership --- through which U.S. taxable investors subscribe. The domestic feeder invests substantially all of its assets into the master fund.
268: >
269: > \(b\) An *offshore feeder* --- organized as a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership, a Cayman Islands exempted company, or a similar offshore entity --- through which non-U.S. investors and U.S. tax-exempt investors subscribe. The offshore feeder similarly invests substantially all of its assets into the master fund. The offshore feeder may function as a blocker for UBTI and ECI purposes, depending on its entity classification for U.S. tax purposes.
270: 
271: Each feeder is a standalone entity with its own governing documents, although the economic terms (management fee, carried interest, preferred return, and distribution waterfall) are designed to replicate the master fund\'s terms. The general partner (or an affiliate) manages all entities, and investment decisions are made at the master fund level.
272: 
273: **2. Advantages.** The master-feeder structure offers certain advantages:
274: 
275: **Clean Investor Segregation.** The master-feeder architecture cleanly separates U.S. taxable, U.S. tax-exempt, and non-U.S. investor constituencies into distinct legal entities, each of which can be structured to optimize the tax treatment of its particular investor class.
276: 
277: **Offshore blocker Functionality.** An offshore feeder organized as an entity classified as a corporation for U.S. tax purposes (such as a Cayman Islands exempted company that does not elect partnership treatment) can serve as a blocker for UBTI and ECI, shielding tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors from flow-through of undesirable categories of income.
278: 
279: **Established Architecture.** The master-feeder structure is well-established in hedge fund and larger private equity fund contexts, and sophisticated institutional investors are familiar with its mechanics.
280: 
281: **3. Disadvantages.** Despite its structural elegance, the master-feeder architecture presents significant disadvantages for the Fund:
282: 
283: **Incremental Formation and Ongoing Costs.** A full master-feeder requires the formation and maintenance of multiple entities across multiple jurisdictions. Offshore legal counsel (Cayman Islands or other offshore jurisdiction) must be engaged for the formation and ongoing compliance of the offshore feeder. Registration fees, annual government fees, and economic substance requirements in the offshore jurisdiction add to the cost burden. Dual (or triple) audit engagements, dual fund administration, and multiple sets of tax returns significantly increase ongoing operating costs.
284: 
285: **Disproportionate Complexity.** The complexity of a master-feeder structure is disproportionate to the Fund\'s anticipated investor base. The three identified anchor investors --- Ironwood PERS, Northgate, and Pinnacle --- are all U.S. domestic institutional investors. No significant non-U.S. fundraising target has been identified to date. While sagebrush may source non-U.S. capital during the marketing process, the current pipeline does not support the formation costs and ongoing administrative burden of a full master-feeder at this time.
286: 
287: **Geographic Investment Allocation Is Not Determinative.** The Fund\'s investment strategy permits up to twenty-five percent of aggregate commitments to be deployed in Western Europe and Israel. This geographic allocation relates to the location of portfolio companies --- not the domicile of investors --- and does not, standing alone, require an offshore fund vehicle.
288: 
289: **Market Practice.** In our experience, first-time opportunistic life-sciences funds at the \$750 million target size generally do not employ a master-feeder structure unless substantial non-U.S. limited partner demand (typically in excess of \$100 million to \$150 million) exists at the time of fund formation or is reasonably anticipated.
290: 
291: **4. Recommendation. The dual master-feeder structure is not recommended at this time.** The structure\'s incremental costs and complexity are not justified by the Fund\'s current investor pipeline, which is predominantly U.S. domestic institutional. If sagebrush\'s marketing efforts identify more than \$50 million in non-U.S. investor demand, a parallel fund (Option 3, discussed below) may provide a more cost-effective and administratively efficient alternative to a full master-feeder.
292: 
293: We note that this recommendation can be revisited at any time prior to the first close if fundraising dynamics change materially. The LPA for the main Fund should include enabling provisions that would permit the formation of a parallel fund or feeder vehicle without requiring LP consent, as discussed in Section IV.C below.
294: 
295: **[C. Option 3: Parallel Fund for Non-U.S. and/or Tax-Exempt Investors]{.underline}**
296: 
297: **1. Description.** Under this alternative, a separate limited partnership or offshore vehicle (the \"Parallel Fund\") would be formed to invest alongside the main Fund on a pro rata basis in all investments. The Parallel Fund would be structured to address specific tax or regulatory needs of non-U.S. investors or certain U.S. tax-exempt investors --- for example, by functioning as a UBTI blocker at the vehicle level, by avoiding the generation of effectively connected income for non-U.S. investors, or by providing a separately administered vehicle that can independently satisfy ERISA or VCOC requirements.
298: 
299: The General Partner (or an affiliate) would manage both the main Fund and the Parallel Fund. Investments would be allocated between the main Fund and the Parallel Fund on a pro rata basis (based on their respective aggregate commitments), and the economic terms of the Parallel Fund --- including management fee, carried interest, preferred return, and distribution waterfall --- would be identical to those of the main Fund. The economics of the main Fund and the Parallel Fund would be aggregated for purposes of calculating the carried interest waterfall, concentration limits, recycling allowances, and other provisions that reference aggregate capital.
