**[I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY]{.underline}**

The purpose of this memorandum is to present and evaluate the principal fund structuring alternatives available for Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP (\"CLSO Fund I\" or the \"Fund\"), the inaugural opportunistic life-sciences fund to be sponsored by Cobalt Ventures LP (\"Cobalt\" or the \"Sponsor\"). This memorandum analyzes the structural options in light of the Fund\'s anticipated investment strategy, target investor base, economic terms, regulatory requirements, and tax considerations, and provides our recommendations for the preferred fund architecture.

**Recommendation.** Based on our analysis, we recommend that the Fund be organized as a **single-tier Delaware limited partnership** as the primary fund vehicle, supplemented by ancillary structures --- including alternative investment vehicle (\"AIV\") mechanics, a Delaware C-corporation blocker entity, and optional parallel fund or feeder arrangements --- to be deployed on an as-needed basis for specific investor constituencies. This approach provides an institutional-quality structure that is consistent with market practice for life-sciences opportunistic funds at this scale, while preserving maximum flexibility to accommodate the tax, regulatory, and governance requirements of the Fund\'s diverse anticipated investor base.
The key parameters of the Fund are as follows:
> • **Target fund size:** \$750,000,000
> • **First close minimum:** \$250,000,000 (one-third of target)
> • **Target first close:** November 15, 2026
> • **Target final close:** May 15, 2027

This memorandum is being delivered concurrently with a separate **Tax Structuring Memorandum** prepared by Leonard Cross (Specialist Partner, Tax) of Calderwood & Harkness LLP, in coordination with Greystone Tax Advisors LLC (Kenneth Liu, Managing Director), which addresses UBTI and ECI planning, carried interest treatment under IRC §1061, state tax nexus considerations, and blocker entity modeling in greater detail. In addition, the regulatory analysis contained herein has been coordinated with Fielding & O\'Hara PLLC (Brian Liddell, Partner -- Investment Management), which is advising Cobalt on Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (the \"Advisers Act\") compliance, Form ADV preparation, and related regulatory matters.

This memorandum is organized as follows: Section II provides background on the Sponsor, the Fund\'s investment strategy, and the anticipated investor base. Section III summarizes the key fund economic terms that inform structural decisions. Section IV presents our analysis of six structural alternatives and our recommendations for each. Sections V through XI address the recommended entity hierarchy, general partner and management company structural considerations, ERISA and VCOC matters, regulatory considerations, banking and custody arrangements, the service provider framework, and governance structure. Section XII sets forth the proposed formation timeline and next steps. Section XIII provides our concluding recommendations.
**[II. BACKGROUND AND CONTEXT]{.underline}**
**[A. Cobalt Ventures LP --- Sponsor Overview]{.underline}**

Cobalt Ventures LP was founded in 2018 by **Dr. Marcus Yeung** and **Priya Dasgupta** as a dedicated life-sciences investment platform focused on venture-stage and growth-stage biotechnology companies. Over the past eight years, the Sponsor has established a track record of disciplined capital deployment and strong returns across two prior vintage vehicles.

**Dr. Marcus Yeung** holds an MD/PhD from Stanford University and brings eighteen years of life-sciences investing experience to the firm. Prior to founding Cobalt, Dr. Yeung served as a Partner at Prumvane Biosciences, where he led investments in fourteen biotechnology companies, including three that completed initial public offerings and two that were acquired through trade-sale exits. Dr. Yeung\'s deep domain expertise in clinical-stage therapeutics and regulatory pathways is central to the Fund\'s investment strategy.

**Priya Dasgupta** holds an MBA from the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania and brings fifteen years of healthcare investing experience spanning venture capital, growth equity, and public markets. Prior to co-founding Cobalt, Ms. Dasgupta served as Vice President at Ridgeline Health Capital, where she was responsible for sourcing, evaluating, and managing healthcare investments across the capital structure. Ms. Dasgupta leads the firm\'s fundraising and investor relations functions and plays a key role in portfolio company governance.

The Sponsor is headquartered at 3400 Sand Hill Road, Suite 220, Menlo Park, California 94025. Cobalt Ventures LP is organized as a Delaware limited partnership (DE LP File No. 7824931; California Secretary of State File No. 202118412387; EIN: 83-2947561). The firm\'s registered agent in Delaware is Hollowell Technologies, 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801.

Cobalt currently manages approximately **\$420 million** in assets under management across two prior vintage vehicles: Cobalt Ventures Fund A, LP and Cobalt Ventures Fund B, LP. The Sponsor\'s historical strategy has centered on single-fund venture investments in the range of \$5 million to \$25 million, targeting early- and growth-stage biotechnology companies. The launch of CLSO Fund I represents a significant evolution in the Sponsor\'s strategy, as discussed in Section II.B below.

In addition to the co-founders, **Alan Whitford** serves as Partner, Head of Research. Mr. Whitford holds a PhD in Molecular Biology from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and previously served as Chief Scientific Officer at Meridian Therapeutics. He joined Cobalt in 2021 and plays a critical role in scientific diligence, portfolio company monitoring, and strategic advisory. Mr. Whitford will participate in the Fund\'s carried interest allocation as described in Section III.
**[B. Investment Strategy for CLSO Fund I]{.underline}**

CLSO Fund I represents a material step-up in the Sponsor\'s investment strategy, transitioning from venture-stage investments with smaller check sizes to larger, concentrated positions in later-stage life-sciences companies. The Fund\'s investment strategy is defined by the following parameters:
**Sector Focus.** The Fund will target investments in three primary sub-sectors within life sciences:

> \(i\) *Clinical-stage therapeutics* --- companies with drug candidates in Phase II clinical trials or later, where meaningful clinical data exists or is expected within the Fund\'s investment horizon and where regulatory pathways to approval are identifiable;

> \(ii\) *Medical devices* --- companies pursuing FDA 510(k) clearance or Premarket Approval (PMA) pathways, with a preference for devices addressing large, underserved markets with demonstrable clinical utility; and

> \(iii\) *Platform biotechnology* --- companies developing enabling technologies in gene editing, synthetic biology, and AI-enabled drug discovery, where the platform has the potential to generate multiple product candidates or licensing opportunities.

**Geographic Focus.** The Fund will invest primarily in North American companies. Up to twenty-five percent (25%) of aggregate commitments may be deployed in companies headquartered or principally operating in Western Europe and Israel, reflecting the maturity and depth of the life-sciences ecosystems in those regions. This geographic allocation is an investment-level parameter and does not, standing alone, necessitate an offshore fund vehicle, although it may inform AIV considerations for specific transactions (for example, investments requiring a local holding entity in a European jurisdiction).

**Check Size.** The Fund targets initial investments in the range of **\$30,000,000 to \$100,000,000** per portfolio company, with capital reserved for follow-on investments in existing portfolio companies. This represents a significant increase from the Sponsor\'s historical check sizes of \$5 million to \$25 million, consistent with the Fund\'s focus on later-stage, larger-capitalization opportunities.

**Control and Governance.** The Fund will target board seats or contractual governance rights (such as board observer seats, information rights, protective provisions, and consent rights) in one hundred percent (100%) of its portfolio companies. This governance focus is not only central to the Fund\'s value-creation strategy but is also essential for the Fund\'s intended qualification as a \"venture capital operating company\" under the Department of Labor\'s plan asset regulations, as discussed in Section VII below.

**Concentration and Reserves.** The Fund\'s Limited Partnership Agreement (the \"LPA\") will include a concentration limit of fifteen percent (15%) of aggregate commitments per investment, and the Fund will maintain a recycling allowance of fifteen percent (15%) of aggregate commitments to permit redeployment of certain realized proceeds during the investment period.
**[C. Anticipated Investor Base]{.underline}**

The diversity and composition of the Fund\'s anticipated investor base is a primary driver of the structural analysis in this memorandum. Cobalt has identified three prospective anchor or seed investors whose investment parameters, tax status, and regulatory requirements inform the structural flexibility that the Fund must accommodate:
**1. Ironwood Public Employees\' Retirement System (\"Ironwood PERS\")**

Ironwood PERS is a state government pension fund organized under the laws of the State of Oregon, with approximately \$62 billion in assets under management. The anticipated commitment from Ironwood PERS is **\$100,000,000**. The primary contact is Helen Tsao, Director of Private Markets, whose offices are located at 900 Capitol Way NE, Suite 400, Salem, Oregon 97301.
Ironwood PERS\'s investment committee approval is tentatively scheduled for June 2026. Ms. Tsao has communicated the following key requirements for Ironwood PERS\'s investment in the Fund:

> • **Most Favored Nation (\"MFN\") side letter** --- Ironwood PERS expects to receive an MFN provision entitling it to elect any material economic or governance terms granted to other limited partners in side letters, subject to customary carve-outs.
> • **Advisory committee seat** --- Ironwood PERS has specifically requested a seat on the Fund\'s LP Advisory Committee (the \"LPAC\").
> • **Co-investment rights at no fee/no carry** --- Ironwood PERS expects the right to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund on a no-management-fee, no-carried-interest basis.

> • **Annual in-person reporting** --- Ironwood PERS requires that the Sponsor provide an annual in-person report to Ironwood PERS\'s investment staff, either in Salem, Oregon or at a mutually agreed location.

As a state government pension fund, Ironwood PERS is generally exempt from federal income tax and is typically not subject to unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") in most investment scenarios. However, UBTI treatment should be confirmed for debt-financed income scenarios, as discussed in the Tax Structuring Memorandum. Ironwood PERS\'s status as a governmental plan means it is generally not subject to ERISA, although it may be treated as a \"benefit plan investor\" for purposes of the Department of Labor\'s plan asset regulations under certain analyses. The pay-to-play implications of Ironwood PERS\'s status as a state pension fund are discussed in Section VIII.C below.
**2. Northgate Endowment Management LLC (\"Northgate\")**

Northgate Endowment Management LLC is the investment management arm of a major university endowment with approximately \$8.5 billion in assets under management. Northgate is organized as a Delaware limited liability company. The anticipated commitment is **\$50,000,000**. The primary contact is David Park, Senior Portfolio Manager -- Life Sciences Allocation, whose offices are located at 77 Brattle Street, 4th Floor, Cambridge, Massachusetts 02138.
Northgate has communicated the following key requirements:

> • **ERISA-compliant carve-out structure** --- Northgate has requested a structure that ensures compliance with ERISA to the extent applicable. This request likely reflects concerns about the university endowment\'s potential status as a benefit plan investor and the need to ensure that the Fund qualifies for an exception from plan asset treatment (such as the VCOC exception), or alternatively, that Northgate\'s participation is structured through a separate vehicle that independently satisfies ERISA requirements.
> • **Co-investment rights** --- Northgate expects the right to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund.

> • **Annual detailed portfolio analytics** --- Northgate requires comprehensive annual portfolio-level reporting, including detailed valuation methodologies, attribution analysis, and clinical milestone tracking for each portfolio company.

As a university endowment, Northgate is likely tax-exempt under IRC §501(c)(3), which means it may be subject to UBTI on certain categories of investment income, including debt-financed income and income from the conduct of an unrelated trade or business. Northgate may therefore wish to participate in certain investments through a blocker entity, as discussed in Section IV.E below.
**3. Pinnacle Insurance Group, Inc. (\"Pinnacle\")**

Pinnacle Insurance Group, Inc. is a life and annuity insurance company organized under the laws of the State of Connecticut, with a general account of approximately \$28 billion. The anticipated commitment is **\$75,000,000**. The primary contact is Rachel Stein, Senior Vice President -- Alternative Investments, whose offices are located at 500 Asylum Avenue, Hartford, Connecticut 06103.
Pinnacle has communicated the following key requirements:

> • **Insurance regulatory compliance provisions** --- Pinnacle requires that the Fund\'s structure and documentation comply with applicable Connecticut insurance regulations governing permissible investments by insurers, including limitations on asset concentration, investment-grade and below-investment-grade allocations, and derivative instrument restrictions. Pinnacle may also require specific reporting formats for insurance regulatory filings.

> • **blocker entity for certain tax-exempt structures** --- Pinnacle has specifically requested access to a blocker entity for investments generating income that creates adverse tax, reserve, or risk-based capital treatment under Connecticut insurance accounting rules.
> • **Quarterly NAV statements** --- Pinnacle requires quarterly net asset value statements for financial reporting and regulatory compliance purposes.

As a taxable insurance company, Pinnacle\'s tax considerations differ from those of tax-exempt investors, but Pinnacle may nonetheless prefer blocker participation for investments generating debt-financed income, certain operating company income, or income with adverse insurance regulatory accounting characteristics. The blocker entity analysis is addressed in Section IV.E.
**4. Aggregate Anticipated Anchor Commitments and Remaining Capital to Raise**

The aggregate anticipated commitments from the three identified anchor investors total **\$225,000,000** (\$100 million from Ironwood PERS, \$50 million from Northgate, and \$75 million from Pinnacle). The General Partner\'s commitment will be a minimum of two percent (2%) of aggregate commitments, which at the target fund size of \$750 million equals **\$15,000,000**. Accordingly, the remaining capital to be raised from additional institutional investors to reach the target fund size is approximately **\$510,000,000** (\$750 million minus \$225 million minus \$15 million).
**5. Placement Agent**

Cobalt has engaged **sagebrush Capital Partners LLC** (Jonathan Mercer, Managing Director) as the exclusive global placement agent for the Fund. Sagebrush is a registered broker-dealer with the Securities and Exchange Commission (CRD No. 298714). The placement agent engagement is described in further detail in Section X.E.
**6. Structural Implications of Investor Base Diversity**

The diversity of the anticipated investor base --- encompassing a state pension fund, a university endowment, a life and annuity insurance company, and additional institutional investors yet to be identified by sagebrush --- drives the need for significant structural flexibility in the Fund\'s architecture. Each investor category presents distinct tax, regulatory, and governance requirements that the Fund\'s structure must accommodate. The structural analysis in Section IV is informed by these investor-specific considerations.
**[III. KEY FUND ECONOMIC TERMS (SUMMARY)]{.underline}**

The following table summarizes the core economic and governance terms that inform the structural decisions analyzed in this memorandum. These terms are preliminary and will be set forth in detail in the LPA, the first draft of which is targeted for circulation to the principals on May 31, 2026. The terms presented here reflect our discussions with the Cobalt principals to date and are subject to further refinement during the LPA drafting process and in response to investor feedback during the marketing period.

**Carried Interest Allocation Among Principals.** The carried interest entitlement will be allocated among the principals of the General Partner as follows: Dr. Marcus Yeung --- 55%; Priya Dasgupta --- 35%; Alan Whitford --- 10%. The specific mechanics of this allocation, including vesting schedules, forfeiture provisions, and treatment upon departure of a principal, will be governed by the GP LLC Agreement and any ancillary carried interest allocation agreements, the drafting of which is a separate workstream targeted for completion concurrently with the first draft LPA.
**[Fee Waterfall Illustration (at \$750M Target)]{.underline}**
To illustrate the interplay between the management fee, placement fee, and fee offset mechanics, we present the following simplified calculations at the target fund size of \$750 million:
**Annual Management Fee During Investment Period:**
**Aggregate Management Fees Over 5-Year Investment Period:**
**Illustrative Placement Fee (Assuming sagebrush Sources Entire Third-Party Capital):**
> Total third-party commitments (excluding GP commitment): \$750,000,000 − \$15,000,000 = \$735,000,000
> \$735,000,000 × 1.50% = **\$11,025,000** (fully offset against management fee over the Fund\'s life)
**Net Management Fee to CLSO Management After Full Placement Fee Offset:**
> \$75,000,000 − \$11,025,000 = **\$63,975,000** over the five-year investment period
> This represents an effective net management fee rate of approximately 1.71% per annum on aggregate commitments during the investment period, after giving effect to the placement fee offset.

We note that these calculations are illustrative only. The actual placement fee will be based on the commitments actually sourced by sagebrush (as opposed to commitments obtained directly by the Cobalt principals), and the offset will be applied on a pro rata basis over the Fund\'s life in accordance with the offset mechanics to be specified in the LPA. Additionally, transaction and monitoring fees received by the Management Company from portfolio companies will be subject to an eighty percent (80%) offset against the management fee, further reducing the effective management fee borne by limited partners. The post-investment period management fee, calculated on invested capital rather than aggregate commitments, will decline as portfolio companies are realized, resulting in a naturally declining fee base during the harvest period of the Fund.
**[IV. FUND STRUCTURE ALTERNATIVES ANALYSIS]{.underline}**

This Section IV presents our analysis of six structural alternatives for the Fund. For each alternative, we describe the structure, evaluate its advantages and disadvantages in the context of the Fund\'s specific circumstances, and provide our recommendation. We note that these alternatives are not mutually exclusive --- our recommended approach combines elements of several alternatives to achieve the optimal structure for the Fund.
**[A. Option 1: Single-Tier Delaware Limited Partnership (Recommended)]{.underline}**

**1. Description.** Under this alternative, the Fund would be organized as a **single Delaware limited partnership**: Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP. The Fund would be formed under the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act, 6 Del. C. §§17-101 *et seq.* (the \"DRULPA\"), and would be governed by a limited partnership agreement entered into by the General Partner and all limited partners.

**Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company, would serve as the general partner of the Fund. The General Partner would be managed by Dr. Marcus Yeung and Priya Dasgupta as managing members. The General Partner would hold the carried interest entitlement and would be responsible for all fund management and investment decisions, subject to the terms of the LPA.

**Cobalt Life Sciences Management I, LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company, would serve as the management company. The Management Company would employ the Fund\'s investment professionals (including Dr. Yeung, Ms. Dasgupta, Mr. Whitford, and future hires), receive the management fee from the Fund, and bear organizational expenses in excess of the \$1,500,000 cap set forth in the LPA.

Under this single-tier structure, all limited partners would invest directly into the Fund LP. Each limited partner would subscribe for a limited partnership interest in the Fund by executing a subscription agreement and the LPA (or a joinder thereto), and would be subject to capital calls and entitled to distributions in accordance with the terms of the LPA.

This core structure would be supplemented by ancillary mechanisms --- including AIV provisions, a blocker corporation, and parallel fund enabling provisions --- as described in Sections IV.C through IV.F below, to address the specific needs of particular investors or transactions.
**2. Advantages.** The single-tier Delaware limited partnership offers several significant advantages for the Fund:

**Simplicity and Transparency.** A single fund entity reduces administrative complexity, audit costs, and investor confusion. All limited partners participate in a common pool of investments and are subject to a single waterfall calculation, which simplifies reporting, valuation, and distribution mechanics. Institutional investors and their investment consultants are highly familiar with single-tier Delaware LP structures and can efficiently evaluate the Fund\'s terms and governance.

**Market Standard.** The single-tier Delaware LP is the market-standard structure for U.S. domestic life-sciences, venture capital, and growth equity funds at the Fund\'s target size. Based on our experience advising on fund formations in the life-sciences sector, approximately seventy-five to eighty percent of U.S.-sponsored life-sciences funds with target sizes between \$500 million and \$1 billion employ a single-tier Delaware LP as their primary vehicle, supplemented by ancillary structures as needed.

**Straightforward Waterfall Mechanics.** With a single pool of capital, the distribution waterfall --- including the return of capital, preferred return, GP catch-up, and carried interest --- can be calculated across the entire fund on a unified basis. This avoids the complexities of cross-entity waterfall aggregation that arise in master-feeder and multi-vehicle structures.

**Familiarity to Existing Investor Base.** Cobalt\'s existing investor base in Fund A and Fund B is familiar with single-tier Delaware LP structures. Maintaining structural consistency across the Sponsor\'s fund family reduces investor due diligence burden and facilitates re-ups by existing limited partners.

**Lower Formation and Ongoing Costs.** A single-tier structure requires the formation of fewer entities (the Fund LP, the GP LLC, and the Management Company LLC) compared to a master-feeder or multi-vehicle architecture. Ongoing costs --- including audit fees, tax return preparation, fund administration, and legal compliance --- are correspondingly lower.

**Clear Governance Framework.** A single fund entity permits a single LPAC, a single set of LP consent mechanisms, and a single LPA. Governance provisions are applied uniformly to all limited partners, and the GP\'s authority and obligations are defined in a single governing document (subject to side letter modifications for individual investors).
**3. Disadvantages and Limitations**
The single-tier Delaware LP structure has certain limitations that should be acknowledged:

**Tax-Exempt and Non-U.S. Investor Considerations.** A single-tier LP does not inherently address UBTI or ECI concerns for tax-exempt or non-U.S. investors. Income generated by the Fund flows through to all limited partners on a pro rata basis, including categories of income (such as debt-financed income or operating company income) that may give rise to UBTI for tax-exempt investors or ECI for non-U.S. investors. This limitation is addressed through the blocker corporation (Section IV.E) and AIV mechanics (Section IV.D) described below.

**Non-U.S. Investor Demand.** If significant non-U.S. investor demand materializes during the fundraising process, a single-tier Delaware LP may not be the optimal vehicle for all investor constituencies. Non-U.S. investors may prefer to invest through an offshore vehicle to avoid potential U.S. tax filing obligations and withholding tax complexities. This concern is addressed through the parallel fund option described in Section IV.C.

**Insurance Regulatory Considerations.** Pinnacle Insurance Group, as a Connecticut-domiciled life and annuity insurer, may require blocker entity participation for certain investments that generate income with adverse insurance regulatory accounting characteristics. A single-tier LP does not, standing alone, address these concerns, but the blocker mechanism described in Section IV.E provides the necessary accommodation.

**4. Recommendation. The single-tier Delaware limited partnership is our recommended primary fund vehicle.** Based on the Fund\'s target investor base (which is predominantly U.S. institutional), the Fund\'s target size (\$750 million), the Fund\'s investment strategy (clinical-stage therapeutics, medical devices, and platform biotechnology), and prevailing market practice for life-sciences opportunistic funds, the single-tier Delaware LP provides the optimal combination of simplicity, cost-efficiency, and institutional acceptability.

The limitations identified above --- primarily relating to UBTI/ECI planning for tax-sensitive investors and potential non-U.S. investor demand --- are effectively addressed through the ancillary structures described in Sections IV.C through IV.E below. These ancillary structures are additive to the core single-tier architecture and do not require any modification to the primary fund vehicle.
**[B. Option 2: Dual Master-Feeder Structure]{.underline}**

**1. Description.** Under a dual master-feeder structure, investment activity would be conducted through a **master fund** --- organized either as a Delaware limited partnership or as an offshore entity (such as a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership) --- that receives capital through one or more **feeder funds**. The typical architecture involves two feeder vehicles:

> \(a\) A *domestic feeder* --- organized as a Delaware limited partnership --- through which U.S. taxable investors subscribe. The domestic feeder invests substantially all of its assets into the master fund.

> \(b\) An *offshore feeder* --- organized as a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership, a Cayman Islands exempted company, or a similar offshore entity --- through which non-U.S. investors and U.S. tax-exempt investors subscribe. The offshore feeder similarly invests substantially all of its assets into the master fund. The offshore feeder may function as a blocker for UBTI and ECI purposes, depending on its entity classification for U.S. tax purposes.

Each feeder is a standalone entity with its own governing documents, although the economic terms (management fee, carried interest, preferred return, and distribution waterfall) are designed to replicate the master fund\'s terms. The general partner (or an affiliate) manages all entities, and investment decisions are made at the master fund level.
**2. Advantages.** The master-feeder structure offers certain advantages:

**Clean Investor Segregation.** The master-feeder architecture cleanly separates U.S. taxable, U.S. tax-exempt, and non-U.S. investor constituencies into distinct legal entities, each of which can be structured to optimize the tax treatment of its particular investor class.

**Offshore blocker Functionality.** An offshore feeder organized as an entity classified as a corporation for U.S. tax purposes (such as a Cayman Islands exempted company that does not elect partnership treatment) can serve as a blocker for UBTI and ECI, shielding tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors from flow-through of undesirable categories of income.

**Established Architecture.** The master-feeder structure is well-established in hedge fund and larger private equity fund contexts, and sophisticated institutional investors are familiar with its mechanics.
**3. Disadvantages.** Despite its structural elegance, the master-feeder architecture presents significant disadvantages for the Fund:

**Incremental Formation and Ongoing Costs.** A full master-feeder requires the formation and maintenance of multiple entities across multiple jurisdictions. Offshore legal counsel (Cayman Islands or other offshore jurisdiction) must be engaged for the formation and ongoing compliance of the offshore feeder. Registration fees, annual government fees, and economic substance requirements in the offshore jurisdiction add to the cost burden. Dual (or triple) audit engagements, dual fund administration, and multiple sets of tax returns significantly increase ongoing operating costs.

**Disproportionate Complexity.** The complexity of a master-feeder structure is disproportionate to the Fund\'s anticipated investor base. The three identified anchor investors --- Ironwood PERS, Northgate, and Pinnacle --- are all U.S. domestic institutional investors. No significant non-U.S. fundraising target has been identified to date. While sagebrush may source non-U.S. capital during the marketing process, the current pipeline does not support the formation costs and ongoing administrative burden of a full master-feeder at this time.

**Geographic Investment Allocation Is Not Determinative.** The Fund\'s investment strategy permits up to twenty-five percent of aggregate commitments to be deployed in Western Europe and Israel. This geographic allocation relates to the location of portfolio companies --- not the domicile of investors --- and does not, standing alone, require an offshore fund vehicle.

**Market Practice.** In our experience, first-time opportunistic life-sciences funds at the \$750 million target size generally do not employ a master-feeder structure unless substantial non-U.S. limited partner demand (typically in excess of \$100 million to \$150 million) exists at the time of fund formation or is reasonably anticipated.

**4. Recommendation. The dual master-feeder structure is not recommended at this time.** The structure\'s incremental costs and complexity are not justified by the Fund\'s current investor pipeline, which is predominantly U.S. domestic institutional. If sagebrush\'s marketing efforts identify more than \$50 million in non-U.S. investor demand, a parallel fund (Option 3, discussed below) may provide a more cost-effective and administratively efficient alternative to a full master-feeder.

We note that this recommendation can be revisited at any time prior to the first close if fundraising dynamics change materially. The LPA for the main Fund should include enabling provisions that would permit the formation of a parallel fund or feeder vehicle without requiring LP consent, as discussed in Section IV.C below.
**[C. Option 3: Parallel Fund for Non-U.S. and/or Tax-Exempt Investors]{.underline}**

**1. Description.** Under this alternative, a separate limited partnership or offshore vehicle (the \"Parallel Fund\") would be formed to invest alongside the main Fund on a pro rata basis in all investments. The Parallel Fund would be structured to address specific tax or regulatory needs of non-U.S. investors or certain U.S. tax-exempt investors --- for example, by functioning as a UBTI blocker at the vehicle level, by avoiding the generation of effectively connected income for non-U.S. investors, or by providing a separately administered vehicle that can independently satisfy ERISA or VCOC requirements.

The General Partner (or an affiliate) would manage both the main Fund and the Parallel Fund. Investments would be allocated between the main Fund and the Parallel Fund on a pro rata basis (based on their respective aggregate commitments), and the economic terms of the Parallel Fund --- including management fee, carried interest, preferred return, and distribution waterfall --- would be identical to those of the main Fund. The economics of the main Fund and the Parallel Fund would be aggregated for purposes of calculating the carried interest waterfall, concentration limits, recycling allowances, and other provisions that reference aggregate capital.

43: **3.1 Key-Person Event Analysis**
44: 
45: C&H will undertake a comprehensive analysis of the mechanics and consequences of Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, including the following:
46: 
47: > \(a\) **Section 8.04(a) --- Definition of \"Key Person.\"** C&H will confirm the scope of the \"Key Person\" designation under the A&R LPA, which identifies Marcus J. Whitmore as the sole designated Key Person. C&H will analyze the definition for purposes of establishing the factual predicate for the Key Person Event and for advising on the requirements for designating any Successor Key Person(s) (as described in Section 3.3 below).
48: >
49: > \(b\) **Section 8.04(b) --- Trigger Conditions.** C&H will analyze the trigger conditions set forth in Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA in light of the facts surrounding Mr. Whitmore\'s incapacitation. Specifically, Section 8.04(b) provides that a Key Person Event is deemed to occur when the Key Person becomes unable, whether by reason of death, disability, incapacity, departure, or otherwise, to devote substantially all of his professional time and attention to the affairs of the Fund for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days. Based on the information provided to C&H, Mr. Whitmore has been continuously incapacitated since June 3, 2024, and the seven-consecutive-calendar-day threshold was met as of June 10, 2024. C&H will prepare a memorandum confirming the legal basis for this determination.
50: >
51: > \(c\) **Section 8.04(c) --- Consequences of the Key Person Event.** C&H will advise the Clients regarding the full range of consequences triggered by the occurrence of the Key Person Event under Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, which include the following:
52: >
53: > \(i\) *Immediate Suspension of the Investment Period.* The Investment Period (as defined in Section 1.01 of the A&R LPA) is automatically suspended upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event. During such suspension, the General Partner may not make new portfolio investments on behalf of the Fund, except as provided in clause (ii) below.
54: >
55: > \(ii\) *Follow-On Investment Cap.* Notwithstanding the suspension of the Investment Period, the General Partner retains limited authority to make follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions in an aggregate amount not to exceed one percent (1%) of the Fund\'s assets under management as of the date of the Key Person Event. Based on the Fund\'s most recently reported AUM of approximately \$2.87 billion, the follow-on investment cap is \$28.7 million.
56: >
57: > \(iii\) *LP Notification Requirement.* The General Partner is required to provide written notice to all limited partners of the occurrence of the Key Person Event within five (5) business days of the date on which the Key Person Event is deemed to have occurred. Given that the Key Person Event is deemed to have occurred on June 10, 2024, the contractual deadline for delivery of such notice is June 17, 2024.
58: >
59: > \(iv\) *Commencement of the 90-Calendar-Day Cure Period.* Upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event, a cure period of ninety (90) calendar days (the \"Cure Period\") commences, during which the General Partner may propose one or more Successor Key Persons for approval by the limited partners. The Cure Period with respect to the current Key Person Event will expire on September 8, 2024.
60: >
61: > \(v\) *LP Consent Threshold.* Approval of any proposed Successor Key Person(s) requires the affirmative written consent of limited partners holding at least sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of the aggregate capital commitments of all limited partners of the Fund, excluding for this purpose any co-investment by the General Partner. C&H will advise on the calculation of this threshold based on the most current LP commitment schedule maintained by the Fund\'s administrator.
62: >
63: > \(d\) **Consequences of Failure to Cure.** C&H will further analyze the consequences under Section 8.04(d) of the A&R LPA if no cure is achieved within the Cure Period, including the limited partners\' right to elect, by the same 66⅔% consent threshold described above, either (x) to extend the Cure Period for one or more additional periods or (y) to direct the General Partner to commence an orderly wind-down of the Fund\'s portfolio. C&H will advise the Clients on the mechanics, timing, and fiduciary considerations associated with each of these alternatives.
64: >
65: > \(e\) **Delaware Law Fiduciary Duty Analysis.** C&H will advise the Clients regarding the fiduciary duties owed by DCM, as General Partner, to the limited partners of the Fund during the Key Person Event and throughout the consent solicitation process, as a matter of Delaware law. This analysis will address, among other things, the duty of care and the contractual modification of fiduciary duties under the A&R LPA, including the exculpation and indemnification provisions set forth in Article XII thereof.

Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, C&H does not represent Mr. Whitmore individually, nor does C&H represent any member of the IAC in his, her, or its individual or fiduciary capacity. Each such person and entity is encouraged to seek independent legal counsel to the extent such person or entity deems it necessary or appropriate.

Elaine R. Sato, in her capacity as Deputy Chief Investment Officer and Managing Member (holding a ten percent (10%) membership interest) of DCM, will serve as the primary point of contact for the Clients in connection with this engagement. All communications from C&H regarding this engagement will be directed to Ms. Sato unless otherwise instructed in writing by Ms. Sato. C&H will take direction from Ms. Sato with respect to all matters within the scope of this engagement, subject to the Firm\'s professional obligations.
**[3. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**

C&H\'s representation of the Clients will encompass the following workstreams in connection with the Key Person Event triggered under Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA. Each workstream is described in further detail below.
**3.1 Key-Person Event Analysis**
C&H will undertake a comprehensive analysis of the mechanics and consequences of Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, including the following:

> \(a\) **Section 8.04(a) --- Definition of \"Key Person.\"** C&H will confirm the scope of the \"Key Person\" designation under the A&R LPA, which identifies Marcus J. Whitmore as the sole designated Key Person. C&H will analyze the definition for purposes of establishing the factual predicate for the Key Person Event and for advising on the requirements for designating any Successor Key Person(s) (as described in Section 3.3 below).

> \(b\) **Section 8.04(b) --- Trigger Conditions.** C&H will analyze the trigger conditions set forth in Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA in light of the facts surrounding Mr. Whitmore\'s incapacitation. Specifically, Section 8.04(b) provides that a Key Person Event is deemed to occur when the Key Person becomes unable, whether by reason of death, disability, incapacity, departure, or otherwise, to devote substantially all of his professional time and attention to the affairs of the Fund for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days. Based on the information provided to C&H, Mr. Whitmore has been continuously incapacitated since June 3, 2024, and the seven-consecutive-calendar-day threshold was met as of June 10, 2024. C&H will prepare a memorandum confirming the legal basis for this determination.

> \(c\) **Section 8.04(c) --- Consequences of the Key Person Event.** C&H will advise the Clients regarding the full range of consequences triggered by the occurrence of the Key Person Event under Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, which include the following:

> \(i\) *Immediate Suspension of the Investment Period.* The Investment Period (as defined in Section 1.01 of the A&R LPA) is automatically suspended upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event. During such suspension, the General Partner may not make new portfolio investments on behalf of the Fund, except as provided in clause (ii) below.

> \(ii\) *Follow-On Investment Cap.* Notwithstanding the suspension of the Investment Period, the General Partner retains limited authority to make follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions in an aggregate amount not to exceed one percent (1%) of the Fund\'s assets under management as of the date of the Key Person Event. Based on the Fund\'s most recently reported AUM of approximately \$2.87 billion, the follow-on investment cap is \$28.7 million.

> \(iii\) *LP Notification Requirement.* The General Partner is required to provide written notice to all limited partners of the occurrence of the Key Person Event within five (5) business days of the date on which the Key Person Event is deemed to have occurred. Given that the Key Person Event is deemed to have occurred on June 10, 2024, the contractual deadline for delivery of such notice is June 17, 2024.

> \(iv\) *Commencement of the 90-Calendar-Day Cure Period.* Upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event, a cure period of ninety (90) calendar days (the \"Cure Period\") commences, during which the General Partner may propose one or more Successor Key Persons for approval by the limited partners. The Cure Period with respect to the current Key Person Event will expire on September 8, 2024.

> \(v\) *LP Consent Threshold.* Approval of any proposed Successor Key Person(s) requires the affirmative written consent of limited partners holding at least sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of the aggregate capital commitments of all limited partners of the Fund, excluding for this purpose any co-investment by the General Partner. C&H will advise on the calculation of this threshold based on the most current LP commitment schedule maintained by the Fund\'s administrator.

> \(d\) **Consequences of Failure to Cure.** C&H will further analyze the consequences under Section 8.04(d) of the A&R LPA if no cure is achieved within the Cure Period, including the limited partners\' right to elect, by the same 66⅔% consent threshold described above, either (x) to extend the Cure Period for one or more additional periods or (y) to direct the General Partner to commence an orderly wind-down of the Fund\'s portfolio. C&H will advise the Clients on the mechanics, timing, and fiduciary considerations associated with each of these alternatives.

> \(e\) **Delaware Law Fiduciary Duty Analysis.** C&H will advise the Clients regarding the fiduciary duties owed by DCM, as General Partner, to the limited partners of the Fund during the Key Person Event and throughout the consent solicitation process, as a matter of Delaware law. This analysis will address, among other things, the duty of care and the contractual modification of fiduciary duties under the A&R LPA, including the exculpation and indemnification provisions set forth in Article XII thereof.
**3.2 LP Notification**

C&H will draft the formal written notice to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund disclosing the occurrence of the Key Person Event in compliance with Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA (the \"Key Person Notice\"). The Key Person Notice will describe the factual basis for the Key Person Event, the contractual consequences thereof, the commencement and expected expiration date of the Cure Period, and the process by which the General Partner intends to propose Successor Key Person(s) for approval by the limited partners.

C&H will coordinate with Pinnacle Fund Services (Cayman) Ltd. (the \"Administrator\"), the Fund\'s third-party administrator, regarding the maintenance and accuracy of LP contact information, the appropriate method of delivery (including any notice provisions specified in the A&R LPA or in individual side letters), and the mechanics of distributing the Key Person Notice to all limited partners within the contractual timeframe. C&H will confirm with the Administrator that notice is delivered by a method that satisfies the delivery requirements of Section 15.01 of the A&R LPA.

It is critical that the Key Person Notice be delivered within the five (5) business-day contractual notification deadline, which, as noted above, falls on June 17, 2024. C&H will prioritize this workstream accordingly and will endeavor to deliver a draft of the Key Person Notice to Ms. Sato for review no later than June 13, 2024.
**3.3 Successor Governance Framework**

C&H will advise the Clients regarding the identification and evaluation of proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the development of a recommended successor governance framework for the Fund. This advisory work may encompass the following elements:

> \(a\) **Designation of Successor Key Person(s).** C&H will advise on the criteria and process for designating one or more Successor Key Persons under the A&R LPA, including the qualifications, investment experience, and operational capabilities that limited partners are likely to consider in evaluating any proposed successor. C&H will assist in preparing biographical and professional materials for inclusion in the consent solicitation package.

> \(b\) **Establishment of an Investment Committee.** In the event that the Clients determine that the successor governance framework should include the establishment of a formal Investment Committee or similar collective governance body (in lieu of, or in addition to, a sole Key Person designation), C&H will advise on the structure, composition, authority, and operating procedures of such body, and will prepare the necessary amendments to the A&R LPA to implement such structure.

> \(c\) **Modifications to Key-Person Clause Mechanics.** C&H will advise on potential modifications to the key-person provisions of Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, which may include revised replacement periods, modified trigger events (including, for example, a threshold requiring the departure or incapacitation of more than one designated Key Person before a Key Person Event is deemed to occur), and other structural changes to reduce single-person dependency risk.

> \(d\) **Carried Interest Reallocation.** C&H will advise the Clients on the legal and governance considerations associated with any proposed reallocation of carried interest among GP personnel in connection with the transition, including the interplay between the carried interest provisions of the A&R LPA and the operating agreement of DCM.

> \(e\) **Designation of Senior Advisor or Emeritus Role.** To the extent the Clients determine it appropriate, C&H will advise on the creation of a Senior Advisor or emeritus role for Mr. Whitmore, including the scope of any continuing economic interest, advisory responsibilities, and governance rights that may be associated with such role.

> \(f\) **Fiduciary Duty Obligations.** Throughout the development of the successor governance framework, C&H will advise the Clients regarding their fiduciary duty obligations under applicable Delaware law, including the duty to act in good faith and in the best interests of the limited partners in proposing any successor governance arrangements.
**3.4 LPA Amendment Drafting**

C&H will prepare one or more amendments to the A&R LPA (each, an \"LPA Amendment\") to implement the successor governance framework developed pursuant to Section 3.3 above. It is anticipated that the LPA Amendments will include modifications to the following provisions of the A&R LPA, among others:
> \(a\) Section 8.04 (Key Person), to reflect the designation of Successor Key Person(s) and any revised key-person clause mechanics;

> \(b\) Section 9.02 (Investor Advisory Committee), to the extent any changes to the composition, authority, or procedures of the IAC are contemplated in connection with the successor governance framework;
> \(c\) Section 14.01 (Amendments), to the extent any changes to the amendment mechanics are necessary or advisable; and
> \(d\) Related schedules and exhibits, including the schedule of Key Persons attached to the A&R LPA.

All LPA Amendments will be subject to the consent requirements set forth in Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA, which generally requires the written consent of the General Partner and limited partners holding at least 66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments (excluding GP co-investment) for amendments to certain specified provisions, including Section 8.04. C&H will advise the Clients regarding the applicable consent thresholds for each proposed amendment.
**3.5 LP Consent Solicitation**

C&H will advise on and coordinate the consent solicitation process necessary to obtain limited partner approval of the proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the related LPA Amendments. This workstream will include the following:

> \(a\) **Successor Key Person Proposal Letter.** C&H will draft a detailed letter to all limited partners setting forth the proposed Successor Key Person(s), the rationale for the proposed designation(s), the terms of the proposed successor governance framework, and a summary of the proposed LPA Amendments (the \"Proposal Letter\"). The Proposal Letter will be designed to provide limited partners with all information reasonably necessary to make an informed decision regarding the proposed successor arrangements.

> \(b\) **Form of LP Written Consent.** C&H will prepare a Form of LP Written Consent (the \"Consent Form\") for execution by limited partners approving the proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the related LPA Amendments. The Consent Form will be structured to comply with the requirements of Section 14.01 and Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA.

> \(c\) **Coordination of Consent Solicitation Process.** C&H will coordinate the distribution of the Proposal Letter and Consent Form to all forty-seven (47) limited partners, working in conjunction with the Administrator to ensure accurate and timely delivery. C&H will manage the consent solicitation timeline with a view toward obtaining the requisite LP consents prior to the expiration of the Cure Period on September 8, 2024.

> \(d\) **Tabulation and Certification.** C&H will tabulate the LP consents received and prepare a closing certificate confirming that the requisite consent threshold (66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments, excluding GP co-investment) has been satisfied and that the LPA Amendments are effective as of the date specified therein (the \"Closing Certificate\").

> \(e\) **Engagement with IAC Counsel.** C&H will engage with counsel to the Investor Advisory Committee, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, as necessary and appropriate regarding the IAC\'s review of and comments on the proposed Successor Key Person(s), the successor governance framework, and the LPA Amendments. C&H will coordinate with the Clients regarding any modifications to the proposed arrangements that may be requested by the IAC or its counsel.
**[4. Limitations on Scope]{.underline}**
The Clients should be aware of the following limitations on the scope of C&H\'s engagement:

> \(a\) **Cayman Islands Law.** C&H does not provide legal advice regarding the laws of the Cayman Islands. The Clients should consult separately with qualified Cayman Islands counsel regarding any Cayman Islands regulatory, partnership law, or other legal matters that may arise in connection with the Key Person Event or the transactions contemplated by this engagement, including any filings or notifications required under Cayman Islands law in connection with changes to the Fund\'s governance structure.

> \(b\) **Tax Advice.** C&H is not engaged to provide tax advice in connection with this engagement. The Clients should consult their own tax advisors regarding the U.S. federal, state, local, and non-U.S. tax implications of any carried interest reallocation, structural changes to the Fund or DCM, or other transactions contemplated by this engagement.

> \(c\) **Investment Advice.** C&H is not engaged to provide investment advice or to evaluate the investment merits of any portfolio positions held by the Fund. The Clients acknowledge that any decisions regarding the management, disposition, or retention of portfolio positions during the suspension of the Investment Period or otherwise are solely the responsibility of the Clients and their investment professionals.

> \(d\) **Third-Party Service Providers.** C&H does not represent the Fund\'s independent auditor (Graystone & Whitfield LLP), the Fund\'s prime broker (Halcyon Securities International Ltd.), the Administrator, or any other third-party service provider to the Fund or DCM. Each such service provider is represented by its own counsel, and the Clients should not assume that C&H\'s representation extends to any of those parties.

> \(e\) **Litigation and Regulatory Matters.** This engagement does not extend to any litigation, arbitration, regulatory investigation, enforcement action, or other adversarial or contested proceeding, whether existing or threatened, unless separately agreed in writing between C&H and the Clients. In the event any such matter arises during the course of this engagement, C&H will promptly advise the Clients and, if requested, discuss the terms of a separate engagement to address such matter.
**[5. Engagement Team]{.underline}**
C&H has assigned the following professionals to this engagement:
**Name**                **Role**                **Title**
Graham Sutherland       Responsible Partner     Partner, Funds & Asset Management
Pamela Cross            Billing Partner         Partner, Funds & Asset Management
Stephen Adler           Lead Associate          Associate, Funds & Asset Management
Theresa Kim             Working Associate       Associate, Funds & Asset Management

Graham Sutherland will serve as the responsible partner overseeing all legal advice rendered in connection with this engagement. Mr. Sutherland will be the Clients\' primary legal point of contact for substantive matters, and all material legal memoranda, draft documents, and advice letters will be reviewed and approved by Mr. Sutherland prior to delivery to the Clients.

Pamela Cross will serve as the billing partner responsible for fee arrangements, invoicing, and all financial aspects of the engagement. Any questions regarding billing, fees, or disbursements should be directed to Ms. Cross.

Stephen Adler will serve as the lead associate responsible for the day-to-day execution of the engagement workstreams described in Section 3 above, under the supervision of Mr. Sutherland. Theresa Kim will support Mr. Adler on all workstreams, with particular focus on document drafting and consent solicitation logistics.

C&H may assign additional attorneys, paralegals, or other professionals to this engagement as reasonably necessary to ensure the timely and effective completion of the workstreams described herein. C&H will provide prior notice to Ms. Sato before assigning any additional professionals whose time will be billed to the Clients.
**[6. Fee Arrangement]{.underline}**
**6.1 Hourly Rates**
Services rendered by C&H attorneys in connection with this engagement will be billed on an hourly basis at the following standard rates:
> • **Partners:** \$1,650 per hour
> • **Associates:** \$895 per hour

The foregoing rates are effective as of the date of this engagement letter and are subject to annual adjustment in accordance with C&H\'s standard rate-setting process. C&H will provide the Clients with at least thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of any rate increase. Paralegal and other support staff time, if any, will be billed at rates communicated to the Clients in advance.
**6.2 Fee Cap**

Total professional fees for the engagement shall not exceed Three Hundred Eighty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$385,000) (the \"Fee Cap\") without the prior written consent of the Clients. The Fee Cap encompasses all professional fees of C&H attorneys assigned to this engagement for the workstreams described in Section 3 above. In the event C&H anticipates that total fees may approach or exceed the Fee Cap, C&H will promptly notify the Clients and discuss whether an adjustment to the Fee Cap is warranted. No fees in excess of the Fee Cap will be billed to the Clients absent prior written authorization from Ms. Sato or another authorized representative of DCM. The Fee Cap does not include out-of-pocket disbursements, which are addressed separately in Section 6.3 below.
**6.3 Disbursements and Expenses**

The Clients will reimburse C&H for reasonable out-of-pocket disbursements incurred in connection with this engagement, including, without limitation, costs of document production, photocopying, overnight courier and delivery charges, filing fees, database and research charges, and travel expenses (including airfare, lodging, and ground transportation), if any. All disbursements will be billed at cost, without markup. Disbursements are not subject to the Fee Cap set forth in Section 6.2. C&H will exercise reasonable judgment in incurring disbursements and will obtain the Clients\' prior approval before incurring any single disbursement in excess of Five Thousand Dollars (\$5,000).
**6.4 Billing and Payment**

C&H will issue monthly invoices to DCM at the address set forth in Section 2 above (or to such other address as DCM may designate in writing). Each invoice will include a reasonably detailed description of the services rendered and disbursements incurred during the applicable billing period. Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. C&H reserves the right to suspend the performance of services in the event of non-payment of any invoice for a period exceeding sixty (60) days following the date of such invoice, provided that C&H shall provide at least ten (10) days\' prior written notice to the Clients before exercising such right.
**[7. Governing Law]{.underline}**

This engagement letter and the terms and conditions set forth herein shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflicts of law principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

For the avoidance of doubt, the A&R LPA is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, and C&H\'s analysis and advice rendered under this engagement with respect to the interpretation and enforcement of the provisions of the A&R LPA, including Section 8.04 and the fiduciary duties of the General Partner, will apply the substantive law of the State of Delaware. Nothing in this Section 7 is intended to alter the governing law of the A&R LPA or any other agreement to which the Clients are a party.
**[8. Conflicts of Interest]{.underline}**

C&H has conducted a conflicts check in accordance with the Firm\'s standard procedures and the applicable rules of professional conduct. Based on the results of that check, C&H confirms that it is not aware of any current conflict of interest that would preclude the Firm from undertaking this engagement on behalf of the Clients.

C&H confirms that it does not currently represent any limited partner of the Fund, any member of the Investor Advisory Committee, or the IAC\'s counsel, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, in any matter related to the Fund, DCM, or the Key Person Event. C&H may represent other clients in matters unrelated to this engagement, and the Clients acknowledge that such representations do not constitute a conflict of interest for purposes of this engagement.

In the event that a conflict of interest arises during the course of this engagement, C&H will promptly notify the Clients and take appropriate steps in accordance with the applicable rules of professional conduct governing attorneys admitted to practice in the State of New York, including, where appropriate, seeking a waiver of the conflict or, if necessary, withdrawing from the engagement.
**[9. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

C&H will maintain the confidentiality of all information received from or on behalf of the Clients in connection with this engagement, consistent with the Firm\'s professional responsibility obligations under the applicable rules of professional conduct and the protections afforded by the attorney-client privilege and the work product doctrine. C&H will implement reasonable safeguards to protect the confidentiality of such information within the Firm.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, C&H may disclose confidential information: (a) as required by applicable law, regulation, or court order; (b) as authorized or directed by the Clients; or (c) to the extent reasonably necessary in connection with the performance of the services described in this engagement letter, including, without limitation, in communications with the Administrator, counsel to the IAC, or other third parties as directed by the Clients.
**[10. Document Retention]{.underline}**

Upon completion of the engagement, C&H will retain client files (including electronic files) in accordance with the Firm\'s document retention policy, which currently provides for retention of engagement files for a period of ten (10) years from the date of engagement closure. Following the expiration of such retention period, C&H may destroy or dispose of the engagement files without further notice to or consent from the Clients, unless the Clients have previously requested the return of such files.

Original documents provided by the Clients to C&H during the course of this engagement will be returned to the Clients upon written request. C&H may retain copies of such original documents in accordance with the retention policy described above.
**[11. Termination]{.underline}**

Either party may terminate this engagement at any time upon thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to the other party. In the event of termination by either party, the Clients will remain responsible for payment of all fees and disbursements incurred by C&H through the effective date of termination, subject to the Fee Cap set forth in Section 6.2.

Upon termination, C&H will cooperate in the orderly transition of the matter to successor counsel designated by the Clients, including the prompt delivery of all work product, client files, and other materials in C&H\'s possession that are necessary for successor counsel to continue the representation. C&H\'s obligation to assist in the orderly transition of the matter shall survive the termination of this engagement.
**[12. Acceptance]{.underline}**

We would appreciate it if you would confirm the Clients\' acceptance of the terms set forth in this engagement letter by signing and returning a copy of this letter to the undersigned at your earliest convenience. This engagement shall be deemed to have commenced as of June 11, 2024, upon your execution of this letter. If you have any questions regarding the terms of this engagement, please do not hesitate to contact either of the undersigned.
We look forward to working with you and the Driftwood team on this important matter.
Very truly yours,
**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP**

33: **[I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY]{.underline}**
34: 
35: Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") was engaged on June 11, 2024 by Driftwood Capital Management LLC (\"DCM\"), in its capacity as General Partner of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. (\"DARF\" or the \"Fund\"), to advise on the legal implications of, and governance response to, a key-person event triggered by the sudden medical incapacitation of Marcus J. Whitmore, the Fund\'s founder, Chief Investment Officer, and sole designated Key Person under Section 8.04 of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership, dated as of March 15, 2017 (the \"A&R LPA\"). The engagement arose under circumstances requiring immediate attention: Whitmore suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke on June 3, 2024, and the contractual Key Person Event was deemed triggered on June 10, 2024 upon expiration of the seven-consecutive-calendar-day threshold set forth in Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA, thereby suspending the Fund\'s Investment Period and initiating a 90-calendar-day Cure Period expiring September 8, 2024.

37: The scope of the engagement, as set forth in the engagement letter dated June 11, 2024, encompassed the following principal workstreams: (i) comprehensive analysis of Section 8.04 key-person clause mechanics and the contractual consequences flowing from the triggering event; (ii) preparation and review of the limited partner notification required under Section 8.04(c); (iii) development and recommendation of a successor governance framework, including the designation of successor Key Persons and the establishment of an Investment Committee; (iv) drafting and negotiation of the First Amendment to the A&R LPA (the \"First Amendment\") to implement the successor governance framework; and (v) solicitation and tabulation of limited partner consents as required under the A&R LPA for approval of the successor Key Persons and the related amendments.

39: All engagement objectives were achieved within the contractual Cure Period and in compliance with all applicable provisions of the A&R LPA, Delaware law, and Cayman Islands regulatory requirements. Thirty-eight (38) of the Fund\'s forty-seven (47) limited partners delivered written consents representing \$2,412.8 million of LP capital commitments, or approximately 86.2% of voting LP commitments --- well in excess of the 66⅔% supermajority threshold required under Section 8.04(c). The First Amendment to the A&R LPA became effective on August 26, 2024, designating Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons, establishing a three-member Investment Committee, transitioning Marcus J. Whitmore to a Senior Advisor role without governance authority, and implementing a revised carried interest allocation among the principals of DCM. The Cure Period deadline of September 8, 2024 was thereby mooted by the successful completion of the successor governance process thirteen (13) calendar days in advance.
