97: **[III. ENGAGEMENT TEAM AND FEE ARRANGEMENT]{.underline}**
98: 
99: **A. Calderwood & Harkness LLP Engagement Team**
100: 
101: The following attorneys of Calderwood & Harkness LLP\'s Funds & Asset Management practice group were assigned to this matter and performed substantive work during the engagement:
102: 
103:   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
104:   **Name**                **Role**                **Position**
105:   ----------------------- ----------------------- -------------------------------------
106:   Graham Sutherland       Responsible Partner     Partner, Funds & Asset Management
107: 
108:   Pamela Cross            Billing Partner         Partner, Funds & Asset Management
109: 
110:   Stephen Adler           Lead Associate          Associate, Funds & Asset Management
111: 
112:   Theresa Kim             Working Associate       Associate, Funds & Asset Management
113:   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
114: 
115: Graham Sutherland served as the Responsible Partner for the engagement and maintained oversight of all legal analysis, strategic recommendations, client communications, and substantive deliverables throughout the matter. Mr. Sutherland personally led the negotiation with Wexford Crane & Albright LLP on behalf of the Investor Advisory Committee and participated in the July 29, 2024 IAC meeting. Pamela Cross served as the Billing Partner and was responsible for all billing and engagement economics matters. Stephen Adler served as the Lead Associate and was principally responsible for the preparation of all memoranda, the drafting of the First Amendment, the LP consent solicitation process, and the tabulation of LP consents. Theresa Kim served as the Working Associate and supported all research, drafting, and document management functions throughout the engagement.
116: 
117: **B. Fee Arrangement**
118: 
119: The Firm\'s engagement was subject to an hourly billing arrangement, with an aggregate fee cap of \$385,000 for the entirety of the engagement. The applicable billing rates were as follows:
120: 
121: > • Partner rate: \$1,650 per hour
122: >
123: > • Associate rate: \$895 per hour
124: 
125: The billing partner for the engagement was Pamela Cross. The engagement letter was dated June 11, 2024, and was addressed to Elaine R. Sato, in her capacity as Deputy Chief Investment Officer of DCM. The engagement letter was countersigned by Ms. Sato on behalf of DCM and returned to the Firm on the same date. All fees incurred during the engagement were within the aggregate fee cap.
126: 
127: **C. Counterparty Counsel**
128: 
129: The Investor Advisory Committee of the Fund retained independent legal counsel in connection with its review and negotiation of the successor governance framework and the First Amendment. The details of counterparty counsel are as follows:
130: 
131: **Firm:** Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, 51 West 52nd Street, 40th Floor, New York, NY 10019
132: 
133: **Lead Partner:** Helen M. Calloway, Partner, Investment Funds Group
134: 
135: **Senior Associate:** David Pineda, Senior Associate, Investment Funds Group
136: 
137: Wexford Crane & Albright LLP (\"WCA\") represented the interests of the Investor Advisory Committee throughout the review and negotiation period described in Section V.C below. WCA\'s representation was limited to the IAC and did not extend to any individual limited partner or to the limited partner body as a whole. The costs of WCA\'s representation were borne by the Fund in accordance with the IAC expense reimbursement provisions set forth in Section 9.04 of the A&R LPA.
138: 
139: **[IV. BACKGROUND: THE KEY-PERSON EVENT]{.underline}**
140: 
141: **A. Marcus J. Whitmore --- Profile**
142: 
143: Marcus J. Whitmore is the founder, Chief Investment Officer, and controlling Managing Member (90% membership interest) of Driftwood Capital Management LLC. Whitmore established DCM and the Fund in 2017 following a distinguished career spanning twenty-eight (28) years in multi-strategy institutional investing. Prior to founding DCM, Whitmore served as Managing Director and Head of Multi-Strategy Investing at Veltrano Asset Partners LLC from 2004 to 2016, where he oversaw a multi-billion-dollar allocation across equity long/short, event-driven, and credit strategies within the financial services sector. Before joining Veltrano, Whitmore served as a Portfolio Manager at Fieldstone Capital Advisors LP from 1996 to 2004, where he managed equity long/short portfolios focused on the banking and specialty finance sectors.
144: 
145: Whitmore was the sole designated \"Key Person\" under Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA. His designation as the sole Key Person reflected his central role in the Fund\'s investment process, including his direct management of the largest strategy books, his sole authority over portfolio construction and risk limits at the fund level, and his personal relationships with many of the Fund\'s largest institutional investors. Whitmore\'s capital commitment to the Fund was \$57.4 million, representing 2.0% of the Fund\'s assets under management as of May 31, 2024. His carried interest entitlement, prior to the amendment described herein, was 18% of the General Partner\'s 20% incentive allocation --- equivalent to 3.6% of the Fund\'s net new profits above the high-water mark.
146: 
147: **B. Incapacitation Event**
148: 
149: On June 3, 2024, Marcus J. Whitmore suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke at his residence in New York City. Whitmore was transported to Lenox Hill Medical Center in New York, where he was admitted for emergency treatment and subsequently commenced an intensive neurorehabilitation program. According to information conveyed to DCM by Whitmore\'s immediate family and treating physicians, the attending neurological team projected a minimum recovery period of twelve (12) to eighteen (18) months, with an uncertain prognosis regarding Whitmore\'s ability to return to full-time professional activity. As of the date of this memorandum, Whitmore remains in a rehabilitation setting and has not resumed any professional duties with respect to DCM or the Fund.
150: 
151: The severity and sudden onset of Whitmore\'s medical condition meant that no advance notice was given to DCM, the limited partners, or any service provider prior to the incapacitation. DCM\'s Deputy CIO, Elaine R. Sato, assumed day-to-day operational and investment management responsibilities for the Fund on an interim basis effective June 3, 2024, subject to the contractual constraints described below.
152: 
153: **C. Key-Person Event Trigger Analysis**
154: 
155: Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA provides, in relevant part, as follows:
156: 
157: > A \"Key Person Event\" shall be deemed to have occurred if a Key Person designated pursuant to Section 8.04(a) is \"unable to devote substantially all of his professional time and attention to the affairs of the Partnership for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days,\" absent the prior written notice of such Key Person delivered to the General Partner and each member of the Investor Advisory Committee setting forth the anticipated duration and reason for such absence.
158: 
159: No prior written notice was delivered by Whitmore, as his incapacitation was sudden and unexpected. The incapacitation commenced on June 3, 2024. The seven-consecutive-calendar-day period prescribed by Section 8.04(b) elapsed at 11:59 p.m. (Eastern Time) on June 9, 2024, and accordingly the Key Person Event was deemed triggered as of the close of business on June 10, 2024 (the first business day following the expiration of the seven-day period). The C&H engagement team confirmed this trigger date through a detailed analysis of the A&R LPA\'s definitions and day-count conventions, as set forth in the Key-Person Event Analysis Memorandum delivered to DCM on June 13, 2024.
160: 
161: **D. Contractual Consequences (Section 8.04(c))**
162: 
163: Upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event, Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA imposed the following immediate and automatic consequences:
164: 
165: > \(i\) **Suspension of the Investment Period.** The Fund\'s Investment Period was immediately suspended. During the suspension, DCM was prohibited from making any new investments on behalf of the Fund. For purposes of this provision, a \"new investment\" was defined as any acquisition of a position not held in the Fund\'s portfolio as of the date of the Key Person Event.
166: >
167: > \(ii\) **Follow-On Investment Cap.** Follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions were permitted, but were capped at an aggregate of \$28.7 million (1.0% of AUM as of the most recent month-end preceding the Key Person Event, calculated as 1.0% of \$2.87 billion).
168: >
169: > \(iii\) **LP Notification Requirement.** The General Partner was required to notify all limited partners of the Fund in writing within five (5) business days of the occurrence of the Key Person Event. Given the Key Person Event trigger date of June 10, 2024 (a Monday), the five-business-day notification deadline fell on June 17, 2024 (the following Monday).
170: >
171: > \(iv\) **Commencement of the 90-Day Cure Period.** A Cure Period of ninety (90) calendar days commenced on June 10, 2024, expiring on September 8, 2024. During the Cure Period, the General Partner was afforded the opportunity to propose one or more Successor Key Persons, subject to approval by limited partners holding not less than 66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments (excluding the GP co-investment).
172: >
173: > \(v\) **Failure to Cure.** If no Successor Key Person was approved by the requisite supermajority of limited partners within the Cure Period, the A&R LPA provided that limited partners holding a majority-in-interest could elect either (a) to extend the Cure Period by up to ninety (90) additional calendar days, or (b) to commence an orderly wind-down of the Fund.
174: 
175: **E. LP Consent Voting Mechanics**
176: 
177: The approval threshold for designation of Successor Key Persons under Section 8.04(c) required the affirmative written consent of limited partners holding not less than 66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments, with the GP co-investment excluded from the denominator. The applicable calculations were as follows:
178: 
179: > • Total Fund AUM (May 31, 2024): \$2,870,000,000
180: >
181: > • Less: Marcus J. Whitmore GP co-investment: (\$57,400,000)
182: >
183: > • Less: Elaine R. Sato co-investment (as Managing Member of GP entity): (\$14,350,000)
184: >
185: > • Voting LP Capital Commitments: \$2,798,250,000
186: >
187: > • Required Consent Threshold (66⅔%): \$1,865,500,000
188: 
189: The foregoing calculation was confirmed in the Key-Person Event Analysis Memorandum and was consistent with the methodology specified in Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA for the computation of LP voting percentages.
190: 
191: **[V. DETAILED MATTER TIMELINE]{.underline}**
192: 
193: **A. Phase 1: Initial Response (June 10--17, 2024)**
194: 
195: **June 10, 2024 --- Key Person Event Deemed Triggered.** As described in Section IV.C above, the Key Person Event under Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA was deemed triggered as of June 10, 2024, upon expiration of the seven-consecutive-calendar-day period during which Whitmore was unable to devote substantially all of his professional time and attention to the affairs of the Fund. The Investment Period was automatically suspended, and the 90-calendar-day Cure Period commenced running.
196: 
197: **June 11, 2024 --- Engagement Opened.** Calderwood & Harkness LLP was formally engaged by DCM on June 11, 2024. The engagement letter was executed by Elaine R. Sato on behalf of DCM and by Graham Sutherland on behalf of C&H. Matter No. 1024-00002 was assigned. The engagement team was assembled immediately, and an initial conference call was held with Ms. Sato and DCM\'s General Counsel to receive a factual briefing on the circumstances of Whitmore\'s incapacitation and to discuss preliminary legal considerations.
198: 
199: **June 11--13, 2024 --- Legal Analysis and Internal Memorandum.** The C&H engagement team undertook a comprehensive analysis of the key-person clause mechanics under Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, the contractual consequences of the Key Person Event, and the applicable provisions of Delaware law governing limited partnerships. This analysis included a review of the entire A&R LPA, with particular focus on the definitions of \"Key Person,\" \"Key Person Event,\" \"Investment Period,\" \"Cure Period,\" and \"Successor Key Person,\" as well as the voting and consent provisions set forth in Article XIV. The team also analyzed the interplay between the key-person provisions and the Fund\'s investment management agreement and related side letters with certain institutional limited partners. The Key-Person Event Analysis Memorandum was prepared and delivered to DCM on June 13, 2024. The memorandum confirmed the trigger date, outlined the contractual consequences, identified the applicable deadlines, and set forth a recommended course of action for the Cure Period.
200: 
201: **June 14, 2024 --- LP Notification Letter.** The LP Notification Letter was finalized, reviewed, and approved by C&H. The letter was signed by Elaine R. Sato in her capacity as Deputy Chief Investment Officer of DCM and distributed to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund via email (with contemporaneous hard copy via overnight courier). The notification disclosed the following: (i) the occurrence of the Key Person Event; (ii) the nature of the triggering circumstance (medical incapacitation of Marcus J. Whitmore); (iii) the automatic suspension of the Investment Period; (iv) the follow-on investment cap of \$28.7 million; (v) the commencement of the 90-day Cure Period expiring September 8, 2024; and (vi) DCM\'s intention to propose Successor Key Persons during the Cure Period. The LP Notification Letter was sent three (3) business days in advance of the contractual deadline of June 17, 2024, ensuring full compliance with the timing requirements of Section 8.04(c).
202: 
203: **B. Phase 2: Successor Governance Framework Development (June 17--July 15, 2024)**
204: 
205: Following the delivery of the LP Notification Letter, the C&H engagement team commenced the development of a comprehensive successor governance framework. This workstream involved extensive consultation with Elaine R. Sato and other senior members of DCM\'s investment team, a review of industry best practices for key-person succession in institutional hedge fund structures, and an analysis of the expectations and concerns likely to be raised by the Fund\'s institutional limited partner base and the Investor Advisory Committee.
206: 
207: **Successor Governance Framework Memorandum.** C&H prepared and delivered to DCM a detailed Successor Governance Framework Memorandum setting forth the Firm\'s analysis and recommendations. The principal recommendations were as follows:
208: 
209: > \(a\) **Designation of Joint Successor Key Persons.** C&H recommended the designation of Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons under an amended Section 8.04. The recommendation was based on the complementary expertise and track records of the two individuals, their existing roles within DCM\'s investment process, and the need to demonstrate to the LP base that the Fund\'s multi-strategy mandate could be sustained without reliance on a single individual. The joint designation structure was also designed to address anticipated LP concerns regarding concentration of authority in a sole Key Person --- the very structure that had created the vulnerability exposed by Whitmore\'s incapacitation.
210: >
211: > \(b\) **Establishment of a Three-Member Investment Committee.** C&H recommended the creation of a formal Investment Committee under a new Section 8.05 of the A&R LPA. The Investment Committee was to be composed of three members: Sato (as Chair), Huang, and one independent member to be designated by the Investor Advisory Committee. The inclusion of an IAC-designated independent member was intended to enhance governance credibility and LP confidence, and to provide an institutional check on investment decision-making in the absence of Whitmore.
212: >
213: > \(c\) **Revised Key-Person Clause Mechanics.** C&H recommended a revision to the key-person clause to reflect the joint designation structure. Specifically, the loss of one Successor Key Person would trigger a 180-day Replacement Period --- during which the remaining Successor Key Person and the Investment Committee could continue to manage the Fund --- rather than an automatic Investment Period suspension. Only the loss of both Successor Key Persons would trigger the automatic Investment Period suspension and standard cure mechanics previously applicable under Section 8.04. This tiered approach was designed to provide operational continuity while preserving meaningful LP protections.
214: >
215: > \(d\) **Reduced Follow-On Investment Cap.** C&H recommended that the follow-on investment cap during any future Key Person Event be reduced from \$28.7 million (1.0% of AUM) to \$14.35 million (0.5% of AUM). This reduction was recommended as a concession to LP interests and in recognition of the fact that the establishment of the Investment Committee and the designation of two Successor Key Persons provided a more robust governance structure that warranted a correspondingly tighter investment restriction during any future disruption.
216: >
217: > \(e\) **Marcus J. Whitmore --- Senior Advisor Designation.** C&H recommended that Whitmore be transitioned to a \"Senior Advisor\" role with no governance authority under the A&R LPA as amended. Whitmore would retain no voting rights, no investment approval authority, and no management decision-making power with respect to the Fund. This designation was intended to preserve Whitmore\'s association with the Fund in a manner appropriate to his medical circumstances while making clear to the LP base that active governance authority had been fully transferred to the Successor Key Persons and the Investment Committee.
218: >
219: > \(f\) **Carried Interest Reallocation and Vesting.** C&H recommended a reallocation of the carried interest entitlements among the principals of DCM to reflect the shift in governance responsibility, with a corresponding vesting schedule for Whitmore\'s residual carried interest, as detailed in Section VI.E below.
220: 
221: **Drafting of the First Amendment.** Based on the approved governance framework, C&H drafted the First Amendment to the A&R LPA, incorporating all of the recommended structural changes. C&H also prepared the Successor Key Person Proposal and Consent Solicitation Letter to the limited partners (the \"Successor Proposal Letter\"), which set forth the rationale for the proposed successor governance framework, summarized the key terms of the First Amendment, and enclosed the Form of LP Written Consent.
222: 
223: **July 15, 2024 --- Circulation to Limited Partners.** The Successor Proposal Letter, the draft First Amendment, and the Form of LP Written Consent were circulated to all forty-seven (47) limited partners on July 15, 2024. The consent solicitation established a deadline of August 23, 2024 --- forty (40) calendar days from the date of circulation --- for the return of executed LP consent forms.
224: 
225: **C. Phase 3: IAC Review and Negotiation (July 15--August 5, 2024)**
226: 
227: **IAC Briefing.** In advance of the IAC\'s review of the Successor Proposal and draft First Amendment, C&H prepared a comprehensive IAC Briefing Memorandum. The memorandum was distributed to the five members of the Investor Advisory Committee, who collectively represented \$1,140 million in capital commitments to the Fund. The IAC members, their affiliations, and their respective capital commitments were as follows:
228: 
229:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
230:   **IAC Member**           **Affiliation**                                  **Role**                              **Capital Commitment**
231:   ------------------------ ------------------------------------------------ ------------------------------------- ------------------------
232:   Diana Cortland (Chair)   Northvale Public Employees\' Retirement System   Chief Investment Officer              \$310 million
233: 
234:   Richard Oshima           Sycamore Endowment Partners LP                   Director of Alternative Investments   \$275 million
235: 
236:   Catherine Mercer         Velthorn Institutional Fund of Funds III, L.P.   Managing Director                     \$220 million
237: 
238:   Thomas Ashworth          Bridlewood Family Office Holdings Ltd.           Principal                             \$185 million
239: 
240:   Nadia Al-Rashid          Atlas Sovereign Wealth Advisory LLC              Senior Portfolio Manager              \$150 million
241: 
242:   **Total**                                                                                                       **\$1,140 million**
243:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
244: 
245: The IAC Briefing Memorandum described the circumstances of the Key Person Event, the contractual consequences, the successor governance framework recommended by C&H and adopted by DCM, the key terms of the proposed First Amendment, and the consent solicitation process and timeline. The memorandum also included background information on the proposed Successor Key Persons, including their professional experience, roles at DCM, capital commitments to the Fund, and proposed carried interest allocations.
246: 
247: **July 29, 2024 --- IAC Meeting.** A formal meeting of the Investor Advisory Committee was held on July 29, 2024 by videoconference. The meeting was attended by all five IAC members and their respective representatives, as well as Graham Sutherland and Stephen Adler of C&H (on behalf of DCM) and Helen M. Calloway and David Pineda of Wexford Crane & Albright LLP (as counsel to the IAC). Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang of DCM also participated in portions of the meeting to present their respective backgrounds, investment philosophies, and plans for the ongoing management of the Fund. The IAC meeting lasted approximately two and one-half hours and included a detailed discussion of the proposed governance framework, the qualifications of the Successor Key Persons, the scope of the independent Investment Committee member\'s authority, and the LP consent solicitation process.
248: 
249: **WCA Comments and Negotiation.** Following the IAC meeting, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, acting on behalf of the IAC, submitted written comments on the draft First Amendment. The principal areas of comment and negotiation included the following:
250: 
251: > \(i\) **180-Day Replacement Period Mechanics.** WCA sought clarification and additional specificity regarding the mechanics of the 180-day Replacement Period triggered by the loss of one Successor Key Person, including the process for identifying and proposing a replacement, the voting threshold applicable to the replacement, and the consequences of a failure to replace within the 180-day period. C&H responded with proposed language establishing a structured replacement process, including a requirement that the General Partner submit a replacement proposal to the IAC within sixty (60) days, followed by a full LP consent solicitation within the remaining period.
252: >
253: > \(ii\) **Scope of IAC-Designated Independent Investment Committee Member\'s Authority.** WCA advocated for enhanced authority for the IAC-designated independent member of the Investment Committee, including a veto right over investments exceeding a specified threshold. C&H, after consultation with DCM, agreed to grant the independent member a consultative role and a negative consent right on any single investment exceeding 5% of the Fund\'s NAV, but resisted the imposition of a general veto right, which C&H advised would be inconsistent with the General Partner\'s fiduciary obligations and the Fund\'s operational requirements.
254: >
255: > \(iii\) **Follow-On Investment Cap Reduction.** WCA endorsed the proposed reduction of the follow-on investment cap from 1.0% to 0.5% of AUM during any future Key Person Event. No further negotiation was required on this point.
256: >
257: > \(iv\) **Whitmore Carried Interest Vesting Schedule.** WCA raised concerns regarding the pace of Whitmore\'s residual carried interest vesting, seeking to extend the vesting period from thirty-six (36) months to forty-eight (48) months. After negotiation, the parties agreed to retain the thirty-six (36) month vesting period, subject to a provision that any unvested carried interest would be forfeited if Whitmore were to compete with the Fund (a non-compete carve-out applicable to the vesting period).
258: >
259: > \(v\) **GP Fiduciary Obligations During Future Key Person Events.** WCA requested the inclusion of an express statement in the First Amendment confirming the GP\'s ongoing fiduciary obligations to the limited partners during any future Key Person Event. C&H agreed to the inclusion of a confirmatory provision, noting that such obligations already existed under Delaware law and the A&R LPA but acknowledging that an express restatement would provide additional comfort to the LP base.

**[I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") was engaged on June 11, 2024 by Driftwood Capital Management LLC (\"DCM\"), in its capacity as General Partner of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. (\"DARF\" or the \"Fund\"), to advise on the legal implications of, and governance response to, a key-person event triggered by the sudden medical incapacitation of Marcus J. Whitmore, the Fund\'s founder, Chief Investment Officer, and sole designated Key Person under Section 8.04 of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership, dated as of March 15, 2017 (the \"A&R LPA\"). The engagement arose under circumstances requiring immediate attention: Whitmore suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke on June 3, 2024, and the contractual Key Person Event was deemed triggered on June 10, 2024 upon expiration of the seven-consecutive-calendar-day threshold set forth in Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA, thereby suspending the Fund\'s Investment Period and initiating a 90-calendar-day Cure Period expiring September 8, 2024.

The scope of the engagement, as set forth in the engagement letter dated June 11, 2024, encompassed the following principal workstreams: (i) comprehensive analysis of Section 8.04 key-person clause mechanics and the contractual consequences flowing from the triggering event; (ii) preparation and review of the limited partner notification required under Section 8.04(c); (iii) development and recommendation of a successor governance framework, including the designation of successor Key Persons and the establishment of an Investment Committee; (iv) drafting and negotiation of the First Amendment to the A&R LPA (the \"First Amendment\") to implement the successor governance framework; and (v) solicitation and tabulation of limited partner consents as required under the A&R LPA for approval of the successor Key Persons and the related amendments.

All engagement objectives were achieved within the contractual Cure Period and in compliance with all applicable provisions of the A&R LPA, Delaware law, and Cayman Islands regulatory requirements. Thirty-eight (38) of the Fund\'s forty-seven (47) limited partners delivered written consents representing \$2,412.8 million of LP capital commitments, or approximately 86.2% of voting LP commitments --- well in excess of the 66⅔% supermajority threshold required under Section 8.04(c). The First Amendment to the A&R LPA became effective on August 26, 2024, designating Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons, establishing a three-member Investment Committee, transitioning Marcus J. Whitmore to a Senior Advisor role without governance authority, and implementing a revised carried interest allocation among the principals of DCM. The Cure Period deadline of September 8, 2024 was thereby mooted by the successful completion of the successor governance process thirteen (13) calendar days in advance.

The engagement is closed as of September 2, 2024. The matter status is: **closed_completed**. No outstanding legal issues, open work items, or continuing obligations of the Firm remain as of the date of this memorandum.

The client entity for this engagement is Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd., a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership registered under the Exempted Limited Partnership Act (As Revised) of the Cayman Islands. The Fund\'s key identifying information and structural details are set forth below.

**Investment Strategy:** The Fund pursues a multi-strategy absolute return mandate, deploying capital across three primary strategy verticals: (i) equity long/short, (ii) event-driven (including merger arbitrage, activist situations, and special situations), and (iii) credit relative value. The Fund maintains a sector focus on the financial services industry, with particular emphasis on asset management and banking subsectors. The Fund\'s strategy is implemented on a global basis, with the majority of risk exposure concentrated in North American and Western European markets.
**Fund Inception Date:** March 15, 2017

The Fund does not accept investments from natural persons other than through institutional vehicles.

**Full Legal Name:** Driftwood Capital Management LLC
**Entity Type:** Delaware limited liability company
**Employer Identification Number (EIN):** 82-4917653
**Principal Office:** 680 Lexington Avenue, 31st Floor, New York, NY 10022
**Delaware Registered Agent:** Capitol Registered Agents, Inc., 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801
**Managing Members:** DCM is managed by two Managing Members. As of the date of the Key Person Event, the membership interests and management responsibilities were allocated as follows:

> \(a\) **Marcus J. Whitmore** --- Managing Member, holding a 90% membership interest in DCM. Whitmore served as founder and Chief Investment Officer of DCM and the Fund from inception, and was the sole designated Key Person under Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA.

Mr. Sutherland personally led the negotiation with Wexford Crane & Albright LLP on behalf of the Investor Advisory Committee and participated in the July 29, 2024 IAC meeting. Pamela Cross served as the Billing Partner and was responsible for all billing and engagement economics matters. Stephen Adler served as the Lead Associate and was principally responsible for the preparation of all memoranda, the drafting of the First Amendment, the LP consent solicitation process, and the tabulation of LP consents. Theresa Kim served as the Working Associate and supported all research, drafting, and document management functions throughout the engagement.
**B. Fee Arrangement**
The Firm\'s engagement was subject to an hourly billing arrangement, with an aggregate fee cap of \$385,000 for the entirety of the engagement. The applicable billing rates were as follows:
> • Partner rate: \$1,650 per hour
> • Associate rate: \$895 per hour

The billing partner for the engagement was Pamela Cross. The engagement letter was dated June 11, 2024, and was addressed to Elaine R. Sato, in her capacity as Deputy Chief Investment Officer of DCM. The engagement letter was countersigned by Ms. Sato on behalf of DCM and returned to the Firm on the same date. All fees incurred during the engagement were within the aggregate fee cap.
**C. Counterparty Counsel**

The Investor Advisory Committee of the Fund retained independent legal counsel in connection with its review and negotiation of the successor governance framework and the First Amendment. The details of counterparty counsel are as follows:
**Firm:** Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, 51 West 52nd Street, 40th Floor, New York, NY 10019
**Lead Partner:** Helen M. Calloway, Partner, Investment Funds Group
**Senior Associate:** David Pineda, Senior Associate, Investment Funds Group

Wexford Crane & Albright LLP (\"WCA\") represented the interests of the Investor Advisory Committee throughout the review and negotiation period described in Section V.C below. WCA\'s representation was limited to the IAC and did not extend to any individual limited partner or to the limited partner body as a whole. The costs of WCA\'s representation were borne by the Fund in accordance with the IAC expense reimbursement provisions set forth in Section 9.04 of the A&R LPA.
**[IV. BACKGROUND: THE KEY-PERSON EVENT]{.underline}**
**A. Marcus J. Whitmore --- Profile**

Marcus J. Whitmore is the founder, Chief Investment Officer, and controlling Managing Member (90% membership interest) of Driftwood Capital Management LLC. Whitmore established DCM and the Fund in 2017 following a distinguished career spanning twenty-eight (28) years in multi-strategy institutional investing. Prior to founding DCM, Whitmore served as Managing Director and Head of Multi-Strategy Investing at Veltrano Asset Partners LLC from 2004 to 2016, where he oversaw a multi-billion-dollar allocation across equity long/short, event-driven, and credit strategies within the financial services sector. Before joining Veltrano, Whitmore served as a Portfolio Manager at Fieldstone Capital Advisors LP from 1996 to 2004, where he managed equity long/short portfolios focused on the banking and specialty finance sectors.

Whitmore was the sole designated \"Key Person\" under Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA. His designation as the sole Key Person reflected his central role in the Fund\'s investment process, including his direct management of the largest strategy books, his sole authority over portfolio construction and risk limits at the fund level, and his personal relationships with many of the Fund\'s largest institutional investors. Whitmore\'s capital commitment to the Fund was \$57.4 million, representing 2.0% of the Fund\'s assets under management as of May 31, 2024. His carried interest entitlement, prior to the amendment described herein, was 18% of the General Partner\'s 20% incentive allocation --- equivalent to 3.6% of the Fund\'s net new profits above the high-water mark.
**B. Incapacitation Event**

On June 3, 2024, Marcus J. Whitmore suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke at his residence in New York City. Whitmore was transported to Lenox Hill Medical Center in New York, where he was admitted for emergency treatment and subsequently commenced an intensive neurorehabilitation program. According to information conveyed to DCM by Whitmore\'s immediate family and treating physicians, the attending neurological team projected a minimum recovery period of twelve (12) to eighteen (18) months, with an uncertain prognosis regarding Whitmore\'s ability to return to full-time professional activity. As of the date of this memorandum, Whitmore remains in a rehabilitation setting and has not resumed any professional duties with respect to DCM or the Fund.

The severity and sudden onset of Whitmore\'s medical condition meant that no advance notice was given to DCM, the limited partners, or any service provider prior to the incapacitation. DCM\'s Deputy CIO, Elaine R. Sato, assumed day-to-day operational and investment management responsibilities for the Fund on an interim basis effective June 3, 2024, subject to the contractual constraints described below.
**C. Key-Person Event Trigger Analysis**
Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA provides, in relevant part, as follows:

> A \"Key Person Event\" shall be deemed to have occurred if a Key Person designated pursuant to Section 8.04(a) is \"unable to devote substantially all of his professional time and attention to the affairs of the Partnership for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days,\" absent the prior written notice of such Key Person delivered to the General Partner and each member of the Investor Advisory Committee setting forth the anticipated duration and reason for such absence.

No prior written notice was delivered by Whitmore, as his incapacitation was sudden and unexpected. The incapacitation commenced on June 3, 2024. The seven-consecutive-calendar-day period prescribed by Section 8.04(b) elapsed at 11:59 p.m. (Eastern Time) on June 9, 2024, and accordingly the Key Person Event was deemed triggered as of the close of business on June 10, 2024 (the first business day following the expiration of the seven-day period). The C&H engagement team confirmed this trigger date through a detailed analysis of the A&R LPA\'s definitions and day-count conventions, as set forth in the Key-Person Event Analysis Memorandum delivered to DCM on June 13, 2024.
**D. Contractual Consequences (Section 8.04(c))**
Upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event, Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA imposed the following immediate and automatic consequences:

> \(i\) **Suspension of the Investment Period.** The Fund\'s Investment Period was immediately suspended. During the suspension, DCM was prohibited from making any new investments on behalf of the Fund. For purposes of this provision, a \"new investment\" was defined as any acquisition of a position not held in the Fund\'s portfolio as of the date of the Key Person Event.

> \(ii\) **Follow-On Investment Cap.** Follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions were permitted, but were capped at an aggregate of \$28.7 million (1.0% of AUM as of the most recent month-end preceding the Key Person Event, calculated as 1.0% of \$2.87 billion).

> \(iii\) **LP Notification Requirement.** The General Partner was required to notify all limited partners of the Fund in writing within five (5) business days of the occurrence of the Key Person Event. Given the Key Person Event trigger date of June 10, 2024 (a Monday), the five-business-day notification deadline fell on June 17, 2024 (the following Monday).

> \(iv\) **Commencement of the 90-Day Cure Period.** A Cure Period of ninety (90) calendar days commenced on June 10, 2024, expiring on September 8, 2024. During the Cure Period, the General Partner was afforded the opportunity to propose one or more Successor Key Persons, subject to approval by limited partners holding not less than 66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments (excluding the GP co-investment).

> \(v\) **Failure to Cure.** If no Successor Key Person was approved by the requisite supermajority of limited partners within the Cure Period, the A&R LPA provided that limited partners holding a majority-in-interest could elect either (a) to extend the Cure Period by up to ninety (90) additional calendar days, or (b) to commence an orderly wind-down of the Fund.
**E. LP Consent Voting Mechanics**

The approval threshold for designation of Successor Key Persons under Section 8.04(c) required the affirmative written consent of limited partners holding not less than 66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments, with the GP co-investment excluded from the denominator. The applicable calculations were as follows:
> • Less: Marcus J. Whitmore GP co-investment: (\$57,400,000)
> • Less: Elaine R. Sato co-investment (as Managing Member of GP entity): (\$14,350,000)
> • Voting LP Capital Commitments: \$2,798,250,000
> • Required Consent Threshold (66⅔%): \$1,865,500,000

The foregoing calculation was confirmed in the Key-Person Event Analysis Memorandum and was consistent with the methodology specified in Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA for the computation of LP voting percentages.
**[V. DETAILED MATTER TIMELINE]{.underline}**
**A. Phase 1: Initial Response (June 10--17, 2024)**

**June 10, 2024 --- Key Person Event Deemed Triggered.** As described in Section IV.C above, the Key Person Event under Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA was deemed triggered as of June 10, 2024, upon expiration of the seven-consecutive-calendar-day period during which Whitmore was unable to devote substantially all of his professional time and attention to the affairs of the Fund. The Investment Period was automatically suspended, and the 90-calendar-day Cure Period commenced running.

**June 11, 2024 --- Engagement Opened.** Calderwood & Harkness LLP was formally engaged by DCM on June 11, 2024. The engagement letter was executed by Elaine R. Sato on behalf of DCM and by Graham Sutherland on behalf of C&H. Matter No. 1024-00002 was assigned. The engagement team was assembled immediately, and an initial conference call was held with Ms. Sato and DCM\'s General Counsel to receive a factual briefing on the circumstances of Whitmore\'s incapacitation and to discuss preliminary legal considerations.

**June 11--13, 2024 --- Legal Analysis and Internal Memorandum.** The C&H engagement team undertook a comprehensive analysis of the key-person clause mechanics under Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, the contractual consequences of the Key Person Event, and the applicable provisions of Delaware law governing limited partnerships. This analysis included a review of the entire A&R LPA, with particular focus on the definitions of \"Key Person,\" \"Key Person Event,\" \"Investment Period,\" \"Cure Period,\" and \"Successor Key Person,\" as well as the voting and consent provisions set forth in Article XIV. The team also analyzed the interplay between the key-person provisions and the Fund\'s investment management agreement and related side letters with certain institutional limited partners. The Key-Person Event Analysis Memorandum was prepared and delivered to DCM on June 13, 2024. The memorandum confirmed the trigger date, outlined the contractual consequences, identified the applicable deadlines, and set forth a recommended course of action for the Cure Period.

**June 14, 2024 --- LP Notification Letter.** The LP Notification Letter was finalized, reviewed, and approved by C&H. The letter was signed by Elaine R. Sato in her capacity as Deputy Chief Investment Officer of DCM and distributed to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund via email (with contemporaneous hard copy via overnight courier). The notification disclosed the following: (i) the occurrence of the Key Person Event; (ii) the nature of the triggering circumstance (medical incapacitation of Marcus J. Whitmore); (iii) the automatic suspension of the Investment Period; (iv) the follow-on investment cap of \$28.7 million; (v) the commencement of the 90-day Cure Period expiring September 8, 2024; and (vi) DCM\'s intention to propose Successor Key Persons during the Cure Period. The LP Notification Letter was sent three (3) business days in advance of the contractual deadline of June 17, 2024, ensuring full compliance with the timing requirements of Section 8.04(c).
**B. Phase 2: Successor Governance Framework Development (June 17--July 15, 2024)**

Following the delivery of the LP Notification Letter, the C&H engagement team commenced the development of a comprehensive successor governance framework. This workstream involved extensive consultation with Elaine R. Sato and other senior members of DCM\'s investment team, a review of industry best practices for key-person succession in institutional hedge fund structures, and an analysis of the expectations and concerns likely to be raised by the Fund\'s institutional limited partner base and the Investor Advisory Committee.

**Successor Governance Framework Memorandum.** C&H prepared and delivered to DCM a detailed Successor Governance Framework Memorandum setting forth the Firm\'s analysis and recommendations. The principal recommendations were as follows:

> \(a\) **Designation of Joint Successor Key Persons.** C&H recommended the designation of Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons under an amended Section 8.04. The recommendation was based on the complementary expertise and track records of the two individuals, their existing roles within DCM\'s investment process, and the need to demonstrate to the LP base that the Fund\'s multi-strategy mandate could be sustained without reliance on a single individual. The joint designation structure was also designed to address anticipated LP concerns regarding concentration of authority in a sole Key Person --- the very structure that had created the vulnerability exposed by Whitmore\'s incapacitation.

> \(b\) **Establishment of a Three-Member Investment Committee.** C&H recommended the creation of a formal Investment Committee under a new Section 8.05 of the A&R LPA. The Investment Committee was to be composed of three members: Sato (as Chair), Huang, and one independent member to be designated by the Investor Advisory Committee. The inclusion of an IAC-designated independent member was intended to enhance governance credibility and LP confidence, and to provide an institutional check on investment decision-making in the absence of Whitmore.

> \(c\) **Revised Key-Person Clause Mechanics.** C&H recommended a revision to the key-person clause to reflect the joint designation structure. Specifically, the loss of one Successor Key Person would trigger a 180-day Replacement Period --- during which the remaining Successor Key Person and the Investment Committee could continue to manage the Fund --- rather than an automatic Investment Period suspension. Only the loss of both Successor Key Persons would trigger the automatic Investment Period suspension and standard cure mechanics previously applicable under Section 8.04. This tiered approach was designed to provide operational continuity while preserving meaningful LP protections.

> \(d\) **Reduced Follow-On Investment Cap.** C&H recommended that the follow-on investment cap during any future Key Person Event be reduced from \$28.7 million (1.0% of AUM) to \$14.35 million (0.5% of AUM). This reduction was recommended as a concession to LP interests and in recognition of the fact that the establishment of the Investment Committee and the designation of two Successor Key Persons provided a more robust governance structure that warranted a correspondingly tighter investment restriction during any future disruption.

> \(e\) **Marcus J. Whitmore --- Senior Advisor Designation.** C&H recommended that Whitmore be transitioned to a \"Senior Advisor\" role with no governance authority under the A&R LPA as amended. Whitmore would retain no voting rights, no investment approval authority, and no management decision-making power with respect to the Fund. This designation was intended to preserve Whitmore\'s association with the Fund in a manner appropriate to his medical circumstances while making clear to the LP base that active governance authority had been fully transferred to the Successor Key Persons and the Investment Committee.

> \(f\) **Carried Interest Reallocation and Vesting.** C&H recommended a reallocation of the carried interest entitlements among the principals of DCM to reflect the shift in governance responsibility, with a corresponding vesting schedule for Whitmore\'s residual carried interest, as detailed in Section VI.E below.

**Drafting of the First Amendment.** Based on the approved governance framework, C&H drafted the First Amendment to the A&R LPA, incorporating all of the recommended structural changes. C&H also prepared the Successor Key Person Proposal and Consent Solicitation Letter to the limited partners (the \"Successor Proposal Letter\"), which set forth the rationale for the proposed successor governance framework, summarized the key terms of the First Amendment, and enclosed the Form of LP Written Consent.

**July 15, 2024 --- Circulation to Limited Partners.** The Successor Proposal Letter, the draft First Amendment, and the Form of LP Written Consent were circulated to all forty-seven (47) limited partners on July 15, 2024. The consent solicitation established a deadline of August 23, 2024 --- forty (40) calendar days from the date of circulation --- for the return of executed LP consent forms.
**C. Phase 3: IAC Review and Negotiation (July 15--August 5, 2024)**

**IAC Briefing.** In advance of the IAC\'s review of the Successor Proposal and draft First Amendment, C&H prepared a comprehensive IAC Briefing Memorandum. The memorandum was distributed to the five members of the Investor Advisory Committee, who collectively represented \$1,140 million in capital commitments to the Fund. The IAC members, their affiliations, and their respective capital commitments were as follows:
**IAC Member**           **Affiliation**                                  **Role**                              **Capital Commitment**
Diana Cortland (Chair)   Northvale Public Employees\' Retirement System   Chief Investment Officer              \$310 million
Richard Oshima           Sycamore Endowment Partners LP                   Director of Alternative Investments   \$275 million
Catherine Mercer         Velthorn Institutional Fund of Funds III, L.P.   Managing Director                     \$220 million
Thomas Ashworth          Bridlewood Family Office Holdings Ltd.           Principal                             \$185 million
Nadia Al-Rashid          Atlas Sovereign Wealth Advisory LLC              Senior Portfolio Manager              \$150 million
**Total**                                                                                                       **\$1,140 million**

The IAC Briefing Memorandum described the circumstances of the Key Person Event, the contractual consequences, the successor governance framework recommended by C&H and adopted by DCM, the key terms of the proposed First Amendment, and the consent solicitation process and timeline. The memorandum also included background information on the proposed Successor Key Persons, including their professional experience, roles at DCM, capital commitments to the Fund, and proposed carried interest allocations.

**July 29, 2024 --- IAC Meeting.** A formal meeting of the Investor Advisory Committee was held on July 29, 2024 by videoconference. The meeting was attended by all five IAC members and their respective representatives, as well as Graham Sutherland and Stephen Adler of C&H (on behalf of DCM) and Helen M. Calloway and David Pineda of Wexford Crane & Albright LLP (as counsel to the IAC). Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang of DCM also participated in portions of the meeting to present their respective backgrounds, investment philosophies, and plans for the ongoing management of the Fund. The IAC meeting lasted approximately two and one-half hours and included a detailed discussion of the proposed governance framework, the qualifications of the Successor Key Persons, the scope of the independent Investment Committee member\'s authority, and the LP consent solicitation process.

**WCA Comments and Negotiation.** Following the IAC meeting, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, acting on behalf of the IAC, submitted written comments on the draft First Amendment. The principal areas of comment and negotiation included the following:

> \(i\) **180-Day Replacement Period Mechanics.** WCA sought clarification and additional specificity regarding the mechanics of the 180-day Replacement Period triggered by the loss of one Successor Key Person, including the process for identifying and proposing a replacement, the voting threshold applicable to the replacement, and the consequences of a failure to replace within the 180-day period. C&H responded with proposed language establishing a structured replacement process, including a requirement that the General Partner submit a replacement proposal to the IAC within sixty (60) days, followed by a full LP consent solicitation within the remaining period.

> \(ii\) **Scope of IAC-Designated Independent Investment Committee Member\'s Authority.** WCA advocated for enhanced authority for the IAC-designated independent member of the Investment Committee, including a veto right over investments exceeding a specified threshold. C&H, after consultation with DCM, agreed to grant the independent member a consultative role and a negative consent right on any single investment exceeding 5% of the Fund\'s NAV, but resisted the imposition of a general veto right, which C&H advised would be inconsistent with the General Partner\'s fiduciary obligations and the Fund\'s operational requirements.

> \(iii\) **Follow-On Investment Cap Reduction.** WCA endorsed the proposed reduction of the follow-on investment cap from 1.0% to 0.5% of AUM during any future Key Person Event. No further negotiation was required on this point.

> \(iv\) **Whitmore Carried Interest Vesting Schedule.** WCA raised concerns regarding the pace of Whitmore\'s residual carried interest vesting, seeking to extend the vesting period from thirty-six (36) months to forty-eight (48) months. After negotiation, the parties agreed to retain the thirty-six (36) month vesting period, subject to a provision that any unvested carried interest would be forfeited if Whitmore were to compete with the Fund (a non-compete carve-out applicable to the vesting period).

> \(v\) **GP Fiduciary Obligations During Future Key Person Events.** WCA requested the inclusion of an express statement in the First Amendment confirming the GP\'s ongoing fiduciary obligations to the limited partners during any future Key Person Event. C&H agreed to the inclusion of a confirmatory provision, noting that such obligations already existed under Delaware law and the A&R LPA but acknowledging that an express restatement would provide additional comfort to the LP base.

Huang are, at the same time, unable to devote substantially all of their respective professional time to the affairs of the Partnership, by reason of death, permanent disability (as determined in good faith by the General Partner based on medical evidence reasonably available), voluntary or involuntary departure from DCM or the Partnership, termination for cause, or any other cause, for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days. If only **one** of the two Key Persons ceases active involvement in the management of the Partnership\'s investment portfolio for any reason whatsoever (a \'Single Key Person Departure\'), a Key Person Event shall not be deemed to have occurred; provided, however, that the provisions of Section 8.04(c)(ii) (Replacement Period) shall apply in the case of a Single Key Person Departure. The determination of whether a Key Person Event or a Single Key Person Departure has occurred shall be made by the General Partner in good faith, and the General Partner shall promptly notify the Investor Advisory Committee and all Limited Partners of any such determination.\"
80: 
81: **Section 2.3 --- Amendment of Section 8.04(c) --- Consequences of Key Person Event and Single Key Person Departure.** Section 8.04(c) of the Agreement is hereby amended and restated in its entirety to read as follows:
82: 
83: > \"**Section 8.04(c)** --- *Consequences of Key Person Event and Single Key Person Departure.*
84: >
85: > **(i) Full Key Person Event (Both Key Persons).** Upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event (i.e., both Key Persons ceasing active involvement simultaneously or within seven (7) consecutive calendar days of each other):
86: >
87: > \(A\) the Investment Period shall be immediately suspended, and no new investments shall be permitted during the period of such suspension;
88: >
89: > \(B\) follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions shall be capped at Fourteen Million Three Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$14,350,000), representing 0.5% of assets under management as of the most recent net asset value determination available at the time of the Key Person Event (for the avoidance of doubt, this cap replaces the prior cap of \$28,700,000 representing 1.0% of assets under management that was applicable under the Agreement as in effect prior to the Amendment Effective Date);
90: >
91: > \(C\) the General Partner shall notify all Limited Partners in writing within five (5) business days of the occurrence of the Key Person Event, setting forth in reasonable detail the circumstances giving rise to the Key Person Event and the General Partner\'s initial assessment of the impact on the Partnership\'s investment activities;
92: >
93: > \(D\) a Cure Period of ninety (90) calendar days shall commence on the date of the Key Person Event, during which the General Partner may propose one or more replacement Key Persons for approval by the Limited Partners;
94: >
95: > \(E\) approval of any proposed replacement Key Person shall require the written consent of Limited Partners holding not less than sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment), such consent to be solicited in writing in accordance with the notice provisions of the Agreement; and
96: >
97: > \(F\) if no replacement Key Person is approved within the Cure Period, Limited Partners holding a majority-in-interest of aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment) may elect, by written notice delivered to the General Partner within thirty (30) calendar days following the expiration of the Cure Period, to (x) extend the Cure Period by up to ninety (90) additional calendar days on the same terms set forth in this Section 8.04(c)(i), or (y) direct the General Partner to commence an orderly wind-down of the Partnership in accordance with Section 12.01 of this Agreement.
98: >
99: > **(ii) Single Key Person Departure (One Key Person).** Upon the occurrence of a Single Key Person Departure (i.e., only one of the two Key Persons ceasing active involvement):
100: >
101: > \(A\) the Investment Period shall **not** be automatically suspended;
102: >
103: > \(B\) a Replacement Period of one hundred eighty (180) calendar days shall commence on the date of the Single Key Person Departure;
104: >
105: > \(C\) during the Replacement Period, the remaining Key Person shall continue to manage the Partnership\'s investments in the ordinary course, subject to oversight by the Investment Committee established under Section 8.05 of this Agreement, and the remaining Key Person shall not have the authority to make any new investment or commitment in excess of Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000) without the prior approval of the Investment Committee;
106: >
107: > \(D\) during the Replacement Period, the General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to identify and propose a replacement for the departed Key Person, and any such proposed replacement shall be subject to approval by Limited Partners holding not less than sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment);
108: >
109: > \(E\) follow-on investments during the Replacement Period shall be capped at Fourteen Million Three Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$14,350,000), representing 0.5% of assets under management as of the most recent net asset value determination;
110: >
111: > \(F\) the General Partner shall notify all Limited Partners in writing within five (5) business days of a Single Key Person Departure, setting forth in reasonable detail the circumstances giving rise to the Single Key Person Departure, the identity of the remaining Key Person, and the General Partner\'s plan for identifying a replacement Key Person; and
112: >
113: > \(G\) if no replacement Key Person is approved prior to the expiration of the Replacement Period, a Key Person Event shall be deemed to have occurred on the date of such expiration, and the provisions of Section 8.04(c)(i) shall thereupon apply as if such Key Person Event had occurred on such date.\"
114: 
115: **[ARTICLE III --- ADDITION OF SECTION 8.05 (INVESTMENT COMMITTEE)]{.underline}**
116: 
117: **Section 3.1 --- New Section 8.05.** A new Section 8.05 is hereby added to the Agreement immediately following Section 8.04 (as amended by Article II of this Amendment), which Section 8.05 shall read in its entirety as follows:
118: 
119: > \"**Section 8.05** --- *Investment Committee.*
120: >
121: > **(a) Establishment.** Effective as of the Amendment Effective Date, the General Partner shall establish an Investment Committee of the Partnership (the \'Investment Committee\'). The Investment Committee shall be a standing committee of the Partnership and shall continue in existence for so long as the Partnership continues to conduct investment operations.
122: >
123: > **(b) Composition.** The Investment Committee shall consist of three (3) members, as follows:
124: >
125: > \(i\) Elaine R. Sato, who shall serve as Chair of the Investment Committee and who shall preside over all meetings of the Investment Committee;
126: >
127: > \(ii\) Jonathan K. Huang, who shall serve as a member of the Investment Committee; and
128: >
129: > \(iii\) one independent member (the \'IAC-Designated Member\') to be designated by a majority vote of the members of the Investor Advisory Committee established under Section 9.02 of this Agreement, such designation to occur within sixty (60) days of the Amendment Effective Date. The IAC-Designated Member shall be a natural person who is not an employee, officer, member, partner, or affiliate of the General Partner, DCM, or any of their respective affiliates. The IAC-Designated Member shall serve at the pleasure of the Investor Advisory Committee and may be removed and replaced by a majority vote of the IAC members at any time.
130: >
131: > Vacancies on the Investment Committee arising by reason of death, resignation, removal, or incapacity of any member shall be filled in the same manner as the original appointment of such member (i.e., vacancies in positions (i) or (ii) above shall be filled by the General Partner, and vacancies in position (iii) shall be filled by a majority vote of the Investor Advisory Committee). Any vacancy shall be filled within thirty (30) calendar days of its occurrence, and pending the filling of any vacancy, the remaining members of the Investment Committee shall continue to exercise the authority and functions of the Investment Committee.
132: >
133: > **(c) Authority and Functions.** The Investment Committee shall oversee the investment activities of the Partnership, including, without limitation, the review and approval of all new investments, all material follow-on investments, all material dispositions of portfolio investments, and all other material portfolio decisions as determined in good faith by the Chair of the Investment Committee. All investment decisions requiring Investment Committee approval shall require the affirmative vote of at least two (2) of the three (3) members of the Investment Committee. In the event of a tie or deadlock, the Chair of the Investment Committee shall not have a casting vote, and the matter shall be tabled for further discussion at the next meeting of the Investment Committee unless the Chair determines, in her reasonable judgment, that the matter requires immediate action to protect the interests of the Partnership, in which case the Chair may take such action as she deems reasonably necessary and shall promptly report such action to the full Investment Committee and the Investor Advisory Committee.
134: >
135: > The Investment Committee shall meet not less frequently than monthly, either in person or by telephonic or video conference, and shall keep written minutes of its proceedings, which minutes shall be made available to the Investor Advisory Committee upon request.
136: >
137: > **(d) Reporting.** The Investment Committee shall provide quarterly written reports to the Investor Advisory Committee and to all Limited Partners summarizing the activities and investment decisions of the Investment Committee during the preceding quarter, including a summary of all new investments approved, all investments declined, all material portfolio actions taken, and any other matters the Investment Committee deems relevant to the Limited Partners\' understanding of the Partnership\'s investment activities. Such quarterly reports shall be delivered within thirty (30) calendar days following the end of each calendar quarter.\"
138: 
139: **[ARTICLE IV --- ADDITION OF SECTION 8.06 (SENIOR ADVISOR)]{.underline}**
140: 
141: **Section 4.1 --- New Section 8.06.** A new Section 8.06 is hereby added to the Agreement immediately following Section 8.05 (as added by Article III of this Amendment), which Section 8.06 shall read in its entirety as follows:
142: 
143: > \"**Section 8.06** --- *Senior Advisor.*
144: >
145: > **(a) Designation.** Marcus J. Whitmore is hereby designated as \'Senior Advisor\' to the Partnership, effective as of the Amendment Effective Date, in recognition of his foundational role in establishing and building the Partnership and his contributions to the Partnership\'s investment strategy and performance since inception.
146: >
147: > **(b) Role and Limitations.** The Senior Advisor shall have no governance authority, voting rights, or decision-making power with respect to the Partnership\'s investments, operations, or other affairs. The Senior Advisor shall not serve as a member of the Investment Committee. The Senior Advisor shall not have the authority to bind the Partnership or the General Partner in any respect, and shall not hold himself out as having any such authority. The Senior Advisor may, at the request of the General Partner (acting through its authorized officers), provide non-binding advisory input on investment strategy, portfolio construction, risk management, or such other matters as the General Partner may reasonably request from time to time, but the Senior Advisor shall have no obligation to provide any such advisory input, and any advisory input provided by the Senior Advisor shall be solely for informational purposes and shall not be binding on the General Partner, the Investment Committee, or the Partnership.
148: >
149: > For the avoidance of doubt, the designation of Marcus J. Whitmore as Senior Advisor does not constitute the Senior Advisor as a Key Person, general partner, managing member, officer, director, or employee of the Partnership or DCM, and shall not give rise to any fiduciary duty or obligation on the part of the Senior Advisor to the Partnership, the General Partner, or any Limited Partner, except to the extent that the Senior Advisor\'s continued status as a Managing Member of DCM may give rise to obligations under DCM\'s operating agreement or applicable law.
150: >
151: > **(c) Compensation and Carried Interest.** The Senior Advisor\'s carried interest entitlement shall be as set forth in amended Schedule A to this Agreement, as amended by Section 5.1 of this Amendment. The Senior Advisor\'s carried interest shall vest in accordance with the schedule set forth in Section 5.2 of this Amendment. The Senior Advisor shall not be entitled to any management fee, salary, bonus, or other compensation from the Partnership or DCM in respect of his role as Senior Advisor, except for the carried interest allocation described in this Section 8.06(c) and in Schedule A.\"
152: 
153: **[ARTICLE V --- AMENDMENT OF SCHEDULE A (CARRIED INTEREST ALLOCATION)]{.underline}**
154: 
155: **Section 5.1 --- Amended Schedule A.** Schedule A to the Agreement (Carried Interest Allocation) is hereby amended and restated in its entirety, effective as of the Amendment Effective Date, as set forth in Exhibit A attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference. For convenience of reference, the material terms of the amended carried interest allocation are summarized as follows:
156: 
157: The General Partner\'s aggregate incentive allocation shall remain at twenty percent (20%) of net new profits above the high-water mark, subject to the six percent (6%) annualized hurdle rate with full catch-up, as provided in the Agreement. This Amendment does not modify the aggregate incentive allocation or the hurdle rate and catch-up provisions. The internal allocation of the General Partner\'s twenty percent (20%) incentive allocation among the principals of DCM shall be as follows, effective as of the Amendment Effective Date:
158: 
159:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
160:   **Individual**       **Role**               **Pre-Amendment Allocation**                         **Post-Amendment Allocation**
161:   -------------------- ---------------------- ---------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------
162:   Marcus J. Whitmore   Senior Advisor         18% of GP\'s 20% (= 3.6% of net new fund profits)    9% of GP\'s 20% (= 1.8% of net new fund profits)
163: 
164:   Elaine R. Sato       Key Person, IC Chair   1.5% of GP\'s 20% (= 0.3% of net new fund profits)   7% of GP\'s 20% (= 1.4% of net new fund profits)
165: 
166:   Jonathan K. Huang    Key Person             0.5% of GP\'s 20% (= 0.1% of net new fund profits)   4% of GP\'s 20% (= 0.8% of net new fund profits)
167: 
168:   **Total**                                   **20% of GP\'s 20%**                                 **20% of GP\'s 20%**
169:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
170: 
171: For the avoidance of doubt, the GP-level total incentive allocation of twenty percent (20%) of net new fund profits above the high-water mark is unchanged by this Amendment. The reallocation set forth in this Section 5.1 affects only the internal allocation of the General Partner\'s incentive allocation among the individual principals of DCM and does not alter the aggregate economics payable by the Partnership to the General Partner.
172: 
173: **Section 5.2 --- Whitmore Carried Interest Vesting Schedule.** Marcus J. Whitmore\'s accrued and future carried interest entitlement under amended Schedule A shall vest in accordance with the following schedule:
174: 
175: > \(a\) **Immediate Vesting.** Fifty percent (50%) of the carried interest accrued to the account of Marcus J. Whitmore as of June 10, 2024 (the date of the Key Person Event) shall vest immediately as of the Amendment Effective Date. For purposes of this Section 5.2(a), the amount of accrued carried interest as of June 10, 2024 shall be determined by the Fund Administrator based on the net asset value of the Partnership as of such date, calculated in accordance with the valuation provisions of the Agreement.
176: >
177: > \(b\) **Ratable Vesting.** The remaining fifty percent (50%) of such accrued carried interest, together with any carried interest accruing on or after June 10, 2024 attributable to the Senior Advisor\'s nine percent (9%) allocation under amended Schedule A, shall vest ratably on a monthly basis over a period of thirty-six (36) months commencing on June 10, 2024. Specifically, one thirty-sixth (1/36th) of such carried interest shall vest on the 10th day of each calendar month following June 10, 2024, with the first installment having vested on July 10, 2024 and the final installment vesting on June 10, 2027. For the avoidance of doubt, installments that vested prior to the Amendment Effective Date pursuant to the foregoing schedule shall be deemed to have vested retroactively as of the applicable vesting date.
178: >
179: > \(c\) **Acceleration Upon Death.** In the event of the Senior Advisor\'s death during the thirty-six (36) month vesting period described in Section 5.2(b), all unvested carried interest of the Senior Advisor shall immediately vest in full as of the date of the Senior Advisor\'s death and shall be payable to the Senior Advisor\'s estate or designated beneficiary in accordance with the distribution provisions of the Agreement.
180: >
181: > \(d\) **Payment of Vested Carried Interest.** Vested carried interest of the Senior Advisor shall be payable in accordance with the distribution provisions of Section 6.03 of the Agreement, subject to the clawback provisions of Section 6.04 of the Agreement. Unvested carried interest shall not be distributable and shall remain subject to the vesting schedule set forth in this Section 5.2 until vested in accordance with its terms.
182: 
183: **Section 5.3 --- No Change to Management Fee.** For the avoidance of doubt, this Amendment does not modify the management fee of two percent (2.0%) of net asset value per annum, payable quarterly in advance, or any other fee provisions of the Agreement. The management fee shall continue to be calculated and payable in accordance with the terms of the Agreement as in effect immediately prior to the Amendment Effective Date.
184:

186: 
187: **Section 6.1 --- Conforming Amendment to Section 14.01.** Section 14.01 of the Agreement is hereby amended to add the following proviso at the end of the first sentence thereof:
188: 
189: > \"; *provided, further,* that any future amendment to Section 8.04 (Key Person Provisions), Section 8.05 (Investment Committee), Section 8.06 (Senior Advisor), or Schedule A (Carried Interest Allocation) of this Agreement (each as amended by the First Amendment to this Agreement dated as of August 26, 2024) shall require the written consent of Limited Partners holding not less than sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment), and in no event shall any such amendment be effected by the consent of the General Partner alone or by action of the Investment Committee.\"
