**[MEMORANDUM]{.underline}**
February 2, 2024
**TO:** Sandra M. Whitfield, General Counsel, Briarwood Family Office LLC Derek T. Calloway, Director of External Investments, Briarwood Family Office LLC
**FROM:** Theresa Kim, Lead Associate, Calderwood & Harkness LLP Owen Fischer, Working Associate, Calderwood & Harkness LLP
**SUPERVISED BY:** Pamela Cross, Partner, Funds & Asset Management, Calderwood & Harkness LLP
**RE:** Review and Analysis of Limited Partnership Agreement --- Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P.
Calderwood & Harkness LLP 425 Lexington Avenue New York, NY 10017
Right-click to update Table of Contents
**[I. Executive Summary]{.underline}**

The purpose of this memorandum is to provide Briarwood Family Office LLC (\"BFO\") with a comprehensive review and legal analysis of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. (the \"Fund\" or \"Fund IV\"), dated December 20, 2023 (the \"LPA\"), in connection with BFO\'s evaluation of a proposed limited partnership commitment of Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000) to Fund IV. This memorandum has been prepared at the request of BFO\'s General Counsel, Sandra M. Whitfield, and is intended to assist BFO\'s investment committee in its evaluation and approval process.

Fund IV is organized as a Delaware limited partnership, filed with the Delaware Secretary of State under Certificate Number LP-2023-08841. The Fund is managed by its general partner, Meridian Peak Capital Partners GP IV LLC (the \"GP\" or the \"General Partner\"), a Delaware limited liability company whose sole member is Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC (\"MPCA\"). The LPA is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, and the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act (\"DRULPA\") applies to the extent not expressly modified by the LPA.

Fund IV\'s stated investment strategy is to pursue value-add and opportunistic investments in North American commercial real estate, real estate operating companies, and asset management platforms. The Fund has established a target fund size of \$1,500,000,000 and a hard cap of \$1,750,000,000. The Fund anticipates holding its first close on or about April 30, 2024, with a final close deadline of October 31, 2024. BFO\'s proposed commitment of \$75,000,000 would represent approximately 5.0% of the target fund size and approximately 4.29% of the hard cap, positioning BFO as a meaningful but not anchor-level investor in the Fund.

MPCA was founded in 2011 by Conrad J. Ellsworth and Priya Narayan, who continue to serve as the firm\'s Co-Founders and Managing Partners. Mr. Ellsworth serves as Chief Executive Officer and Ms. Narayan serves as Chief Investment Officer. Since its founding, MPCA has raised three prior funds --- Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund I, L.P., Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund II, L.P., and Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund III, L.P. (collectively, \"Funds I--III\") --- aggregating approximately \$3.2 billion in committed capital. Fund IV represents a meaningful step-up in target fund size relative to the prior fund vintages, and the GP\'s ability to deploy capital effectively at this increased scale is a consideration that BFO should evaluate as part of its broader investment diligence, which is addressed separately in our concurrent PPM Summary & Risk Assessment Memorandum.

**Overall Assessment.** Following a thorough review of the LPA, it is our view that the agreement is broadly consistent with prevailing market terms for a mid-market real estate private equity fund of this size and strategy. The economic terms --- including a 1.75% management fee on committed capital during the Investment Period, a 20% carried interest above an 8% preferred return, and a European (whole-fund) waterfall --- are within the range we observe across comparable funds in the current market environment. However, several provisions in the LPA warrant attention and, in our recommendation, should be the subject of negotiation through a side letter to the LPA. These provisions relate primarily to (i) the absence of excuse and exclusion rights in the base LPA, (ii) the management fee structure, (iii) co-investment rights, (iv) most favored nation protections, (v) enhanced reporting obligations, (vi) key person provisions, (vii) transfer rights, and (viii) confidentiality carve-outs. Our detailed recommendations on each of these points are summarized at Section XV of this memorandum and discussed in the relevant sections throughout.

This memorandum should be read in conjunction with the separate PPM Summary & Risk Assessment Memorandum prepared by Calderwood & Harkness and delivered concurrently to BFO, which addresses the investment risk factors, market positioning, and track record analysis for Fund IV based on the Private Placement Memorandum dated December 15, 2023.
**[II. Defined Terms and Interpretive Provisions]{.underline}**

Throughout this memorandum, we use capitalized terms as defined in the LPA unless otherwise noted. For the convenience of BFO\'s review, we highlight below the key defined terms in the LPA that are most relevant to BFO\'s evaluation of the proposed commitment and that recur throughout this memorandum:

> • **\"Capital Commitment\"** means the total amount that a Limited Partner has committed to contribute to the Fund as set forth in such Limited Partner\'s Subscription Agreement. BFO\'s proposed Capital Commitment is \$75,000,000.

> • **\"Capital Account\"** means, with respect to each Partner, such Partner\'s capital account as maintained by the Fund in accordance with Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv) and the applicable provisions of the LPA.

> • **\"Carried Interest\"** means the performance-based allocation payable to the General Partner equal to 20% of the Fund\'s net profits in excess of the Preferred Return, as more fully described in Section V.C below.

> • **\"Commitment Period\"** (synonymous with \"Investment Period\") means the period beginning on the date of the Final Close and ending on the fourth anniversary thereof, during which the General Partner may make new Investments on behalf of the Fund. The Commitment Period is subject to early termination upon a Key Person Event as described in Section VIII.

> • **\"Fund Expenses\"** means the operating expenses of the Fund as described in Section 5.4 of the LPA, including audit fees, legal fees, administration fees, valuation expenses, insurance premiums, taxes, regulatory filing costs, broken-deal costs, and other customary expenses of the Fund. Fund Expenses are discussed in detail in Section V.D of this memorandum.

> • **\"Investment\"** means any investment made by the Fund in a Portfolio Company or other asset in furtherance of the Fund\'s investment strategy, including equity investments, debt investments, mezzanine investments, and joint venture interests.

> • **\"Net Asset Value\" or \"NAV\"** means the fair market value of the Fund\'s assets less the Fund\'s liabilities, as determined by the General Partner in accordance with the valuation provisions of the LPA (Section 9.3 of the LPA).

> • **\"Organizational Expenses\"** means the costs and expenses incurred in connection with the formation and organization of the Fund, including legal fees, regulatory filing fees, and printing costs, which are borne by the Fund subject to the cap described in Section V.D of this memorandum.
> • **\"Preferred Return\"** means the annual compounded preferred return of 8% per annum on contributed capital, as described in the waterfall provisions of the LPA.
> • **\"Subscription Agreement\"** means the subscription agreement entered into between the Fund and each Limited Partner in connection with such Limited Partner\'s admission to the Fund.

The LPA specifies that it is governed by, and to be construed in accordance with, the laws of the State of Delaware without regard to conflicts of law principles. The Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act (\"DRULPA\"), 6 Del. C. §§ 17-101 et seq., governs the Fund to the extent not expressly modified by the LPA. The LPA contains extensive interpretation clauses stating that, where the provisions of the LPA expressly address a subject also addressed by DRULPA, the LPA provisions are intended to supersede the default DRULPA provisions. This is standard practice in Delaware limited partnership agreements and permits the parties to contract around certain default provisions of DRULPA (as DRULPA expressly permits), including provisions governing distributions, voting, and dissolution.

The LPA makes reference to the Private Placement Memorandum dated December 15, 2023, which sets forth the Fund\'s offering terms, risk factors, and investment strategy in greater detail. Additionally, we note that the GP filed a Form D with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on January 2, 2024, reflecting the Fund\'s reliance on the private placement exemption under Regulation D of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. The PPM and Form D are addressed in our separate PPM Summary & Risk Assessment Memorandum.
**[III. Formation, Term, and Fund Structure]{.underline}**
**A. Formation and Structure**

Fund IV was formed as a Delaware limited partnership pursuant to a Certificate of Limited Partnership filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware under Certificate Number LP-2023-08841. The Fund\'s organizational structure is consistent with the standard structure employed by institutional real estate private equity funds and provides for a single general partner entity and multiple limited partners admitted through a private placement process.

The General Partner of the Fund is Meridian Peak Capital Partners GP IV LLC, a Delaware limited liability company formed for the sole purpose of serving as the general partner of Fund IV. The sole member of the GP is Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC (\"MPCA\"), the MPCA management company entity through which Messrs. Ellsworth and Narayan and the broader MPCA investment team operate. This single-layer GP structure --- in which the GP is a direct subsidiary of the management company --- is standard for funds of this type and does not raise any structural concerns from BFO\'s perspective. We note, however, that because the GP is a limited liability company with a single member, BFO should be aware that any change in control of MPCA (whether through admission of new members, transfer of membership interests, or otherwise) would effectively constitute a change of control of the GP. The LPA does not contain an express change-of-control provision with respect to MPCA, though the Key Person provisions (discussed in Section VIII below) provide some protection against departure of the principal investment professionals.

The Fund\'s registered agent in the State of Delaware is Beacon Statutory Services LLC, located at 1013 Centre Road, Wilmington, Delaware 19805. The General Partner\'s registered agent is also Beacon Statutory Services LLC at the same address. This is a standard commercial registered agent arrangement.

The GP maintains its principal office at 200 Clarendon Street, 42nd Floor, Boston, Massachusetts 02116, which is the primary business address of MPCA and the location from which Fund IV\'s investment activities are expected to be conducted.
The LPA identifies the following key service providers to the Fund:

> • **Fund Administrator:** Granite Ledger Fund Services LLC, located at 100 Summer Street, Suite 2700, Boston, Massachusetts 02110. The client relationship manager for Fund IV at Granite Ledger is Catherine J. Halloran. The fund administrator will be responsible for maintaining the Fund\'s books and records, processing capital calls and distributions, preparing quarterly financial statements, and coordinating with the Fund\'s auditor on annual audited financial statements. Granite Ledger is a well-established fund services provider with a significant presence in the real estate fund administration space.

> • **Fund Auditor:** Brockton Marsh & Associates LLP, located at 500 Boylston Street, 30th Floor, Boston, Massachusetts 02116. The engagement partner for Fund IV at Brockton Marsh is Neil A. Strickland. Brockton Marsh will be responsible for conducting the annual audit of the Fund\'s financial statements. While Brockton Marsh is a reputable regional audit firm, it is not among the Big Four accounting firms. BFO should assess whether the audit quality and market reputation of Brockton Marsh are consistent with BFO\'s expectations for a fund of this size, though we do not consider this to be a material concern from a legal perspective.

> • **Placement Agent:** Pinnacle Capital Markets LLC, located at 399 Park Avenue, 18th Floor, New York, New York 10022. The managing director responsible for the Fund IV placement is Roland S. Abernathy. Pinnacle was engaged by the GP pursuant to a placement agent engagement letter dated November 1, 2023. The placement agent\'s compensation and the offset provisions applicable to BFO are discussed in Section V.B of this memorandum.

> • **GP Counsel:** Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP, located at 1 Federal Street, Suite 3600, Boston, Massachusetts 02110. Ashford Crane serves as outside legal counsel to the General Partner and MPCA in connection with the formation, offering, and operation of Fund IV. We have been in communication with Harrison K. Drummond and Elaine C. Woodbury of Ashford Crane in connection with BFO\'s diligence process, and we anticipate that any side-letter negotiations will be conducted with Ashford Crane on behalf of the GP.
**B. Fund Term**

The LPA establishes a Fund term of ten (10) years commencing on the date of the Final Close. Assuming the Final Close occurs on October 31, 2024 (the stated deadline), the initial term of the Fund would expire on October 31, 2034.

The LPA further provides for two (2) one-year extension periods, each at the sole discretion of the General Partner, which would extend the Fund term to a maximum of twelve (12) years from the Final Close (i.e., potentially through October 31, 2036). Critically, the LPA does not require Limited Partner consent, LPAC approval, or any form of investor vote for either extension period. The GP may exercise each extension unilaterally by providing written notice to the Limited Partners at least 90 days prior to the expiration of the then-current term.

We note that the absence of any LP consent requirement for the extension periods is a less favorable term from BFO\'s perspective. While the first one-year extension at GP discretion is consistent with common market practice, there is an increasing trend in the institutional private equity market to require some form of investor consent for the second extension year --- typically either (i) approval by the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\"), or (ii) a vote of a majority or super-majority of Limited Partners. The rationale for such a requirement is that a second extension indicates potential difficulty in realizing the Fund\'s remaining portfolio, and LPs should have a voice in determining whether continued management by the GP is in the best interests of the Fund.

**Recommendation:** We recommend that BFO negotiate a side-letter provision requiring LPAC consent or, alternatively, the affirmative vote of Limited Partners holding a super-majority (66⅔% or 75%) of the aggregate Capital Commitments for the exercise of the second one-year extension. If LPAC consent is the mechanism employed, BFO should ensure it has adequate representation on or access to the LPAC, which is discussed further in Section XI.A below.

**C. Closings.** The LPA contemplates multiple closings for the admission of Limited Partners. The anticipated first close is April 30, 2024. The final close deadline is October 31, 2024, which is six (6) months following the anticipated first close. This six-month window between first and final close is standard for a fund of this size and provides the GP with adequate time to complete its fundraising activities.

Between the first close and the final close, the GP may hold one or more subsequent closings at its discretion to admit additional Limited Partners or to accept increased Capital Commitments from existing Limited Partners. The timing and number of subsequent closings are entirely within the GP\'s discretion, and no minimum or maximum number of closings is specified in the LPA.

The LPA includes an interest equalization mechanism for Limited Partners admitted at subsequent closings after the first close. Under this mechanism, subsequent-close LPs are required to contribute their pro rata share of all capital that has previously been called from first-close LPs, together with interest thereon at a rate equal to the Prime Rate plus 2.0% per annum, calculated from the date of each prior capital call through the date of the subsequent-close LP\'s admission. This interest equalization payment is intended to put subsequent-close LPs in the same economic position as if they had been admitted at the first close. The interest equalization payments are distributed to first-close LPs (and any previously-admitted subsequent-close LPs) in proportion to their respective shares of the prior capital calls. This is a standard provision and does not raise any concerns. Given that BFO is likely to be admitted at or near the first close, we do not anticipate significant interest equalization payments by BFO, though this should be confirmed during the subscription process.
**[IV. Capital Commitments and Capital Calls]{.underline}**
**A. Commitment Mechanics**

BFO\'s proposed Capital Commitment to Fund IV is \$75,000,000. The minimum Capital Commitment established in the LPA is \$10,000,000, subject to the GP\'s right to waive such minimum in its sole discretion. BFO\'s proposed commitment is well in excess of the minimum and, as noted above, represents approximately 5.0% of the target fund size and 4.29% of the hard cap.

Capital calls are issued by the General Partner by written notice delivered to each Limited Partner. The LPA requires that capital call notices be delivered no less than ten (10) business days prior to the funding date. Each capital call notice must specify (i) the aggregate amount being called from all Limited Partners, (ii) the individual Limited Partner\'s pro rata share of the capital call, (iii) the purpose of the capital call (i.e., whether for new investments, follow-on investments, Fund Expenses, or reserves), (iv) the funding date, and (v) wire transfer instructions for remittance. We note that the ten-business-day notice period is standard for institutional real estate funds and provides BFO with adequate time to process funding requests internally.

During the Investment Period, the GP may issue capital calls for any purpose related to the Fund\'s operations, including (i) the acquisition of new investments, (ii) follow-on investments in existing portfolio companies or assets, (iii) payment of Fund Expenses, (iv) establishment of reserves as determined by the GP, and (v) repayment of borrowings under any subscription credit facility.

Following the expiration or termination of the Investment Period, the GP\'s authority to issue capital calls is more limited. Post-Investment Period capital calls may be made only for the following purposes: (i) follow-on investments in existing portfolio companies or assets (subject to the 18-month limitation discussed in Section VI.A below), (ii) payment of Fund Expenses, (iii) establishment or maintenance of reserves, and (iv) repayment of borrowings under credit facilities. No capital may be called post-Investment Period for the purpose of making new investments.

The General Partner is required to fund its own GP Capital Commitment on a pari passu basis with the Limited Partners --- that is, the GP must fund its pro rata share of each capital call at the same time and in the same proportion as the Limited Partners. The GP\'s Capital Commitment is established in the LPA at 1.0% of aggregate Capital Commitments. At the target fund size of \$1,500,000,000, the GP\'s anticipated commitment would be \$15,000,000. This 1.0% GP commitment is standard for the market, though we note that some institutional investors prefer a GP commitment in the range of 1.5%--3.0% to ensure stronger alignment of interest between the GP and the LPs. BFO may wish to consider this point in its broader investment evaluation, though we do not recommend it as a side-letter negotiation item as it is unlikely to be modified for a single investor.
**B. Overcall and Recycling Provisions**

**Recycling.** The LPA permits the GP to recycle investment proceeds --- that is, to recall and reinvest capital that has been returned to Limited Partners from realized investments. Recycling is subject to two conditions: (i) the proceeds to be recycled must be derived from investments that were realized within twenty-four (24) months of their initial acquisition, and (ii) the aggregate amount of capital called from Limited Partners (inclusive of recycled capital) may not exceed 125% of total Capital Commitments. This 125% recycling cap means that, in addition to the initial \$75,000,000 Capital Commitment, BFO could potentially be required to fund up to an additional \$18,750,000 in recycled capital calls over the life of the Fund (i.e., \$75,000,000 × 125% = \$93,750,000 total, less \$75,000,000 initial commitment = \$18,750,000 maximum additional recycled calls). We note that the 125% recycling cap is on the higher end of the market range (which typically falls between 110% and 125%) and reflects the GP\'s desire for flexibility in reinvesting early-realization proceeds. While recycling can be beneficial to LPs by increasing the Fund\'s invested capital base and potentially enhancing returns, it also extends the period during which LPs\' capital is subject to call and increases the overall cash outflows from an LP\'s perspective.

**Overcall.** The LPA also contains an overcall provision that permits the GP to call additional capital from non-defaulting Limited Partners in the event that another Limited Partner defaults on a capital call obligation. Under the overcall provision, the GP may call up to 125% of a given non-defaulting LP\'s pro rata share of any capital call to cover a defaulting LP\'s shortfall. This provision creates potential overcall exposure for BFO --- in a default scenario, BFO could be required to fund up to 25% more than its pro rata share of a capital call. The overcall provision is standard in form, though the 125% overcall limit (rather than a lower threshold, such as 110%) is somewhat aggressive.

**Recommendation:** We recommend that BFO monitor both the recycling cap and the overcall provisions carefully. BFO should consider negotiating a side-letter limitation on overcall exposure, potentially capping BFO\'s aggregate overcall obligation at a lower threshold (e.g., 110% of BFO\'s pro rata share of any given capital call, or establishing an absolute dollar cap on aggregate overcall funding over the life of the Fund). We recognize that the GP may resist modifications to the overcall provision, as it serves a structural purpose in protecting the Fund against LP defaults, but the exposure should be flagged for BFO\'s investment committee.
**[V. Fund Economics]{.underline}**
**A. Management Fee**
The management fee structure under the LPA is divided into two tiers based on the Investment Period:

**During the Investment Period (Years 1--4):** The management fee is 1.75% per annum, calculated on the aggregate Capital Commitments of all Limited Partners. For BFO, based on a Capital Commitment of \$75,000,000, the annual management fee during the Investment Period would be:
Over the four-year Investment Period, BFO\'s cumulative management fee burden (absent any negotiated reduction) would be:

We note that the management fee during the Investment Period is calculated on committed capital (i.e., the full \$75,000,000), not on called or invested capital. This is standard practice for a fund of this size, but it means that BFO will be paying management fees on the full amount of its commitment from the outset, even though a significant portion of that commitment will remain uncalled during the early years of the Fund\'s life. This represents a real economic cost to BFO, as management fees on uncalled capital effectively reduce the net return on invested capital.

**Post-Investment Period (Years 5--10+):** Following the expiration of the Investment Period, the management fee steps down to 1.50% per annum, calculated on net invested capital (defined as the aggregate cost basis of unrealized investments, less any write-downs approved by the Fund\'s auditor). This post-Investment Period fee structure is favorable to LPs relative to a structure that continues to charge fees on committed capital, as the fee base will decline over time as investments are realized and capital is returned to LPs. The precise amount of the post-Investment Period management fee will vary depending on the pace of portfolio realizations and the extent of any write-downs, and therefore cannot be calculated with certainty at this time.

Management fees are payable quarterly in advance. The GP issues management fee invoices to the Fund (not directly to individual LPs), and management fees are funded through capital calls or, alternatively, through the use of a subscription credit facility, with such fees being allocated among the Limited Partners in proportion to their respective Capital Commitments.
**Proposed Side-Letter Negotiation on Management Fee.** We recommend that BFO negotiate a reduction in the management fee through a side letter, as follows:
> • **Investment Period fee:** Reduce from 1.75% to 1.50% per annum on committed capital (a 25 basis point reduction)
> • **Post-Investment Period fee:** Reduce from 1.50% to 1.25% per annum on net invested capital (a 25 basis point reduction)
The economic impact of the proposed reduction during the Investment Period would be as follows:
> • Negotiated annual fee: \$75,000,000 × 1.50% = \$1,125,000 per year
> • Cumulative savings over the four-year Investment Period: \$187,500 × 4 = \$750,000

The post-Investment Period savings would be variable and dependent on the level of net invested capital, but would represent a consistent 25 basis point benefit to BFO throughout the remaining life of the Fund.

We believe a 25 basis point reduction is a reasonable and achievable negotiating objective for a commitment of BFO\'s size. At \$75,000,000, BFO is a meaningful investor representing 5.0% of the target fund size, and fee reductions of this magnitude are commonly granted to investors at or above this commitment level in the current market environment. We anticipate that the GP may counter at a smaller reduction, such as 15 basis points (resulting in rates of 1.60% during the Investment Period and 1.35% post-Investment Period), and we would recommend that BFO be prepared to accept such a counter if it is the GP\'s final position on this point.
**B. Placement Agent Fee Offset**

Pinnacle Capital Markets LLC, the Fund\'s placement agent, is entitled to receive a placement fee equal to 1.0% of the Capital Commitment of each Limited Partner introduced to the Fund through Pinnacle\'s placement activities. Based on BFO\'s proposed Capital Commitment of \$75,000,000, the placement fee attributable to BFO would be:

The LPA provides that 100% of placement fees incurred with respect to a given Limited Partner are to be offset against the management fees otherwise payable by that Limited Partner. This means that the \$750,000 placement fee attributable to BFO would be credited against BFO\'s management fee obligations, reducing BFO\'s net management fee burden by \$750,000 over the offset period. We have confirmed that this 100% offset provision is contained in the base LPA itself (Section 5.2(d)) and is not limited to investors who have negotiated a specific side-letter provision.

We note, however, that the LPA does not specify the precise mechanics of the placement fee offset --- for example, whether the offset is applied ratably over the Investment Period (i.e., \$750,000 ÷ 4 years = \$187,500 per year), applied in full against the first management fee payment, or applied in some other manner. This ambiguity should be clarified.

**Recommendation:** We recommend that BFO\'s side letter explicitly confirm the 100% offset and specify the timing and mechanics of the offset application. Our preference would be for the offset to be applied as a dollar-for-dollar reduction to the first management fee payments until the \$750,000 offset is fully exhausted, as this would provide the maximum economic benefit to BFO through early recovery of the placement fee amount.
**C. Carried Interest / Performance Allocation**

The General Partner is entitled to a carried interest (referred to in the LPA as the \"Performance Allocation\") equal to 20% of the Fund\'s net profits in excess of the Preferred Return. The carried interest is the primary performance-based compensation mechanism for the GP and its investment professionals.
The carried interest is calculated and distributed in accordance with a whole-fund European-style distribution waterfall, which operates as follows:

**Step 1 --- Return of Contributed Capital.** All distributions are first applied to return to the Limited Partners the aggregate amount of capital contributed by such Limited Partners to the Fund, including capital attributable to recycled investments. This provision ensures that no carried interest is payable to the GP until LPs have received a full return of their invested capital across the entire Fund portfolio.

No attorney-client relationship shall arise between the Firm and any such individual by virtue of this Engagement Letter or the Firm\'s performance of services hereunder, and the interests of any such individual may not necessarily be aligned with the interests of Pellegrino as an entity in all respects.

37: **[3. Scope of Services]{.underline}**
38: 
39: Calderwood & Harkness will provide legal services to Pellegrino in connection with the co-investment described above. 41: **3.1 Review and Negotiation of Co-Investment Documentation**
42: 
43: Calderwood & Harkness will undertake the review, analysis, markup, and negotiation of the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P. (the \"Co-Invest LPA\"). We understand that the initial draft of the Co-Invest LPA has been prepared by Hartwell Velmoran & Pratt LLP, counsel to the sponsor, Ridgeline Equity Management LLC (the \"Sponsor\"). Our review will focus on the terms and provisions of the Co-Invest LPA that are material to Pellegrino\'s rights, obligations, and economic interests as a limited partner in the Co-Invest Vehicle, including but not limited to provisions relating to capital contributions and capital calls, distributions and distribution waterfalls, management fees and carried interest, clawback obligations, excuse and exclusion mechanisms, indemnification and exculpation of the general partner, transfer restrictions, dissolution and winding up, reporting and audit rights, key person events, and amendments and waivers.
44: 
45: In addition, Calderwood & Harkness will draft and negotiate a side letter agreement (the \"Side Letter\") between Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest GP LLC (the \"Co-Invest GP\") and Pellegrino. The Side Letter is intended to contain investor-specific protections and additional rights for the benefit of Pellegrino, including the following:
46: 
47: > \(a\) most-favored-nation (\"MFN\") rights, entitling Pellegrino to elect to receive the benefit of any more favorable term or right granted to any other limited partner of the Co-Invest Vehicle in a side letter or other agreement, subject to customary exclusions;
48: >
49: > \(b\) a right to a seat on the limited partner advisory committee (\"LPAC\") of the Co-Invest Vehicle, or, if no LPAC is formed for the Co-Invest Vehicle, a right to a seat on the LPAC of Ridgeline Fund IV, to the extent such rights are available;

51: > \(c\) enhanced reporting rights, including quarterly unaudited financial statements, annual audited financial statements, and ad hoc reporting on material events affecting the Co-Invest Vehicle or the Acquisition;

53: > \(d\) ESG reporting covenants, requiring the Sponsor or the Co-Invest GP to provide Pellegrino with periodic environmental, social, and governance reporting with respect to Clarion and the portfolio, consistent with Pellegrino\'s own ESG reporting framework and investor disclosure obligations;

55: > \(e\) future co-investment allocation rights, entitling Pellegrino to a right of first offer or similar priority allocation right with respect to future co-investment opportunities originated by the Sponsor or Ridgeline Equity Management LLC in connection with Ridgeline Fund IV or any successor fund; and

57: > \(f\) excuse and exclusion protections, permitting Pellegrino to be excused from participation in, or excluded from the costs of, any investment or activity that would cause Pellegrino to violate applicable law, regulation, or any provision of its organizational documents or constituent fund documentation.

63: **3.2 Tax Analysis and Coordination**
64: 
65: Calderwood & Harkness will prepare an internal tax analysis memorandum (the \"Tax Memorandum\") addressing the federal income tax implications of the co-investment structure for Pellegrino. The Tax Memorandum will address, among other matters, the following topics:
66: 
67: > \(a\) classification of the Co-Invest Vehicle as a partnership for federal income tax purposes under Subchapter K of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the \"Code\"), and the implications of its organization as a Delaware limited partnership;
68: >
69: > \(b\) unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") considerations, to the extent relevant to Pellegrino or its underlying investors, including analysis of potential UBTI generated through the use of acquisition indebtedness or other debt-financed structures in connection with the Acquisition;
70: >
71: > \(c\) analysis of the Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act of 1980 (\"FIRPTA\"), to the extent Clarion\'s assets include U.S. real property interests within the meaning of Section 897 of the Code;
72: >
73: > \(d\) the allocation methodology under Section 704(b) of the Code (economic effect and substantiality) and Section 704(c) of the Code (contributed property and reverse Section 704(c) allocations), as reflected in the Co-Invest LPA;
74: >
75: > \(e\) carried interest treatment under Section 1061 of the Code, including the three-year holding period requirement applicable to certain partnership interests held in connection with the performance of services; and
76: >
77: > \(f\) state and local tax nexus analysis, with a particular focus on the states of Delaware, Florida, Tennessee, and New York, addressing potential filing obligations, withholding requirements, and composite return elections.

79: In connection with the foregoing, Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with Pellegrino\'s independent tax and accounting advisor, Whitfield Greer & Associates LLP (\"Whitfield Greer\"), and specifically with Robert K. Anand, Engagement Partner at Whitfield Greer, regarding their independent tax structuring analysis, Schedule K-1 delivery mechanics and timing, and any other tax-related matters relevant to Pellegrino\'s participation in the Co-Invest Vehicle. Calderwood & Harkness\'s tax analysis is intended to supplement, and not to replace, the independent advice and analysis provided by Whitfield Greer.

91: > \(d\) an officer\'s certificate or secretary\'s certificate of Pellegrino, certifying as to the authority of the person or persons executing the transaction documents on behalf of Pellegrino, the incumbency of such person or persons, and the authenticity of the organizational documents of Pellegrino delivered in connection with the closing.

Cheng, Partner, and Meredith L. Tanaka, Associate, at Hartwell Velmoran & Pratt LLP, and reporting on the status of such negotiations to Pellegrino; and

Dear Ms. Voss:
**[1. Introduction and Purpose]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Pellegrino Capital Group LLC (\"Pellegrino\" or \"PCG\"), a Delaware limited liability company, in connection with Pellegrino\'s proposed Twenty-Five Million Dollar (\$25,000,000) co-investment alongside Ridgeline Equity Partners Fund IV, L.P. (\"Ridgeline Fund IV\") in Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P. (the \"Co-Invest Vehicle\"), a Delaware limited partnership formed for the purpose of facilitating co-investment alongside Ridgeline Fund IV.

As we understand the transaction, the Co-Invest Vehicle will co-invest alongside Ridgeline Fund IV in the equity of Clarion Holdings Acquisition Corp. (\"AcquisitionCo\"), a Delaware corporation formed to acquire one hundred percent (100%) of the equity interests of Clarion Hospitality Holdings, Inc. (\"Clarion\"), an integrated hospitality asset management platform headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee. The acquisition of Clarion by AcquisitionCo (the \"Acquisition\") is expected to be structured as a leveraged buyout, with the equity capitalization of AcquisitionCo funded through commitments from Ridgeline Fund IV, the Co-Invest Vehicle, and any other co-investment vehicles or equity participants designated by the sponsor.

Pellegrino\'s \$25,000,000 commitment to the Co-Invest Vehicle represents approximately thirty-three and one-third percent (33.33%) of the Co-Invest Vehicle\'s aggregate Seventy-Five Million Dollar (\$75,000,000) in commitments, and approximately ten percent (10.0%) of the total Two Hundred Fifty Million Dollar (\$250,000,000) equity capitalization of AcquisitionCo. We understand that the balance of the equity capitalization will be comprised of commitments from Ridgeline Fund IV and, potentially, other co-investment participants alongside the Co-Invest Vehicle.

This letter agreement (the \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions governing Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement by Pellegrino, including the scope of legal services to be provided, attorney staffing, fees and billing arrangements, conflict of interest disclosures, confidentiality obligations, and other terms and conditions of the attorney-client relationship. We ask that you review this Engagement Letter carefully and confirm Pellegrino\'s agreement to these terms by executing and returning a copy as described in Section 13 below.
**[2. Client Identification]{.underline}**

The client in this engagement is Pellegrino Capital Group LLC, and no other person or entity. Calderwood & Harkness\'s duties of loyalty, confidentiality, and professional responsibility in connection with this matter run solely to Pellegrino Capital Group LLC as an entity.

Calderwood & Harkness does not represent, and shall not be deemed to represent, any affiliate, subsidiary, member, manager, officer, director, employee, or agent of Pellegrino individually in connection with this engagement, including without limitation Marco A. Pellegrino (Founder & Managing Member) or Daniella R. Pellegrino (Chief Financial Officer), unless a separate written engagement agreement is entered into between the Firm and such individual expressly establishing such a representation. No attorney-client relationship shall arise between the Firm and any such individual by virtue of this Engagement Letter or the Firm\'s performance of services hereunder, and the interests of any such individual may not necessarily be aligned with the interests of Pellegrino as an entity in all respects.

The primary client contact for this engagement shall be Adriana Voss, Vice President & General Counsel, Pellegrino Capital Group LLC. Unless otherwise directed in writing, all substantive communications, deliverables, and invoices will be directed to Ms. Voss. We understand that Ms. Voss is authorized to provide instructions, approve work product, and make decisions on behalf of Pellegrino in connection with this engagement, subject to such internal approvals as may be required under Pellegrino\'s organizational documents and governance procedures.
**[3. Scope of Services]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will provide legal services to Pellegrino in connection with the co-investment described above. The scope of our engagement is set forth in greater detail in Sections 3.1 through 3.5 below. We will endeavor to keep Pellegrino informed of material developments and to seek instructions on significant issues as they arise during the course of the representation.
**3.1 Review and Negotiation of Co-Investment Documentation**

Calderwood & Harkness will undertake the review, analysis, markup, and negotiation of the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P. (the \"Co-Invest LPA\"). We understand that the initial draft of the Co-Invest LPA has been prepared by Hartwell Velmoran & Pratt LLP, counsel to the sponsor, Ridgeline Equity Management LLC (the \"Sponsor\"). Our review will focus on the terms and provisions of the Co-Invest LPA that are material to Pellegrino\'s rights, obligations, and economic interests as a limited partner in the Co-Invest Vehicle, including but not limited to provisions relating to capital contributions and capital calls, distributions and distribution waterfalls, management fees and carried interest, clawback obligations, excuse and exclusion mechanisms, indemnification and exculpation of the general partner, transfer restrictions, dissolution and winding up, reporting and audit rights, key person events, and amendments and waivers.

In addition, Calderwood & Harkness will draft and negotiate a side letter agreement (the \"Side Letter\") between Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest GP LLC (the \"Co-Invest GP\") and Pellegrino. The Side Letter is intended to contain investor-specific protections and additional rights for the benefit of Pellegrino, including the following:

> \(a\) most-favored-nation (\"MFN\") rights, entitling Pellegrino to elect to receive the benefit of any more favorable term or right granted to any other limited partner of the Co-Invest Vehicle in a side letter or other agreement, subject to customary exclusions;

> \(b\) a right to a seat on the limited partner advisory committee (\"LPAC\") of the Co-Invest Vehicle, or, if no LPAC is formed for the Co-Invest Vehicle, a right to a seat on the LPAC of Ridgeline Fund IV, to the extent such rights are available;

> \(c\) enhanced reporting rights, including quarterly unaudited financial statements, annual audited financial statements, and ad hoc reporting on material events affecting the Co-Invest Vehicle or the Acquisition;

> \(d\) ESG reporting covenants, requiring the Sponsor or the Co-Invest GP to provide Pellegrino with periodic environmental, social, and governance reporting with respect to Clarion and the portfolio, consistent with Pellegrino\'s own ESG reporting framework and investor disclosure obligations;

> \(e\) future co-investment allocation rights, entitling Pellegrino to a right of first offer or similar priority allocation right with respect to future co-investment opportunities originated by the Sponsor or Ridgeline Equity Management LLC in connection with Ridgeline Fund IV or any successor fund; and

> \(f\) excuse and exclusion protections, permitting Pellegrino to be excused from participation in, or excluded from the costs of, any investment or activity that would cause Pellegrino to violate applicable law, regulation, or any provision of its organizational documents or constituent fund documentation.

Calderwood & Harkness will also review, negotiate, and complete a subscription agreement (the \"Subscription Agreement\") for Pellegrino\'s Twenty-Five Million Dollar (\$25,000,000) limited partnership interest in the Co-Invest Vehicle, ensuring that the representations, warranties, and covenants contained therein are accurate and appropriate in the context of Pellegrino\'s organizational and regulatory status.

Finally, Calderwood & Harkness will assist Pellegrino with the completion of the investor questionnaire customarily required in connection with subscriptions of this nature, including representations and certifications relating to tax status (including U.S. tax-exempt status, if applicable), the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), the Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (\"FATCA\") and the Common Reporting Standard (\"CRS\"), the Office of Foreign Assets Control (\"OFAC\") sanctions programs, and anti-money laundering (\"AML\") requirements.
**3.2 Tax Analysis and Coordination**

Calderwood & Harkness will prepare an internal tax analysis memorandum (the \"Tax Memorandum\") addressing the federal income tax implications of the co-investment structure for Pellegrino. The Tax Memorandum will address, among other matters, the following topics:

> \(a\) classification of the Co-Invest Vehicle as a partnership for federal income tax purposes under Subchapter K of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the \"Code\"), and the implications of its organization as a Delaware limited partnership;

> \(b\) unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") considerations, to the extent relevant to Pellegrino or its underlying investors, including analysis of potential UBTI generated through the use of acquisition indebtedness or other debt-financed structures in connection with the Acquisition;

> \(c\) analysis of the Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act of 1980 (\"FIRPTA\"), to the extent Clarion\'s assets include U.S. real property interests within the meaning of Section 897 of the Code;

> \(d\) the allocation methodology under Section 704(b) of the Code (economic effect and substantiality) and Section 704(c) of the Code (contributed property and reverse Section 704(c) allocations), as reflected in the Co-Invest LPA;

> \(e\) carried interest treatment under Section 1061 of the Code, including the three-year holding period requirement applicable to certain partnership interests held in connection with the performance of services; and

> \(f\) state and local tax nexus analysis, with a particular focus on the states of Delaware, Florida, Tennessee, and New York, addressing potential filing obligations, withholding requirements, and composite return elections.

In connection with the foregoing, Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with Pellegrino\'s independent tax and accounting advisor, Whitfield Greer & Associates LLP (\"Whitfield Greer\"), and specifically with Robert K. Anand, Engagement Partner at Whitfield Greer, regarding their independent tax structuring analysis, Schedule K-1 delivery mechanics and timing, and any other tax-related matters relevant to Pellegrino\'s participation in the Co-Invest Vehicle. Calderwood & Harkness\'s tax analysis is intended to supplement, and not to replace, the independent advice and analysis provided by Whitfield Greer.
**3.3 Closing Deliverables**
Calderwood & Harkness will prepare or coordinate the following deliverables in connection with the closing of Pellegrino\'s investment in the Co-Invest Vehicle:

> \(a\) a comprehensive closing checklist identifying all deliverables required in connection with the closing, the party responsible for preparation or delivery of each item, the applicable deadline or target date, and the current status of each item;

> \(b\) a funds flow memorandum detailing the movement of Pellegrino\'s Twenty-Five Million Dollar (\$25,000,000) capital contribution from Pellegrino\'s designated bank account, through the escrow account maintained by Continental Fiduciary Services, Inc. (the \"Escrow Agent\") pursuant to the terms of the applicable escrow agreement, to the Co-Invest Vehicle\'s account, and onward to AcquisitionCo in connection with the consummation of the Acquisition;

> \(c\) a legal opinion letter addressed to the Co-Invest GP, in customary form and substance, regarding the due organization, valid existence, and good standing of Pellegrino; the authorization by all necessary action of Pellegrino\'s execution, delivery, and performance of the Co-Invest LPA, the Side Letter, and the Subscription Agreement; and the enforceability of Pellegrino\'s obligations under such documents against Pellegrino in accordance with their respective terms, in each case subject to customary assumptions, qualifications, and exceptions; and

> \(d\) an officer\'s certificate or secretary\'s certificate of Pellegrino, certifying as to the authority of the person or persons executing the transaction documents on behalf of Pellegrino, the incumbency of such person or persons, and the authenticity of the organizational documents of Pellegrino delivered in connection with the closing.
**3.4 General Advisory**
In addition to the specific tasks described above, Calderwood & Harkness will provide the following general advisory services in connection with the co-investment:

> \(a\) preparation of internal memoranda summarizing the key terms of the Co-Invest LPA, identifying issues and risks, and setting forth our recommendations for Pellegrino\'s review and approval prior to the commencement of negotiations or the acceptance of proposed terms;

> \(b\) internal tracking of negotiation points and their resolutions as between Calderwood & Harkness (on behalf of Pellegrino) and Hartwell Velmoran & Pratt LLP (on behalf of the Sponsor), including communications with Douglas W. Cheng, Partner, and Meredith L. Tanaka, Associate, at Hartwell Velmoran & Pratt LLP, and reporting on the status of such negotiations to Pellegrino; and
> \(c\) general legal advice and counsel to Pellegrino in connection with the co-investment as may be reasonably requested by Pellegrino from time to time during the course of this engagement.
**3.5 Limitations on Scope**

The scope of Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement is limited to the services described in Sections 3.1 through 3.4 above. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Pellegrino should be aware of the following limitations:

> \(a\) Calderwood & Harkness is **not** engaged to provide legal advice with respect to the underlying Acquisition of Clarion, including but not limited to the conduct of business, legal, financial, or operational due diligence on Clarion\'s business, assets, liabilities, contracts, regulatory compliance, intellectual property, or workforce matters. Pellegrino should satisfy itself, through its own due diligence or through the diligence conducted by the Sponsor, that the Acquisition and the underlying business of Clarion meet Pellegrino\'s investment criteria.

> \(b\) Calderwood & Harkness is **not** engaged to provide legal advice with respect to the credit facility or any other debt financing provided by Pinnacle National Bank, N.A. or any other lender in connection with the Acquisition, including the terms of any credit agreement, security agreement, guarantee, or intercreditor arrangement.

> \(c\) Calderwood & Harkness is **not** engaged to advise on the interests, rights, or obligations of any party other than Pellegrino, including the Sponsor, the Co-Invest GP, Ridgeline Fund IV, AcquisitionCo, Clarion, any seller, or any other co-investor in the Co-Invest Vehicle (including without limitation Brindoval Growth Capital Fund II, L.P., to the extent it is a participant).

> \(d\) Calderwood & Harkness is **not** engaged to provide tax advice as a substitute for the engagement of Whitfield Greer & Associates LLP. Any tax analysis provided by Calderwood & Harkness is supplemental in nature and is intended to inform Pellegrino\'s understanding of the tax aspects of the co-investment structure; such analysis should be reviewed in conjunction with, and does not supersede, the independent advice of Whitfield Greer & Associates LLP.

> \(e\) Calderwood & Harkness does **not** represent Pellegrino in connection with any regulatory filings, including but not limited to filings under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, or filings with any state regulatory authority, unless separately agreed in writing.

If the scope of our engagement needs to be expanded or modified at any point, we will discuss the matter with you and, if appropriate, confirm any revised scope in a supplemental engagement letter or amendment to this Engagement Letter.
**[4. Staffing]{.underline}**
The following attorneys have been assigned to this engagement and will be the primary members of the Calderwood & Harkness team working on this matter:

**Responsible Partner:** Nicholas Stern, Partner, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Mr. Stern will have overall responsibility for the engagement, including client relationship management, strategic direction, and supervision of all work product produced by the engagement team. Mr. Stern will serve as the primary point of contact for Pellegrino on significant issues, negotiations, and escalation matters.

**Billing Partner:** Graham Sutherland, Partner, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Mr. Sutherland will serve as the billing partner for purposes of rate approvals, billing administration, and invoice review. Mr. Sutherland will also be available to provide substantive legal advice as needed on particular issues within his areas of expertise.

**Lead Associate:** Owen Fischer, Associate, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Mr. Fischer will serve as the day-to-day lead on document review, drafting, markup, and negotiation of the Co-Invest LPA, Side Letter, Subscription Agreement, and related transaction documents. Mr. Fischer will also be responsible for coordinating with Hartwell Velmoran & Pratt LLP on document exchanges and turn schedules.

**Working Associate:** Stephen Adler, Associate, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Mr. Adler will support Mr. Fischer in connection with legal research, preparation of the closing checklist, drafting of the funds flow memorandum and certificates, and coordination of closing mechanics.

Additional attorneys, paralegals, or other professional staff may be assigned to this engagement from time to time as the needs of the matter require. We will endeavor to staff this matter efficiently and to avoid unnecessary duplication of effort. Pellegrino will be notified of any material changes in staffing, including the substitution of any of the named attorneys listed above.
**[5. Fees and Billing]{.underline}**
**5.1 Hourly Rates**

This engagement will be billed on an hourly basis at Calderwood & Harkness\'s standard rates for the attorneys and professional staff assigned to the matter. The current rates for 2025 are as follows:
**Timekeeper Category**             **2025 Hourly Rate Range**
Partners                            \$1,050 -- \$1,250 per hour
Associates                          \$550 -- \$825 per hour
Paralegals                          \$350 -- \$450 per hour

The specific rate for each timekeeper will fall within the applicable range based on the individual\'s seniority and experience level. We will provide Pellegrino with a schedule of the specific rates applicable to each attorney and paralegal assigned to this matter upon request.

Rates are subject to periodic adjustment, typically effective January 1 of each calendar year. Calderwood & Harkness will notify Pellegrino in advance of any rate changes. Any adjusted rates will apply to services rendered on or after the effective date of the adjustment.
**5.2 Fee Estimate**

Based on the anticipated scope of work described in Section 3 above and our experience with comparable co-investment transactions, Calderwood & Harkness estimates that total legal fees for this engagement will be in the range of One Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$175,000) to Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$250,000), exclusive of disbursements and out-of-pocket expenses. This estimate assumes a transaction of moderate complexity, involving two to three rounds of negotiation on the Co-Invest LPA and Side Letter, and a closing timeline of approximately six to eight weeks from the date of this Engagement Letter.

This estimate is provided for budgeting and planning purposes only and does not constitute a cap, ceiling, fixed fee, or guarantee of total fees. Actual fees will depend on a number of factors, including the complexity and duration of negotiations with Hartwell Velmoran & Pratt LLP, the number and extent of drafts and revisions to the transaction documents, the scope and nature of issues that arise during the course of the engagement, and the extent of Pellegrino\'s requests for additional analysis or advisory services. If it appears at any point that our fees are likely to materially exceed this estimate, we will promptly notify Pellegrino and discuss appropriate steps.

Calderwood & Harkness will endeavor to keep Pellegrino informed of the status of accrued fees as the matter progresses, and is prepared to provide interim fee estimates or budget updates upon request.
**5.3 Expenses and Disbursements**

In addition to legal fees, Pellegrino will be responsible for the reimbursement of out-of-pocket costs and disbursements reasonably incurred by Calderwood & Harkness in connection with this engagement. Such costs and disbursements may include, without limitation, the following:
> \(a\) filing fees, including fees for filings with the Delaware Secretary of State, requests for certificates of good standing or certificates of status, and similar governmental charges;
> \(b\) messenger and courier charges;
> \(c\) travel expenses, including airfare, hotel, ground transportation, and meals, if travel is required in connection with the engagement (which we do not currently anticipate);
> \(d\) charges for outside photocopying, printing, or binding services in excess of routine in-office copying;
> \(e\) fees for third-party vendors, including document management platforms, virtual data room access fees, and similar services; and
> \(f\) long-distance telephone and videoconference charges, to the extent separately billable.

Filing fees for Delaware Secretary of State filings or good standing certificates will be billed at cost, without markup. Other disbursements will generally be billed at cost or at Calderwood & Harkness\'s standard internal charge rates, as applicable.
**5.4 Invoicing and Payment**

Invoices for fees and disbursements will be rendered on a monthly basis and are due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of receipt. Each invoice will contain reasonable detail regarding the services rendered, including the identity of the attorney or professional performing the work, the date on which the services were performed, a description of the services rendered, and the amount of time expended.

If Pellegrino has any questions regarding an invoice or wishes to discuss any charge, we encourage you to contact Mr. Sutherland or Mr. Stern promptly so that any concerns can be addressed in a timely manner. Calderwood & Harkness reserves the right to charge interest on past-due balances at a rate of one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is less, on any amounts remaining unpaid for more than sixty (60) days following the date of the applicable invoice.
**[6. Conflicts of Interest]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness has conducted a conflicts check in connection with this engagement in accordance with the Firm\'s standard conflict clearance procedures. Based on that review, the Firm is not aware of any conflict of interest that would prevent it from representing Pellegrino in this matter under the applicable Florida Rules of Professional Conduct.

Specifically, Calderwood & Harkness does not currently represent, and has not in the recent past represented, any of the following entities in connection with this transaction or any related matter: Ridgeline Equity Partners Fund IV, L.P.; Ridgeline Equity Management LLC; Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest GP LLC; Clarion Hospitality Holdings, Inc.; Clarion Holdings Acquisition Corp.; Brindoval Growth Capital Fund II, L.P.; Pinnacle National Bank, N.A.; or any of their respective affiliates, general partners, managing members, or portfolio companies, insofar as such representation would relate to the subject matter of this engagement.

Pellegrino acknowledges and agrees that Calderwood & Harkness is a large, multi-office law firm with a diverse client base, and that the Firm may from time to time represent other clients whose interests may be adverse to Pellegrino in matters that are unrelated to this engagement. Nothing in this Engagement Letter shall be construed to preclude or restrict Calderwood & Harkness from accepting or continuing any such representation, provided that (i) the matter in question does not involve the same or a substantially related matter as this engagement, and (ii) such representation does not create a direct and impermissible conflict of interest with respect to the Firm\'s obligations to Pellegrino under this Engagement Letter and the applicable Rules of Professional Conduct.

In the event that a conflict of interest arises during the course of this engagement, Calderwood & Harkness will promptly notify Pellegrino of the conflict and discuss appropriate steps to address it. Such steps may include, depending on the nature and severity of the conflict, the implementation of an ethical wall or information barrier within the Firm, the obtaining of an informed written waiver from the affected parties, or, if the conflict cannot be adequately resolved, the withdrawal of Calderwood & Harkness from the representation in accordance with Section 9 of this Engagement Letter.
**[7. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will maintain the confidentiality of all information provided by Pellegrino, or obtained by the Firm on behalf of Pellegrino, in connection with this engagement. This obligation is consistent with, and in addition to, the Firm\'s duties of confidentiality under the applicable Florida Rules of Professional Conduct (including Rule 4-1.6) and other applicable law. All confidential information received from Pellegrino will be disclosed within the Firm only to those attorneys, paralegals, and staff who have a need to know such information in connection with the performance of services under this engagement.

Pellegrino hereby authorizes Calderwood & Harkness to disclose confidential information to the following parties to the extent reasonably necessary in connection with the negotiation and closing of the co-investment:
> \(a\) Hartwell Velmoran & Pratt LLP, counsel to the Sponsor, in connection with the negotiation of the Co-Invest LPA, Side Letter, Subscription Agreement, and related transaction documents;

> \(b\) Aldridge Mayer Stevens LLP, counsel to the seller(s) of Clarion, to the extent that the exchange of information with seller\'s counsel is reasonably required in connection with the co-investment closing process;
> \(c\) Whitfield Greer & Associates LLP, Pellegrino\'s independent tax and accounting advisor, in connection with the tax analysis and coordination described in Section 3.2 above; and
> \(d\) Continental Fiduciary Services, Inc., the Escrow Agent, in connection with the preparation and execution of the funds flow memorandum and the mechanics of capital contribution funding.

This authorization is limited to disclosures that are reasonably necessary for the purposes described above and does not constitute a general waiver of Pellegrino\'s right to confidentiality. Calderwood & Harkness will use reasonable efforts to ensure that any such disclosures are made in a manner that preserves applicable privileges, including the attorney-client privilege and the work product doctrine, to the greatest extent practicable.
**[8. Document Retention]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will maintain all files, documents, correspondence, memoranda, work product, and other materials related to this engagement (collectively, \"Engagement Files\") in accordance with the Firm\'s document retention policy, as in effect from time to time. The Engagement Files will include both physical and electronic files.

Upon completion or termination of this engagement, the Firm will retain the Engagement Files for a period of not less than seven (7) years, or such longer period as may be required by applicable professional standards, rules, or regulations. After the expiration of the applicable retention period, and upon reasonable advance written notice to Pellegrino (which notice shall be directed to the last known address of the primary client contact), Calderwood & Harkness may destroy the Engagement Files in accordance with its standard retention and destruction procedures. Pellegrino may request the return or transfer of original documents at any time during the retention period, and the Firm will accommodate such requests within a reasonable time, subject to the Firm\'s right to retain copies for its own records and any applicable lien rights.
**[9. Termination]{.underline}**

Either party may terminate this engagement at any time, with or without cause, upon written notice to the other party. Calderwood & Harkness\'s right to terminate is subject to the Firm\'s professional obligations, including the duty to provide reasonable notice and to avoid prejudice to the client\'s interests, and to any applicable rules governing the withdrawal of counsel.

In the event of termination by either party, Pellegrino will remain responsible for the payment of all fees and expenses incurred by Calderwood & Harkness through the effective date of termination, and all outstanding invoices shall become due and payable upon termination.

Upon termination, Calderwood & Harkness will cooperate with Pellegrino in the orderly transition and transfer of the matter to successor counsel designated by Pellegrino, including the timely delivery of all Engagement Files, work product, and other materials in the Firm\'s possession that are necessary for successor counsel to continue the representation, subject to any applicable lien rights of the Firm and any applicable court rules or professional obligations. Pellegrino agrees to execute any authorizations or consents reasonably necessary to facilitate such transfer.
**[10. Governing Law]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Florida, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. Any dispute arising out of or relating to this Engagement Letter or the services provided hereunder shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Miami-Dade County, Florida, and each party hereby consents to the personal jurisdiction of such courts.
**[11. Limitation of Liability]{.underline}**

To the fullest extent permitted by applicable law and the Florida Rules of Professional Conduct, Calderwood & Harkness\'s aggregate liability to Pellegrino arising out of or relating to the services provided under this engagement, whether based in contract, tort, negligence, breach of fiduciary duty, or otherwise, shall not exceed the total amount of fees actually paid by Pellegrino to Calderwood & Harkness under this Engagement Letter. This limitation of liability shall not apply to claims arising from the Firm\'s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud.

Pellegrino acknowledges that this limitation of liability has been negotiated at arm\'s length and reflects a reasonable allocation of risk between the parties in light of the fees charged for the services rendered. Nothing in this Section 11 shall be construed to limit any rights or remedies available to Pellegrino under the applicable Rules of Professional Conduct or other non-waivable provisions of applicable law.
**[12. Miscellaneous]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter constitutes the entire agreement between Calderwood & Harkness and Pellegrino with respect to the terms and conditions of the engagement described herein and supersedes all prior or contemporaneous discussions, representations, and agreements, whether written or oral, relating to the subject matter hereof.

No amendment, modification, or waiver of any provision of this Engagement Letter shall be effective unless set forth in a writing signed by both Calderwood & Harkness and Pellegrino. No failure or delay by either party in exercising any right or remedy hereunder shall constitute a waiver thereof.

This matter has been assigned the internal reference number **1027-00002** within Calderwood & Harkness\'s matter management system. Pellegrino is requested to reference this matter number on all correspondence and communications directed to the Firm in connection with this engagement, including payment remittances, to ensure proper application and recordkeeping.

The provisions of Sections 5 (Fees and Billing), 7 (Confidentiality), 8 (Document Retention), 10 (Governing Law), and 11 (Limitation of Liability) shall survive the termination or completion of this engagement.
**[13. Acceptance]{.underline}**

If the foregoing terms are acceptable to Pellegrino, we respectfully request that Adriana Voss, in her capacity as Vice President & General Counsel of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC, sign and date this Engagement Letter in the space provided below and return one fully executed copy to the undersigned at your earliest convenience. A countersigned copy may be returned via email (PDF) to nstern@calderwoodharkness.com or via hand delivery or overnight courier to our office address set forth above.

We are genuinely enthusiastic about the opportunity to work with Pellegrino Capital Group and the broader PCG team on this co-investment alongside Ridgeline Fund IV. We are confident that our Funds & Asset Management Practice Group is well positioned to provide Pellegrino with the high-quality legal counsel and responsive client service that this transaction requires, and we look forward to a successful collaboration.
Please do not hesitate to contact me or Owen Fischer if you have any questions regarding this Engagement Letter or if you wish to discuss any of its provisions.
> Very truly yours,
> **CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP**
CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP
