**Section 1.2 --- Rules of Construction**
In this Agreement, unless the context otherwise requires:

\(a\) The term \"including\" means \"including without limitation\" and shall not be construed to limit any general statement that it follows to the specific or similar items or matters immediately following it.

\(b\) The headings and captions of the Articles, Sections, and subsections of this Agreement are inserted for convenience of reference only and shall not affect the interpretation or construction hereof.
\(c\) All references to \"Articles,\" \"Sections,\" \"Schedules,\" and \"Exhibits\" are to Articles, Sections, Schedules, and Exhibits of and to this Agreement, unless otherwise specified.
\(d\) Words in the singular shall include the plural and vice versa, and words in one gender shall include all genders.

\(e\) The terms \"herein,\" \"hereof,\" \"hereunder,\" \"hereto,\" and words of similar import refer to this Agreement as a whole and not to any particular Article, Section, or other subdivision hereof.

\(f\) References to any statute or statutory provision include any statute or statutory provision that amends, extends, consolidates, or replaces the same, or that has been amended, extended, consolidated, or replaced by the same, and include any rules, regulations, orders, and other subordinate legislation made under the relevant statute or statutory provision.
\(g\) References to \"days\" shall mean calendar days unless the term \"Business Days\" is expressly used.
\(h\) All dollar amounts are stated in United States dollars.
\(i\) The words \"shall\" and \"will\" are used interchangeably and have the same meaning.
**[ARTICLE II --- FORMATION AND ORGANIZATION]{.underline}**
**Section 2.1 --- Formation**

The Partnership was formed as a Delaware limited partnership under the Act by the filing of a Certificate of Limited Partnership with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware. The General Partner shall take all actions reasonably necessary to maintain the Partnership\'s status as a limited partnership under the Act, including the filing of any amendments to the Certificate of Limited Partnership and such other certificates, notices, or documents as may be required by the Act or by applicable law in any jurisdiction in which the Partnership may conduct business or own property.
**Section 2.2 --- Name**

The name of the Partnership is Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P. The business of the Partnership shall be conducted under such name or such other name or names as the General Partner may determine from time to time in its sole discretion. The General Partner shall promptly notify each Limited Partner of any change of the Partnership\'s name.
**Section 2.3 --- Registered Office and Registered Agent**

The registered office of the Partnership in the State of Delaware is located at c/o Capitol Registered Agents, Inc., 850 New Burton Road, Suite 201, Dover, DE 19904. The registered agent of the Partnership for service of process at such address is Capitol Registered Agents, Inc. The General Partner may change the registered office or registered agent (or both) of the Partnership from time to time in accordance with the Act by filing the appropriate amendment to the Certificate of Limited Partnership with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware.
**Section 2.4 --- Principal Office**

The principal office of the Partnership shall be located at the offices of the General Partner at 399 Park Avenue, 28th Floor, New York, NY 10022, or at such other place or places as the General Partner may from time to time designate by notice to the Limited Partners. The books and records of the Partnership shall be maintained at the principal office of the Partnership, or at such other location as the General Partner may designate from time to time.
**Section 2.5 --- Purpose**

The purpose of the Partnership is to co-invest alongside Fund IV in the equity of AcquisitionCo, which will acquire 100% of the issued and outstanding equity interests of Clarion Hospitality Holdings, Inc. The Partnership shall hold, manage, monitor, and ultimately dispose of such Investment, and shall engage in all activities incidental, necessary, or related thereto. The Partnership is formed solely for the purpose of making and holding the Investment, and shall not make any follow-on investments, acquire any additional portfolio companies, or accept any additional capital commitments from the Limited Partners beyond the Initial Capital Contributions. Except as expressly provided herein, the Partnership shall not engage in any business or activity other than in furtherance of the foregoing purpose.
**Section 2.6 --- Term**
The term of the Partnership shall be as set forth in Article XI.
**Section 2.7 --- Fiscal Year**

The Fiscal Year of the Partnership shall be the calendar year, commencing on January 1 and ending on December 31 of each year, or such other fiscal year as the General Partner may select in compliance with the Code and applicable Treasury Regulations.
**Section 2.8 --- Tax Classification**

The Partnership intends to be treated as a partnership for United States federal, state, and local income tax purposes and shall not elect to be classified as a corporation or association taxable as a corporation for federal income tax purposes. The General Partner shall not take any action, and shall cause the Partnership not to take any action, that would cause the Partnership to be classified as other than a partnership for United States federal income tax purposes, including not electing to be treated as a corporation under Treasury Regulations Section 301.7701-3. Each Partner agrees that it will not take any position on any tax return or in any tax proceeding that is inconsistent with the treatment of the Partnership as a partnership for United States federal income tax purposes.
**Section 2.9 --- Title to Partnership Property**

All property of the Partnership, whether real, personal, or mixed, and whether tangible or intangible, shall be owned by the Partnership as an entity and shall be held in the name of the Partnership or a nominee designated by the General Partner. No Partner shall have any individual ownership interest in any Partnership property by virtue of being a Partner, and each Partner\'s interest in the Partnership shall be personal property for all purposes. No Partner shall have the right to partition any property of the Partnership or to compel any sale or appraisal of Partnership assets.
**[ARTICLE III --- PARTNERS; ADMISSIONS]{.underline}**
**Section 3.1 --- General Partner**

Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, EIN 93-4817302, is hereby confirmed as the General Partner of the Partnership. The General Partner is wholly owned by Ridgeline Equity Management LLC. The General Partner shall have an interest in the Partnership as set forth in this Agreement, including the right to receive Carried Interest distributions pursuant to Article VI, but shall not be required to make any Capital Contribution to the Partnership. The General Partner\'s rights and obligations with respect to the management and operation of the Partnership are set forth in Article VII.
**Section 3.2 --- Limited Partners**

The Limited Partners of the Partnership are the Persons listed on Schedule A attached hereto, together with their respective Capital Commitments and Partnership Percentages. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing:

\(a\) Pellegrino Capital Group LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (foreign-qualified in the State of Florida), EIN 84-3291047, is admitted as a Limited Partner with a Capital Commitment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), representing a Partnership Percentage of 33.33% of the Aggregate Capital Commitments.

\(b\) The remaining co-investors listed on Schedule A are admitted as Limited Partners with aggregate Capital Commitments of Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000), representing an aggregate Partnership Percentage of 66.67% of the Aggregate Capital Commitments, each with its respective individual Capital Commitment and Partnership Percentage as set forth on Schedule A.

Each Limited Partner\'s Partnership Interest, including its economic and governance rights, shall be determined by reference to its Partnership Percentage as set forth on Schedule A, subject to adjustment as provided herein.
**Section 3.3 --- Admission of Additional Limited Partners**

\(a\) The General Partner may admit additional Limited Partners to the Partnership prior to the Closing Date, in the General Partner\'s sole discretion, subject to maintaining the Aggregate Capital Commitments at Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000). Any such additional Limited Partner shall execute a joinder to this Agreement substantially in the form of Exhibit A and shall be bound by all terms and conditions hereof.

\(b\) After the Closing Date, additional Limited Partners may be admitted to the Partnership only in connection with a Transfer of a Partnership Interest that is permitted under and consummated in accordance with Article VIII. Any transferee admitted as a Limited Partner shall execute a joinder to this Agreement and shall succeed to all rights and obligations of the transferring Limited Partner with respect to the transferred Partnership Interest.
\(c\) The General Partner shall promptly update Schedule A to reflect the admission of any additional Limited Partner and shall provide a copy of the updated Schedule A to all Partners.
**Section 3.4 --- Representations and Warranties of Limited Partners**

Each Limited Partner, severally and not jointly, hereby represents and warrants to the Partnership and the General Partner, as of the date of such Limited Partner\'s execution of this Agreement (or its joinder hereto) and as of the Closing Date, as follows:

\(a\) **Organization and Good Standing.** Such Limited Partner is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing (or the equivalent thereof) under the laws of the jurisdiction of its organization, and is duly qualified or registered to do business in each jurisdiction where the nature of its activities or the character of its properties requires such qualification or registration.

\(b\) **Authority.** Such Limited Partner has full power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform its obligations under this Agreement and to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby. The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement by such Limited Partner has been duly authorized by all necessary corporate, partnership, limited liability company, or other organizational action on the part of such Limited Partner.

\(c\) **No Violations.** The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement by such Limited Partner does not and will not (i) violate, conflict with, or result in a breach of any provision of such Limited Partner\'s organizational documents, (ii) violate any law, rule, regulation, order, judgment, or decree applicable to such Limited Partner, or (iii) conflict with, result in a breach of, or constitute a default under any material agreement or instrument to which such Limited Partner is a party or by which its properties are bound.
\(d\) **Accredited Investor.** Such Limited Partner is an \"accredited investor\" as defined in Rule 501(a) of Regulation D promulgated under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended.

\(e\) **Investment Intent.** Such Limited Partner is acquiring its Partnership Interest for its own account, for investment purposes only, and not with a view to, or for offer or sale in connection with, any distribution thereof within the meaning of the Securities Act. Such Limited Partner acknowledges that the Partnership Interests have not been registered under the Securities Act or the securities laws of any state and cannot be transferred, sold, or otherwise disposed of except in compliance with such laws.

\(f\) **ERISA.** Such Limited Partner is not a \"benefit plan investor\" as defined in Section 3(42) of ERISA and the regulations promulgated thereunder, or if such Limited Partner is a benefit plan investor, the investment by such Limited Partner in the Partnership satisfies all applicable requirements of ERISA, including any applicable prohibited transaction exemptions, and will not result in a non-exempt prohibited transaction under Section 406 of ERISA or Section 4975 of the Code.
\(g\) **Bad Actor.** Such Limited Partner is not a \"bad actor\" within the meaning of Rule 506(d) of Regulation D promulgated under the Securities Act.

\(h\) **Anti-Money Laundering; OFAC; FATCA.** Such Limited Partner is in compliance with all applicable anti-money laundering laws and regulations, including the Bank Secrecy Act, the USA PATRIOT Act, and the regulations administered by the U.S. Department of the Treasury\'s Office of Foreign Assets Control (\"OFAC\"). Such Limited Partner is not (i) a Person listed on the Specially Designated Nationals and blocked Persons List maintained by OFAC, (ii) a Person that is otherwise the target of U.S. sanctions laws, or (iii) a Person located, organized, or resident in a country or territory that is the subject of comprehensive U.S. sanctions. Such Limited Partner is in compliance with the Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (\"FATCA\"), Sections 1471 through 1474 of the Code, and any applicable intergovernmental agreements thereunder.

\(i\) **Sophistication.** Such Limited Partner has such knowledge and experience in financial and business matters that it is capable of evaluating the merits and risks of an investment in the Partnership and making an informed investment decision with respect thereto. Such Limited Partner is able to bear the economic risk of its investment for an indefinite period and is able to afford a complete loss of its investment.
**Section 3.5 --- No Authority of Limited Partners**

No Limited Partner shall have any authority to act for, bind, or otherwise obligate the Partnership or any other Partner in any manner whatsoever solely by virtue of being a Limited Partner. Limited Partners shall have only the rights, powers, and authority specifically granted to them pursuant to this Agreement or as required under the Act, and no Limited Partner shall take any action in its capacity as a Limited Partner that would jeopardize the status of the Partnership as a limited partnership under the Act. No Limited Partner shall participate in the management or control of the Partnership\'s business or transact any business on behalf of the Partnership. The exercise by a Limited Partner of any rights granted under this Agreement, including the right to vote on or consent to matters specified herein, shall not constitute participation in the management or control of the Partnership\'s business for purposes of the Act.

19: **[I. Purpose of This Memorandum]{.underline}**

21: This memorandum supplements the Engagement Letter dated May 12, 2025, executed by Sylvia Hartwell on behalf of Calderwood & Harkness LLP and countersigned by Priya Narasimhan in her capacity as General Counsel of Solara Digital Infrastructure LP. The Engagement Letter established the general terms and conditions governing the attorney-client relationship between Calderwood & Harkness LLP and Solara Digital Infrastructure LP, including applicable fee arrangements, conflict of interest disclosures, and standard terms of representation.

23: The purpose of this memorandum is to set forth in detail the scope of work, underlying assumptions, and limitations of Calderwood & Harkness LLP\'s engagement in connection with the preparation and submission of a private letter ruling (\"PLR\") request to the Internal Revenue Service (\"IRS\") on behalf of Solara Digital Infrastructure LP and its affiliated fund entities. The PLR request concerns a proposed cross-border fund-platform reorganization that will consolidate four legacy offshore fund vehicles into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure, as described more fully in Sections III and IV below.

This memorandum should be read in conjunction with the Engagement Letter, and in the event of any conflict between this memorandum and the Engagement Letter with respect to the description of the scope of work, the terms of this memorandum shall control.

Calderwood & Harkness will provide quarterly budget updates to Mr. Dalmqvist and Ms. Narasimhan, and will promptly notify the client if actual or projected fees are expected to exceed the upper end of the estimated range.
80: 
81: **[III. Background and Business Context]{.underline}**
82: 
83: **[A. Existing Fund Platform Structure]{.underline}**
84: 
85: Solara currently operates its investment activities through six parallel fund vehicles organized across three jurisdictions --- Delaware, the Cayman Islands, and Luxembourg. The parallel fund structure was established to accommodate the differing tax, regulatory, and treaty requirements of Solara\'s diverse investor base, which includes U.S. taxable investors, U.S. tax-exempt institutional investors, and non-U.S. investors from multiple jurisdictions.
86: 
87: The six existing fund vehicles, together with their key attributes, are described below:
88: 
89: **Fund IV Vehicles:**
90: 
91: 1\. **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP** --- A Delaware limited partnership with total capital commitments of \$4.2 billion (vintage 2021), approximately 72% deployed as of March 31, 2025. EIN: 85-2103748. General Partner: Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC. This vehicle serves as the main domestic fund for U.S. taxable investors.
92: 
93: 2\. **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP** --- A Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with total capital commitments of \$1.85 billion, operating as a parallel fund for non-U.S. investors and U.S. tax-exempt investors seeking UBTI blocker benefits. EIN: 98-6241503. CIMA Registration: MF-72491. General Partner: Solara Offshore GP Ltd. Registered office: Harborstone Corporate Services Ltd., P.O. Box 2714, 94 Solaris Avenue, George Town, Grand Cayman KY1-1111.
94: 
95: 3\. **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- A Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with total capital commitments of €1.15 billion (approximately \$1.24 billion at 1.08 EUR/USD), established to provide treaty access and regulatory familiarity for European and Asian institutional investors. EIN: 98-6241571. Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (\"RCS\"): B 248193. General Partner: Solara Luxembourg Management S.à r.l. (RCS B 248194). Registered office: 14, rue Jean-Pierre Brasseur, L-1258 Luxembourg.
96: 
97: **Fund V Vehicles:**
98: 
99: 4\. **Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP** --- A Delaware limited partnership with total capital commitments of \$5.6 billion (vintage 2023), approximately 38% deployed as of March 31, 2025. EIN: 88-3467219. General Partner: Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC. This vehicle serves as the main domestic fund for U.S. taxable investors in the current generation of investments.
100: 
101: 5\. **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-A (Cayman) LP** --- A Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with total capital commitments of \$2.45 billion, serving as the parallel fund for non-U.S. investors and U.S. tax-exempt investors. EIN: 98-7891234. CIMA Registration: MF-89103. Registered office: Harborstone Corporate Services Ltd., George Town, Grand Cayman.
102: 
103: 6\. **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- A Luxembourg special limited partnership with total capital commitments of €1.38 billion (approximately \$1.49 billion at 1.08 EUR/USD). EIN: 98-7891267. RCS: B 271056. Registered office: 14, rue Jean-Pierre Brasseur, L-1258 Luxembourg.
104: 
105: **Investor Base Allocation:**
106: 
107: The allocation of investors across the fund vehicles follows a well-established pattern based on the tax status and domicile of each investor:
108: 
109: > • *U.S. taxable investors* invest through the Delaware main funds (Fund IV LP and Fund V LP). This category includes U.S. taxable institutional investors and family offices. For example, Argyle Family Office Holdings LLC, a U.S. taxable family office, holds commitments of \$95 million in Fund IV LP and \$130 million in Fund V LP.
110: >
111: > • *U.S. tax-exempt investors* invest through the Cayman parallel vehicles to obtain UBTI blocker benefits, thereby avoiding the recognition of unrelated business taxable income under IRC §§ 511--514 that might otherwise arise from leveraged investments or operating business income. Representative U.S. tax-exempt investors include the Pinnacle State Employees\' Retirement System (\$275 million committed to Fund IV-A Cayman; \$340 million committed to Fund V-A Cayman) and the Grandview University Endowment (\$120 million committed to Fund IV-A Cayman; \$185 million committed to Fund V-A Cayman).
112: >
113: > • *Non-U.S. investors* invest through the Cayman or Luxembourg vehicles based on treaty access and regulatory considerations applicable to each investor\'s jurisdiction of domicile. Representative non-U.S. investors include Nordhaven Sovereign Wealth Fund (\$380 million committed to Fund IV-A Cayman; \$500 million committed to Fund V-A Cayman), which invests through the Cayman vehicles, and Kestrel Pacific Insurance Group, a Singapore-domiciled insurer (€200 million committed to Fund IV-B Luxembourg; €275 million committed to Fund V-B Luxembourg), which invests through the Luxembourg vehicles for European treaty access and Solvency II regulatory reporting purposes.
114: 
115: **[B. Business Rationale for the Reorganization]{.underline}**
116: 
117: Solara\'s management team has determined that the existing six-vehicle parallel fund structure has become operationally burdensome and, in light of evolving international tax rules, increasingly less advantageous from a tax perspective. The proposed reorganization is motivated by four principal business considerations:
118: 
119: **Operational Cost Reduction.** Solara currently incurs approximately \$3.8 million annually in duplicative offshore administration, audit, and regulatory compliance fees across the parallel structures. These costs include annual fees payable to Harborstone Corporate Services Ltd. for Cayman registered office services, annual fees payable to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (\"CSSF\") in Luxembourg, annual audit fees for the separate financial statements required for each offshore vehicle, and administration fees payable to Clarendon Fund Services Ltd. for NAV calculation and investor reporting across multiple parallel entities. Consolidation into a single master fund with two feeder vehicles is expected to yield meaningful annual cost savings.
120: 
121: **Pillar Two GloBE Rules.** The OECD Inclusive Framework\'s Pillar Two Global Anti-Base Erosion (\"GloBE\") rules, as implemented by Luxembourg through the Grand Ducal law transposing EU Directive 2022/2523, become effective for Solara\'s Luxembourg entities beginning in fiscal year 2025. The GloBE rules impose a minimum effective tax rate of 15% on the income of constituent entities within large multinational groups. While the Luxembourg SCSp structures were historically designed to provide tax transparency and treaty benefits, the incremental compliance burden and potential top-up tax exposure under the GloBE rules diminish the continuing benefit of maintaining separate Luxembourg fund vehicles.
122: 
123: **FATCA and CRS Simplification.** The existing multi-jurisdictional structure requires separate Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (\"FATCA\") reporting under intergovernmental agreements applicable to each of the Cayman Islands and Luxembourg, as well as Common Reporting Standard (\"CRS\") reporting under the Cayman Tax Information Authority (International Tax Compliance) Regulations and Luxembourg\'s CRS implementing legislation. Consolidation of the offshore vehicles into Cayman-domiciled feeders that invest through a single Delaware master fund will reduce the number of reporting financial institutions and simplify ongoing compliance obligations.
124: 
125: **LP-Requested Governance Simplification.** Several of Solara\'s largest limited partners have expressed a preference for a simplified fund governance structure that reduces the number of separate limited partnership agreements, advisory committee structures, and consent processes to which they are subject. The reorganization responds to this investor feedback by creating a streamlined architecture in which investment decisions and governance matters are centralized at the master fund level.
126: 
127: **[C. Key Portfolio Company Interests Involved]{.underline}**
128: 
129: The proposed reorganization will result in the transfer of portfolio company interests currently held by the four legacy offshore vehicles into the newly established Consolidated Master Fund LP. The six existing fund vehicles collectively hold interests in twenty-three portfolio companies --- eleven in the Fund IV vehicles and twelve in the Fund V vehicles. The portfolio spans the digital infrastructure and enterprise SaaS sectors.
130: 
131: The following representative portfolio company holdings, which are among the largest positions being transferred and which illustrate the range of entity types, asset values, and built-in gain positions involved, are described below for context:
132: 
133: > • **NovaBright Data Systems Inc.** --- A Delaware corporation engaged in the operation of hyperscale data center facilities in Northern Virginia, Dallas, and Phoenix. Fair market value: \$890 million. Adjusted tax basis: \$520 million. Built-in gain: \$370 million. Ownership: Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP holds 60%; Fund IV LP holds 40%.
134: >
135: > • **Crestline Cloud Solutions LLC** --- A Delaware limited liability company classified as a disregarded entity for U.S. federal income tax purposes, operating a cloud-based enterprise SaaS platform for supply chain management. Fair market value: €340 million (\$367 million at 1.08 EUR/USD). Adjusted tax basis: €195 million (\$211 million). Built-in gain: €145 million (\$156 million). Ownership: Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp holds 100%.
136: >
137: > • **Veridian Edge Computing Corp.** --- A Delaware corporation providing edge computing infrastructure and managed services to telecommunications carriers and enterprise customers. Fair market value: \$1.12 billion. Adjusted tax basis: \$780 million. Built-in gain: \$340 million. Ownership: Fund V-A (Cayman) LP holds 55%; Fund V LP holds 45%.
138: >
139: > • **Thorngate Fiber Networks LP** --- A Delaware limited partnership that owns and operates metropolitan and long-haul fiber-optic network assets across the northeastern United States. Fair market value: \$670 million. Adjusted tax basis: \$490 million. Built-in gain: \$180 million. Ownership: Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP holds 100%.
140: >
141: > • **Helix SaaS Holdings Ltd.** --- A Cayman Islands exempted company serving as a holding company for a portfolio of enterprise SaaS businesses focused on financial services technology. Fair market value: \$445 million. Adjusted tax basis: \$310 million. Built-in gain: \$135 million. Ownership: Fund V-A (Cayman) LP holds 100%.
142: 
143: The remaining eighteen portfolio company interests are of comparable character and will be detailed in the asset schedules prepared as part of the PLR exhibits. The aggregate financial summary of all assets being transferred is set forth in Section IV.G below.
144: 
145: **[IV. Description of the Proposed Reorganization]{.underline}**
146: 
147: **[A. Overview --- Five-Step Integrated Transaction]{.underline}**
148: 
149: The proposed reorganization is structured as a five-step integrated transaction designed to consolidate the four legacy offshore fund vehicles --- Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP, Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp, Fund V-A (Cayman) LP, and Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp --- into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure with two Cayman-domiciled feeder vehicles.
150: 
151: The target effective date for completion of all five steps is **December 1, 2025**. Each step has been sequenced to optimize operational logistics, accommodate regulatory lead times in the Cayman Islands and Luxembourg, and minimize the period during which legacy offshore vehicles and new entities will coexist. The five steps are designed to be treated as an integrated transaction for U.S. federal income tax purposes, and the PLR request will present them as such. However, the steps are also designed to be independently defensible under the applicable Internal Revenue Code provisions in the event the IRS were to disaggregate the transaction for analytical purposes.
152: 
153: The five steps are summarized below and described in detail in Sections IV.B through IV.F.
154: 
155: **[B. Step 1 --- Formation of New Entities (Target: September 15, 2025)]{.underline}**
156: 
157: The first step involves the formation of four new legal entities that will constitute the post-reorganization consolidated fund architecture:
158: 
159: 1\. **Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC** --- A Delaware limited liability company to be formed under the Delaware Limited Liability Company Act, 6 Del. C. § 18-101 *et seq.*, which will serve as the general partner of the Consolidated Master Fund LP. This entity will be managed by Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC and will hold a nominal general partner interest in the Master Fund.
160: 
161: 2\. **Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP** --- A Delaware limited partnership to be formed under the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act, which will serve as the master fund vehicle into which all portfolio assets currently held by the four legacy offshore vehicles will be contributed. The general partner of the Master Fund LP will be Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC.
162: 
163: 3\. **Solara International Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- A Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to be formed under the Cayman Islands Exempted Limited Partnership Act (as revised), which will serve as the feeder vehicle for non-U.S. investors who currently invest through the Fund IV-A and Fund V-A Cayman parallel vehicles and through the Fund IV-B and Fund V-B Luxembourg vehicles.
164: 
165: 4\. **Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- A Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to be formed under the same Cayman Islands legislation, which will serve as the feeder vehicle for U.S. tax-exempt investors to mitigate exposure to unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") under IRC §§ 511--514.
166: 
167: Concurrently with or promptly following the formation of each new entity, IRS Form 8832 (Entity Classification Election) will be filed with the IRS under Treasury Regulation § 301.7701-3 to elect classification as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes for each of the three new entities required to make such an election --- namely, the Consolidated Master Fund LP, the International Feeder (Cayman) LP, and the Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP. The effective dates of the check-the-box elections will be coordinated with the target dates for the subsequent reorganization steps to ensure that the new entities are classified as partnerships prior to the contribution transactions described in Steps 2 through 4. The 75-day retroactivity rule under Treasury Regulation § 301.7701-3(c)(1)(iii) will be taken into account in establishing the election effective dates.
168: 
169: **[C. Step 2 --- Contribution of Fund IV-A Cayman Assets (Target: October 1, 2025)]{.underline}**
170: 
171: In Step 2, **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP** will contribute all of its portfolio company assets to **Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP** in exchange for a limited partnership interest in the Consolidated Master Fund LP.
172: 
173: The aggregate financial parameters of the Step 2 contribution are as follows:
174: 
175:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
176:   **Metric**                                           **Amount**
177:   ---------------------------------------------------- -----------------------------------
178:   Aggregate Fair Market Value of Contributed Assets    \$2.31 billion
179: 
180:   Aggregate Adjusted Tax Basis of Contributed Assets   \$1.62 billion
181: 
182:   Aggregate Built-In Gain                              \$690 million
183:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
184: 
185: The intended U.S. federal income tax treatment of the Step 2 contribution is as a tax-free contribution under IRC § 721(a), pursuant to which no gain or loss is recognized by Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP or by the Consolidated Master Fund LP upon the contribution. The adjusted tax basis of each contributed asset will carry over to the Consolidated Master Fund LP under IRC § 723, and the holding period of each contributed asset will include the period during which the asset was held by Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP under IRC § 1223(2).
186: 
187: As part of the tax analysis supporting the PLR request, Calderwood & Harkness will analyze whether the contribution implicates the investment company exception under IRC § 721(b). This provision denies tax-free treatment to a contribution to a partnership that would be treated as an \"investment company\" within the meaning of IRC § 351(e) if the partnership were a corporation. The analysis will address whether the Consolidated Master Fund LP\'s portfolio of operating company interests --- consisting of data center operators, fiber-optic network businesses, edge computing platforms, and SaaS enterprises --- constitutes a portfolio of \"stocks, securities, or other investment assets\" for purposes of this analysis.
188: 
189: **[D. Step 3 --- Contribution of Fund IV-B Luxembourg Assets (Target: October 15, 2025)]{.underline}**
190: 
191: In Step 3, **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** will contribute all of its portfolio company assets to **Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP** in exchange for a limited partnership interest in the Consolidated Master Fund LP.
192: 
193: The aggregate financial parameters of the Step 3 contribution are as follows:
194: 
195:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
196:   **Metric**                     **EUR Amount**          **USD Amount (at 1.08)**
197:   ------------------------------ ----------------------- --------------------------
198:   Aggregate Fair Market Value    €1.07 billion           \$1.16 billion
199: 
200:   Aggregate Adjusted Tax Basis   €782 million            \$844.6 million
201: 
202:   Aggregate Built-In Gain        €288 million            \$311 million
203:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
204: 
205: The intended U.S. federal income tax treatment is the same as Step 2: a tax-free contribution under IRC § 721(a) with carryover basis under IRC § 723 and holding period tacking under IRC § 1223(2).
206: 
207: Step 3 raises additional cross-border tax considerations that are not present in Step 2. Because Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp is a foreign partnership contributing assets to a domestic partnership (the Consolidated Master Fund LP), Calderwood & Harkness will analyze the applicability of IRC § 367 to the contribution. Specifically, the PLR request will address the position that IRC § 367 does not apply to this transfer because, by its terms, IRC § 367(a) applies to transfers of property by a United States person *to a foreign corporation*, and IRC § 367(b) applies to exchanges described in certain enumerated provisions *involving a foreign corporation*. Neither subsection, by its terms, applies to a transfer by a foreign partnership to a domestic partnership. The PLR request will seek an affirmative ruling that IRC § 367 is inapplicable to the Step 3 contribution.
208: 
209: With respect to Luxembourg tax consequences, no Luxembourg capital gains tax is expected to arise at the SCSp level on the transfer, based on Article 3(2) of the Luxembourg law of July 12, 2013 (*Loi du 12 juillet 2013 relative aux gestionnaires de fonds d\'investissement alternatifs*), which provides for tax transparency of the SCSp. However, Calderwood & Harkness expressly disclaims any responsibility for the analysis of Luxembourg tax law, which will be addressed by Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l., as set forth in Section VI.A below.
210: 
211: Additionally, Calderwood & Harkness will analyze whether the contribution gives rise to a deemed disposition triggering withholding obligations under IRC § 1446, which imposes a withholding tax on effectively connected taxable income allocable to foreign partners.
212: 
213: **[E. Step 4 --- Contribution of Fund V Offshore Assets (Target: November 1, 2025)]{.underline}**
214: 
215: In Step 4, the two Fund V offshore vehicles will contribute their respective portfolio company assets to the Consolidated Master Fund LP:
216: 
217: **Fund V-A (Cayman) LP Contribution:**
218: 
219:   -----------------------------------------------------------------------
220:   **Metric**                          **Amount**
221:   ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
222:   Aggregate Fair Market Value         \$2.89 billion
223: 
224:   Aggregate Adjusted Tax Basis        \$2.34 billion
225: 
226:   Aggregate Built-In Gain             \$550 million
227:   -----------------------------------------------------------------------
228: 
229: **Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp Contribution:**
230: 
231:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
232:   **Metric**                     **EUR Amount**          **USD Amount (at 1.08)**
233:   ------------------------------ ----------------------- --------------------------
234:   Aggregate Fair Market Value    €1.29 billion           \$1.39 billion
235: 
236:   Aggregate Adjusted Tax Basis   €1.14 billion           \$1.23 billion
237: 
238:   Aggregate Built-In Gain        €150 million            \$162 million
239:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
240: 
241: The intended U.S. federal income tax treatment is the same as described in Steps 2 and 3 above: tax-free contributions under IRC § 721(a) with carryover basis under IRC § 723 and holding period tacking under IRC § 1223(2). The IRC § 367 inapplicability analysis and IRC § 1446 withholding analysis applicable to the Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp contribution will mirror the analysis described in connection with Step 3.
242: 
243: **[F. Step 5 --- Dissolution of Legacy Offshore Vehicles and LP Migration (Target: December 1, 2025)]{.underline}**
244: 
245: In Step 5, the four legacy offshore vehicles --- Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP, Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp, Fund V-A (Cayman) LP, and Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp --- will dissolve and distribute their respective limited partnership interests in the Consolidated Master Fund LP to their existing limited partners in liquidation of those limited partners\' interests in the dissolving vehicles.
246: 
247: Following the dissolution distributions:
248: 
249: > • **Non-U.S. limited partners** will contribute their distributed Master Fund LP interests to the newly formed **Solara International Feeder (Cayman) LP**, receiving limited partnership interests in the International Feeder in exchange.
250: >
251: > • **U.S. tax-exempt limited partners** will contribute their distributed Master Fund LP interests to the newly formed **Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP**, receiving limited partnership interests in the Tax-Exempt Feeder in exchange.
252: 
253: The intended U.S. federal income tax treatment of the dissolution distributions is as tax-free distributions under IRC § 731(a), pursuant to which no gain or loss is recognized by the distributing partnership or the distributee partners except to the extent that money distributed exceeds a partner\'s adjusted basis in its partnership interest.
254: 
255: A critical aspect of the Step 5 analysis is whether the limited partnership interests in the Consolidated Master Fund LP distributed by the dissolving vehicles constitute \"marketable securities\" within the meaning of IRC § 731(c). If so, the distribution of such interests could be treated as a distribution of money under IRC § 731(c)(1), potentially triggering gain recognition. Calderwood & Harkness will analyze whether the Consolidated Master Fund LP interests are \"marketable securities\" as defined in IRC § 731(c)(2), which generally requires that the securities be actively traded or, in certain cases, that they be of a type that is actively traded. The PLR request will seek a ruling that the Master Fund LP interests are not marketable securities within the meaning of § 731(c)(2), on the basis that they are interests in a newly formed, non-publicly traded limited partnership that are not actively traded on an established securities market or readily tradable on a secondary market or the substantial equivalent thereof.
256: 
257: **Resulting Post-Reorganization Structure.** Upon completion of all five steps, the resulting fund structure will consist of:
258: 
259: > • **Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP** (Delaware), holding the consolidated portfolio of twenty-three portfolio companies previously held by the four legacy offshore vehicles.
260: >
261: > • **Solara International Feeder (Cayman) LP**, holding a limited partnership interest in the Master Fund LP, through which all non-U.S. investors will invest.
262: >
263: > • **Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP**, holding a limited partnership interest in the Master Fund LP, through which all U.S. tax-exempt investors will invest.
264: >
265: > • **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP** and **Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP** (each a Delaware LP), which will continue to hold their existing portfolio company interests directly and will co-invest alongside the Consolidated Master Fund LP. U.S. taxable investors will remain as limited partners in these vehicles.
266: 
267: **[G. Aggregate Financial Summary]{.underline}**
268: 
269: The aggregate financial parameters of the proposed reorganization are as follows:
270: 
271:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
272:   **Metric**                                                                            **Amount**
273:   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------
274:   Total Fair Market Value of Assets Being Transferred to the Consolidated Master Fund   \$7.75 billion
275: 
276:   Total Aggregate Adjusted Tax Basis                                                    \$6.03 billion
277: 
278:   Total Aggregate Built-In Gain                                                         \$1.72 billion
279: 
280:   Aggregate Liabilities Assumed by the Consolidated Master Fund                         \$1.34 billion
281: 
282:   Total Portfolio Companies Transferred                                                 23 (11 from Fund IV vehicles; 12 from Fund V vehicles)
283:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
284: 
285: The magnitude of the aggregate built-in gain of \$1.72 billion underscores the critical importance of obtaining a favorable PLR confirming the tax-free treatment of the contribution and distribution transactions. Any adverse ruling, or failure to obtain the requested rulings, could expose the fund vehicles and their limited partners to significant gain recognition in the year of the reorganization.
286: 
287: **[V. Scope of Work --- Specific Deliverables]{.underline}**
288: 
289: The following subsections describe each category of deliverables that Calderwood & Harkness will produce in connection with this engagement. Except as expressly noted below, all deliverables will be prepared by the Calderwood & Harkness engagement team and will be subject to review and approval by Leonard Cross (Responsible Partner) and Sylvia Hartwell (Billing Partner) prior to delivery to the client or submission to any third party.
290: 
291: **[A. Tax Analysis Memoranda]{.underline}**
292: 
293: Calderwood & Harkness will prepare comprehensive tax analysis memoranda addressing each material provision of the Internal Revenue Code and Treasury Regulations implicated by the proposed reorganization. These memoranda are intended to serve dual purposes: (i) to provide Solara\'s management and tax team with a thorough analysis of the tax consequences of each step of the reorganization, and (ii) to form the analytical foundation for the positions taken in the PLR request.
294: 
295: The following memoranda will be prepared:
296: 
297: 1\. **Master Tax Analysis Memorandum** --- A comprehensive overview memorandum analyzing the entire five-step reorganization as an integrated transaction, identifying each material IRC provision implicated, summarizing the intended tax treatment of each step, and flagging any areas of material uncertainty or risk.
298: 
299: 2\. **IRC § 721(a) Contribution Analysis (Steps 2--4)** --- A detailed memorandum analyzing the application of IRC § 721(a) to the contributions by the four legacy offshore vehicles of their portfolio company interests to the Consolidated Master Fund LP, including discussion of the requirements for nonrecognition treatment, the effect of carryover basis under IRC § 723, and holding period tacking under IRC § 1223(2).
