**[I. Purpose of This Memorandum]{.underline}**

This memorandum supplements the Engagement Letter dated May 12, 2025, executed by Sylvia Hartwell on behalf of Calderwood & Harkness LLP and countersigned by Priya Narasimhan in her capacity as General Counsel of Solara Digital Infrastructure LP. The Engagement Letter established the general terms and conditions governing the attorney-client relationship between Calderwood & Harkness LLP and Solara Digital Infrastructure LP, including applicable fee arrangements, conflict of interest disclosures, and standard terms of representation.

The purpose of this memorandum is to set forth in detail the scope of work, underlying assumptions, and limitations of Calderwood & Harkness LLP\'s engagement in connection with the preparation and submission of a private letter ruling (\"PLR\") request to the Internal Revenue Service (\"IRS\") on behalf of Solara Digital Infrastructure LP and its affiliated fund entities. The PLR request concerns a proposed cross-border fund-platform reorganization that will consolidate four legacy offshore fund vehicles into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure, as described more fully in Sections III and IV below.

This memorandum is intended to provide a definitive reference for the engagement team and the client regarding the boundaries of the representation. It identifies each specific deliverable within scope, delineates the matters expressly excluded from scope, sets forth the factual, legal, and timing assumptions upon which the engagement is predicated, and describes the coordination framework with other professional advisors retained by Solara. This memorandum should be read in conjunction with the Engagement Letter, and in the event of any conflict between this memorandum and the Engagement Letter with respect to the description of the scope of work, the terms of this memorandum shall control.
All capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined herein have the meanings ascribed to them in the Engagement Letter or as set forth in the relevant context below.
**[II. Client and Engagement Overview]{.underline}**
**[A. The Client]{.underline}**

The client for purposes of this engagement is **Solara Digital Infrastructure LP** (\"Solara\" or \"SDILP\"), a Delaware limited partnership formed on March 17, 2014, under the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act, 6 Del. C. § 17-101 *et seq.* Solara\'s principal office and headquarters are located at 1200 Market Street, Suite 3400, Wilmington, Delaware 19801.

Solara is a private equity sponsor focused on digital infrastructure and enterprise software-as-a-service (\"SaaS\") verticals. As of March 31, 2025, Solara had approximately \$14.7 billion in assets under management across its family of fund vehicles. Solara\'s investment portfolio spans data center operations, fiber-optic network infrastructure, edge computing platforms, and enterprise SaaS businesses.

The general partner of Solara Digital Infrastructure LP is **Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company managed by Viktor Raines. Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC holds Employer Identification Number (\"EIN\") 82-4917365. Solara Digital Infrastructure LP holds EIN 82-4917366.
The registered agent for all Delaware entities within the Solara platform is **Capitol Registered Agents Inc.**, located at 850 New Burton Road, Suite 201, Dover, Delaware 19904.
**[B. Engagement Firm and Team]{.underline}**

The engagement firm is **Calderwood & Harkness LLP**, a limited liability partnership organized under the laws of the State of New York. Calderwood & Harkness maintains offices relevant to this engagement at the following locations:
> • **New York Office:** 600 Lexington Avenue, 38th Floor, New York, New York 10022
> • **Washington, D.C. Office:** 1900 K Street NW, Suite 1100, Washington, D.C. 20006
The engagement team assigned to this matter consists of the following professionals:

> • **Leonard Cross** --- Responsible Partner, Tax Practice Group, based in the Washington, D.C. office. Mr. Cross has twenty-eight years of experience advising private equity funds, sovereign wealth funds, and multinational enterprises on matters involving international tax, partnership tax, and fund formation. Mr. Cross will serve as the senior engagement partner with primary responsibility for the substantive tax analysis and all direct interactions with the IRS, including attendance at any pre-submission conference and post-submission communications.

> • **Sylvia Hartwell** --- Billing Partner, Tax Practice Group, based in the New York office. Ms. Hartwell has twenty-four years of experience concentrating in cross-border restructurings, investment fund taxation, and the negotiation of tax-related provisions in fund formation documents. Ms. Hartwell will serve as the billing partner responsible for engagement economics, staffing, and budget management, and will participate in the substantive tax analysis as a senior reviewer.

> • **Robert Jansen** --- Lead Associate, Tax Practice Group, based in the Washington, D.C. office. Mr. Jansen has six years of experience in partnership tax, international tax, and PLR submission practice. Mr. Jansen will serve as the day-to-day lead on drafting the PLR request and supporting memoranda.

> • **Garrett Simmons** --- Working Associate, Tax Practice Group, based in the New York office. Mr. Simmons has three years of experience in tax research, entity classification, and transactional tax analysis. Mr. Simmons will support Mr. Jansen in the preparation of exhibits, research memoranda, and financial schedules.

The primary client-side contacts for this engagement are **Stefan Dalmqvist**, Head of Tax, and **Priya Narasimhan**, General Counsel, each of Solara Digital Infrastructure LP. All substantive communications regarding the engagement, including draft deliverables, data requests, and status updates, will be directed to Mr. Dalmqvist and Ms. Narasimhan unless otherwise agreed.
**[C. Engagement Basics]{.underline}**
The key administrative parameters of the engagement are as follows:
> • **Engagement Letter Execution Date:** May 12, 2025
> • **Matter Opened Date:** May 27, 2025
> • **Engagement Number:** 20250527-SDILP-PLR

> • **Fee Arrangement:** Blended hourly rate of \$1,175 per hour, applicable to all timekeeper hours billed to this matter. The blended rate reflects a weighted average across partner and associate billing rates and was negotiated as part of the Engagement Letter to provide cost certainty relative to the varying seniority levels of professionals staffed on the matter.

> • **Estimated Total Fees:** \$1,800,000 to \$2,400,000. This estimate is based on Calderwood & Harkness\'s experience with PLR submissions of comparable complexity and scope. The estimate is subject to revision based on the complexity of IRS interactions, the number of supplemental submission letters required, and the extent of coordination with foreign counsel and other advisors.

> • **Estimated Disbursements:** \$85,000. This estimate includes the IRS user fee of \$38,000 (per the fee schedule set forth in Rev. Proc. 2025-1), travel expenses for the pre-submission conference at IRS headquarters in Washington, D.C., courier and filing costs, and other out-of-pocket expenses.

> • **Billing Cycle:** Monthly, with invoices rendered on or about the first business day of each month for services performed in the preceding month. Payment is due within thirty (30) days of invoice date.

> • **Fee Cap:** There is no fee cap on this engagement. The matter is billed on a time-and-materials basis. Calderwood & Harkness will provide quarterly budget updates to Mr. Dalmqvist and Ms. Narasimhan, and will promptly notify the client if actual or projected fees are expected to exceed the upper end of the estimated range.
**[III. Background and Business Context]{.underline}**
**[A. Existing Fund Platform Structure]{.underline}**

Solara currently operates its investment activities through six parallel fund vehicles organized across three jurisdictions --- Delaware, the Cayman Islands, and Luxembourg. The parallel fund structure was established to accommodate the differing tax, regulatory, and treaty requirements of Solara\'s diverse investor base, which includes U.S. taxable investors, U.S. tax-exempt institutional investors, and non-U.S. investors from multiple jurisdictions.
The six existing fund vehicles, together with their key attributes, are described below:
**Fund IV Vehicles:**

1\. **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP** --- A Delaware limited partnership with total capital commitments of \$4.2 billion (vintage 2021), approximately 72% deployed as of March 31, 2025. EIN: 85-2103748. General Partner: Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC. This vehicle serves as the main domestic fund for U.S. taxable investors.

2\. **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP** --- A Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with total capital commitments of \$1.85 billion, operating as a parallel fund for non-U.S. investors and U.S. tax-exempt investors seeking UBTI blocker benefits. EIN: 98-6241503. CIMA Registration: MF-72491. General Partner: Solara Offshore GP Ltd. Registered office: Harborstone Corporate Services Ltd., P.O. Box 2714, 94 Solaris Avenue, George Town, Grand Cayman KY1-1111.

3\. **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- A Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with total capital commitments of €1.15 billion (approximately \$1.24 billion at 1.08 EUR/USD), established to provide treaty access and regulatory familiarity for European and Asian institutional investors. EIN: 98-6241571. Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (\"RCS\"): B 248193. General Partner: Solara Luxembourg Management S.à r.l. (RCS B 248194). Registered office: 14, rue Jean-Pierre Brasseur, L-1258 Luxembourg.
**Fund V Vehicles:**

4\. **Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP** --- A Delaware limited partnership with total capital commitments of \$5.6 billion (vintage 2023), approximately 38% deployed as of March 31, 2025. EIN: 88-3467219. General Partner: Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC. This vehicle serves as the main domestic fund for U.S. taxable investors in the current generation of investments.

5\. **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-A (Cayman) LP** --- A Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with total capital commitments of \$2.45 billion, serving as the parallel fund for non-U.S. investors and U.S. tax-exempt investors. EIN: 98-7891234. CIMA Registration: MF-89103. Registered office: Harborstone Corporate Services Ltd., George Town, Grand Cayman.

6\. **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- A Luxembourg special limited partnership with total capital commitments of €1.38 billion (approximately \$1.49 billion at 1.08 EUR/USD). EIN: 98-7891267. RCS: B 271056. Registered office: 14, rue Jean-Pierre Brasseur, L-1258 Luxembourg.
**Investor Base Allocation:**
The allocation of investors across the fund vehicles follows a well-established pattern based on the tax status and domicile of each investor:

> • *U.S. taxable investors* invest through the Delaware main funds (Fund IV LP and Fund V LP). This category includes U.S. taxable institutional investors and family offices. For example, Argyle Family Office Holdings LLC, a U.S. taxable family office, holds commitments of \$95 million in Fund IV LP and \$130 million in Fund V LP.

> • *U.S. tax-exempt investors* invest through the Cayman parallel vehicles to obtain UBTI blocker benefits, thereby avoiding the recognition of unrelated business taxable income under IRC §§ 511--514 that might otherwise arise from leveraged investments or operating business income. Representative U.S. tax-exempt investors include the Pinnacle State Employees\' Retirement System (\$275 million committed to Fund IV-A Cayman; \$340 million committed to Fund V-A Cayman) and the Grandview University Endowment (\$120 million committed to Fund IV-A Cayman; \$185 million committed to Fund V-A Cayman).

> • *Non-U.S. investors* invest through the Cayman or Luxembourg vehicles based on treaty access and regulatory considerations applicable to each investor\'s jurisdiction of domicile. Representative non-U.S. investors include Nordhaven Sovereign Wealth Fund (\$380 million committed to Fund IV-A Cayman; \$500 million committed to Fund V-A Cayman), which invests through the Cayman vehicles, and Kestrel Pacific Insurance Group, a Singapore-domiciled insurer (€200 million committed to Fund IV-B Luxembourg; €275 million committed to Fund V-B Luxembourg), which invests through the Luxembourg vehicles for European treaty access and Solvency II regulatory reporting purposes.
**[B. Business Rationale for the Reorganization]{.underline}**

Solara\'s management team has determined that the existing six-vehicle parallel fund structure has become operationally burdensome and, in light of evolving international tax rules, increasingly less advantageous from a tax perspective. The proposed reorganization is motivated by four principal business considerations:

**Operational Cost Reduction.** Solara currently incurs approximately \$3.8 million annually in duplicative offshore administration, audit, and regulatory compliance fees across the parallel structures. These costs include annual fees payable to Harborstone Corporate Services Ltd. for Cayman registered office services, annual fees payable to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (\"CSSF\") in Luxembourg, annual audit fees for the separate financial statements required for each offshore vehicle, and administration fees payable to Clarendon Fund Services Ltd. for NAV calculation and investor reporting across multiple parallel entities. Consolidation into a single master fund with two feeder vehicles is expected to yield meaningful annual cost savings.

**Pillar Two GloBE Rules.** The OECD Inclusive Framework\'s Pillar Two Global Anti-Base Erosion (\"GloBE\") rules, as implemented by Luxembourg through the Grand Ducal law transposing EU Directive 2022/2523, become effective for Solara\'s Luxembourg entities beginning in fiscal year 2025. The GloBE rules impose a minimum effective tax rate of 15% on the income of constituent entities within large multinational groups. While the Luxembourg SCSp structures were historically designed to provide tax transparency and treaty benefits, the incremental compliance burden and potential top-up tax exposure under the GloBE rules diminish the continuing benefit of maintaining separate Luxembourg fund vehicles.

**FATCA and CRS Simplification.** The existing multi-jurisdictional structure requires separate Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (\"FATCA\") reporting under intergovernmental agreements applicable to each of the Cayman Islands and Luxembourg, as well as Common Reporting Standard (\"CRS\") reporting under the Cayman Tax Information Authority (International Tax Compliance) Regulations and Luxembourg\'s CRS implementing legislation. Consolidation of the offshore vehicles into Cayman-domiciled feeders that invest through a single Delaware master fund will reduce the number of reporting financial institutions and simplify ongoing compliance obligations.

**LP-Requested Governance Simplification.** Several of Solara\'s largest limited partners have expressed a preference for a simplified fund governance structure that reduces the number of separate limited partnership agreements, advisory committee structures, and consent processes to which they are subject. The reorganization responds to this investor feedback by creating a streamlined architecture in which investment decisions and governance matters are centralized at the master fund level.
**[C. Key Portfolio Company Interests Involved]{.underline}**

The proposed reorganization will result in the transfer of portfolio company interests currently held by the four legacy offshore vehicles into the newly established Consolidated Master Fund LP. The six existing fund vehicles collectively hold interests in twenty-three portfolio companies --- eleven in the Fund IV vehicles and twelve in the Fund V vehicles. The portfolio spans the digital infrastructure and enterprise SaaS sectors.

The following representative portfolio company holdings, which are among the largest positions being transferred and which illustrate the range of entity types, asset values, and built-in gain positions involved, are described below for context:

> • **NovaBright Data Systems Inc.** --- A Delaware corporation engaged in the operation of hyperscale data center facilities in Northern Virginia, Dallas, and Phoenix. Fair market value: \$890 million. Adjusted tax basis: \$520 million. Built-in gain: \$370 million. Ownership: Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP holds 60%; Fund IV LP holds 40%.

> • **Crestline Cloud Solutions LLC** --- A Delaware limited liability company classified as a disregarded entity for U.S. federal income tax purposes, operating a cloud-based enterprise SaaS platform for supply chain management. Fair market value: €340 million (\$367 million at 1.08 EUR/USD). Adjusted tax basis: €195 million (\$211 million). Built-in gain: €145 million (\$156 million). Ownership: Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp holds 100%.

> • **Veridian Edge Computing Corp.** --- A Delaware corporation providing edge computing infrastructure and managed services to telecommunications carriers and enterprise customers. Fair market value: \$1.12 billion. Adjusted tax basis: \$780 million. Built-in gain: \$340 million. Ownership: Fund V-A (Cayman) LP holds 55%; Fund V LP holds 45%.

> • **Thorngate Fiber Networks LP** --- A Delaware limited partnership that owns and operates metropolitan and long-haul fiber-optic network assets across the northeastern United States. Fair market value: \$670 million. Adjusted tax basis: \$490 million. Built-in gain: \$180 million. Ownership: Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP holds 100%.

> • **Helix SaaS Holdings Ltd.** --- A Cayman Islands exempted company serving as a holding company for a portfolio of enterprise SaaS businesses focused on financial services technology. Fair market value: \$445 million. Adjusted tax basis: \$310 million. Built-in gain: \$135 million. Ownership: Fund V-A (Cayman) LP holds 100%.

The remaining eighteen portfolio company interests are of comparable character and will be detailed in the asset schedules prepared as part of the PLR exhibits. The aggregate financial summary of all assets being transferred is set forth in Section IV.G below.
**[IV. Description of the Proposed Reorganization]{.underline}**
**[A. Overview --- Five-Step Integrated Transaction]{.underline}**

The proposed reorganization is structured as a five-step integrated transaction designed to consolidate the four legacy offshore fund vehicles --- Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP, Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp, Fund V-A (Cayman) LP, and Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp --- into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure with two Cayman-domiciled feeder vehicles.

The target effective date for completion of all five steps is **December 1, 2025**. Each step has been sequenced to optimize operational logistics, accommodate regulatory lead times in the Cayman Islands and Luxembourg, and minimize the period during which legacy offshore vehicles and new entities will coexist. The five steps are designed to be treated as an integrated transaction for U.S. federal income tax purposes, and the PLR request will present them as such. However, the steps are also designed to be independently defensible under the applicable Internal Revenue Code provisions in the event the IRS were to disaggregate the transaction for analytical purposes.
The five steps are summarized below and described in detail in Sections IV.B through IV.F.
**[B. Step 1 --- Formation of New Entities (Target: September 15, 2025)]{.underline}**
The first step involves the formation of four new legal entities that will constitute the post-reorganization consolidated fund architecture:

1\. **Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC** --- A Delaware limited liability company to be formed under the Delaware Limited Liability Company Act, 6 Del. C. § 18-101 *et seq.*, which will serve as the general partner of the Consolidated Master Fund LP. This entity will be managed by Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC and will hold a nominal general partner interest in the Master Fund.

2\. **Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP** --- A Delaware limited partnership to be formed under the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act, which will serve as the master fund vehicle into which all portfolio assets currently held by the four legacy offshore vehicles will be contributed. The general partner of the Master Fund LP will be Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC.

3\. **Solara International Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- A Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to be formed under the Cayman Islands Exempted Limited Partnership Act (as revised), which will serve as the feeder vehicle for non-U.S. investors who currently invest through the Fund IV-A and Fund V-A Cayman parallel vehicles and through the Fund IV-B and Fund V-B Luxembourg vehicles.

4\. **Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- A Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to be formed under the same Cayman Islands legislation, which will serve as the feeder vehicle for U.S. tax-exempt investors to mitigate exposure to unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") under IRC §§ 511--514.

Concurrently with or promptly following the formation of each new entity, IRS Form 8832 (Entity Classification Election) will be filed with the IRS under Treasury Regulation § 301.7701-3 to elect classification as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes for each of the three new entities required to make such an election --- namely, the Consolidated Master Fund LP, the International Feeder (Cayman) LP, and the Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP. The effective dates of the check-the-box elections will be coordinated with the target dates for the subsequent reorganization steps to ensure that the new entities are classified as partnerships prior to the contribution transactions described in Steps 2 through 4. The 75-day retroactivity rule under Treasury Regulation § 301.7701-3(c)(1)(iii) will be taken into account in establishing the election effective dates.
**[C. Step 2 --- Contribution of Fund IV-A Cayman Assets (Target: October 1, 2025)]{.underline}**

In Step 2, **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP** will contribute all of its portfolio company assets to **Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP** in exchange for a limited partnership interest in the Consolidated Master Fund LP.
The aggregate financial parameters of the Step 2 contribution are as follows:
**Metric**                                           **Amount**
Aggregate Fair Market Value of Contributed Assets    \$2.31 billion
Aggregate Adjusted Tax Basis of Contributed Assets   \$1.62 billion
Aggregate Built-In Gain                              \$690 million

The intended U.S. federal income tax treatment of the Step 2 contribution is as a tax-free contribution under IRC § 721(a), pursuant to which no gain or loss is recognized by Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP or by the Consolidated Master Fund LP upon the contribution. The adjusted tax basis of each contributed asset will carry over to the Consolidated Master Fund LP under IRC § 723, and the holding period of each contributed asset will include the period during which the asset was held by Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP under IRC § 1223(2).

As part of the tax analysis supporting the PLR request, Calderwood & Harkness will analyze whether the contribution implicates the investment company exception under IRC § 721(b). This provision denies tax-free treatment to a contribution to a partnership that would be treated as an \"investment company\" within the meaning of IRC § 351(e) if the partnership were a corporation. The analysis will address whether the Consolidated Master Fund LP\'s portfolio of operating company interests --- consisting of data center operators, fiber-optic network businesses, edge computing platforms, and SaaS enterprises --- constitutes a portfolio of \"stocks, securities, or other investment assets\" for purposes of this analysis.
**[D. Step 3 --- Contribution of Fund IV-B Luxembourg Assets (Target: October 15, 2025)]{.underline}**

In Step 3, **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** will contribute all of its portfolio company assets to **Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP** in exchange for a limited partnership interest in the Consolidated Master Fund LP.
The aggregate financial parameters of the Step 3 contribution are as follows:
**Metric**                     **EUR Amount**          **USD Amount (at 1.08)**
Aggregate Fair Market Value    €1.07 billion           \$1.16 billion
Aggregate Adjusted Tax Basis   €782 million            \$844.6 million
Aggregate Built-In Gain        €288 million            \$311 million
The intended U.S. federal income tax treatment is the same as Step 2: a tax-free contribution under IRC § 721(a) with carryover basis under IRC § 723 and holding period tacking under IRC § 1223(2).

Step 3 raises additional cross-border tax considerations that are not present in Step 2. Because Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp is a foreign partnership contributing assets to a domestic partnership (the Consolidated Master Fund LP), Calderwood & Harkness will analyze the applicability of IRC § 367 to the contribution. Specifically, the PLR request will address the position that IRC § 367 does not apply to this transfer because, by its terms, IRC § 367(a) applies to transfers of property by a United States person *to a foreign corporation*, and IRC § 367(b) applies to exchanges described in certain enumerated provisions *involving a foreign corporation*. Neither subsection, by its terms, applies to a transfer by a foreign partnership to a domestic partnership. The PLR request will seek an affirmative ruling that IRC § 367 is inapplicable to the Step 3 contribution.

With respect to Luxembourg tax consequences, no Luxembourg capital gains tax is expected to arise at the SCSp level on the transfer, based on Article 3(2) of the Luxembourg law of July 12, 2013 (*Loi du 12 juillet 2013 relative aux gestionnaires de fonds d\'investissement alternatifs*), which provides for tax transparency of the SCSp. However, Calderwood & Harkness expressly disclaims any responsibility for the analysis of Luxembourg tax law, which will be addressed by Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l., as set forth in Section VI.A below.

Additionally, Calderwood & Harkness will analyze whether the contribution gives rise to a deemed disposition triggering withholding obligations under IRC § 1446, which imposes a withholding tax on effectively connected taxable income allocable to foreign partners.
**[E. Step 4 --- Contribution of Fund V Offshore Assets (Target: November 1, 2025)]{.underline}**
In Step 4, the two Fund V offshore vehicles will contribute their respective portfolio company assets to the Consolidated Master Fund LP:
**Fund V-A (Cayman) LP Contribution:**
**Metric**                          **Amount**
Aggregate Fair Market Value         \$2.89 billion
Aggregate Adjusted Tax Basis        \$2.34 billion
Aggregate Built-In Gain             \$550 million
**Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp Contribution:**
**Metric**                     **EUR Amount**          **USD Amount (at 1.08)**
Aggregate Fair Market Value    €1.29 billion           \$1.39 billion
Aggregate Adjusted Tax Basis   €1.14 billion           \$1.23 billion
Aggregate Built-In Gain        €150 million            \$162 million

The intended U.S. federal income tax treatment is the same as described in Steps 2 and 3 above: tax-free contributions under IRC § 721(a) with carryover basis under IRC § 723 and holding period tacking under IRC § 1223(2). The IRC § 367 inapplicability analysis and IRC § 1446 withholding analysis applicable to the Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp contribution will mirror the analysis described in connection with Step 3.
**[F. Step 5 --- Dissolution of Legacy Offshore Vehicles and LP Migration (Target: December 1, 2025)]{.underline}**

In Step 5, the four legacy offshore vehicles --- Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP, Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp, Fund V-A (Cayman) LP, and Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp --- will dissolve and distribute their respective limited partnership interests in the Consolidated Master Fund LP to their existing limited partners in liquidation of those limited partners\' interests in the dissolving vehicles.
Following the dissolution distributions:

> • **Non-U.S. limited partners** will contribute their distributed Master Fund LP interests to the newly formed **Solara International Feeder (Cayman) LP**, receiving limited partnership interests in the International Feeder in exchange.

> • **U.S. tax-exempt limited partners** will contribute their distributed Master Fund LP interests to the newly formed **Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP**, receiving limited partnership interests in the Tax-Exempt Feeder in exchange.

The intended U.S. federal income tax treatment of the dissolution distributions is as tax-free distributions under IRC § 731(a), pursuant to which no gain or loss is recognized by the distributing partnership or the distributee partners except to the extent that money distributed exceeds a partner\'s adjusted basis in its partnership interest.

A critical aspect of the Step 5 analysis is whether the limited partnership interests in the Consolidated Master Fund LP distributed by the dissolving vehicles constitute \"marketable securities\" within the meaning of IRC § 731(c). If so, the distribution of such interests could be treated as a distribution of money under IRC § 731(c)(1), potentially triggering gain recognition. Calderwood & Harkness will analyze whether the Consolidated Master Fund LP interests are \"marketable securities\" as defined in IRC § 731(c)(2), which generally requires that the securities be actively traded or, in certain cases, that they be of a type that is actively traded. The PLR request will seek a ruling that the Master Fund LP interests are not marketable securities within the meaning of § 731(c)(2), on the basis that they are interests in a newly formed, non-publicly traded limited partnership that are not actively traded on an established securities market or readily tradable on a secondary market or the substantial equivalent thereof.
**Resulting Post-Reorganization Structure.** Upon completion of all five steps, the resulting fund structure will consist of:
> • **Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP** (Delaware), holding the consolidated portfolio of twenty-three portfolio companies previously held by the four legacy offshore vehicles.
> • **Solara International Feeder (Cayman) LP**, holding a limited partnership interest in the Master Fund LP, through which all non-U.S. investors will invest.
> • **Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP**, holding a limited partnership interest in the Master Fund LP, through which all U.S. tax-exempt investors will invest.

> • **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP** and **Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP** (each a Delaware LP), which will continue to hold their existing portfolio company interests directly and will co-invest alongside the Consolidated Master Fund LP. U.S. taxable investors will remain as limited partners in these vehicles.
**[G. Aggregate Financial Summary]{.underline}**
The aggregate financial parameters of the proposed reorganization are as follows:
**Metric**                                                                            **Amount**
Total Fair Market Value of Assets Being Transferred to the Consolidated Master Fund   \$7.75 billion
Total Aggregate Adjusted Tax Basis                                                    \$6.03 billion
Total Aggregate Built-In Gain                                                         \$1.72 billion
Aggregate Liabilities Assumed by the Consolidated Master Fund                         \$1.34 billion
Total Portfolio Companies Transferred                                                 23 (11 from Fund IV vehicles; 12 from Fund V vehicles)

The magnitude of the aggregate built-in gain of \$1.72 billion underscores the critical importance of obtaining a favorable PLR confirming the tax-free treatment of the contribution and distribution transactions. Any adverse ruling, or failure to obtain the requested rulings, could expose the fund vehicles and their limited partners to significant gain recognition in the year of the reorganization.
**[V. Scope of Work --- Specific Deliverables]{.underline}**

The following subsections describe each category of deliverables that Calderwood & Harkness will produce in connection with this engagement. Except as expressly noted below, all deliverables will be prepared by the Calderwood & Harkness engagement team and will be subject to review and approval by Leonard Cross (Responsible Partner) and Sylvia Hartwell (Billing Partner) prior to delivery to the client or submission to any third party.
**[A. Tax Analysis Memoranda]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will prepare comprehensive tax analysis memoranda addressing each material provision of the Internal Revenue Code and Treasury Regulations implicated by the proposed reorganization. These memoranda are intended to serve dual purposes: (i) to provide Solara\'s management and tax team with a thorough analysis of the tax consequences of each step of the reorganization, and (ii) to form the analytical foundation for the positions taken in the PLR request.
The following memoranda will be prepared:

1\. **Master Tax Analysis Memorandum** --- A comprehensive overview memorandum analyzing the entire five-step reorganization as an integrated transaction, identifying each material IRC provision implicated, summarizing the intended tax treatment of each step, and flagging any areas of material uncertainty or risk.

2\. **IRC § 721(a) Contribution Analysis (Steps 2--4)** --- A detailed memorandum analyzing the application of IRC § 721(a) to the contributions by the four legacy offshore vehicles of their portfolio company interests to the Consolidated Master Fund LP, including discussion of the requirements for nonrecognition treatment, the effect of carryover basis under IRC § 723, and holding period tacking under IRC § 1223(2).

We are pleased to confirm the engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness,\" the \"Firm,\" \"we,\" or \"us\") by Ardent Capital Management LLC (the \"ManCo\" or the \"Client\") to serve as legal counsel in connection with the matters described herein. This letter (the \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions upon which we will provide legal services to the Client in connection with this engagement.
**[1. Purpose and Engagement]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter confirms that Calderwood & Harkness has been engaged by the ManCo to serve as legal counsel in connection with a comprehensive restructuring of the management company and realignment of economics among the principals of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"Fund\"), a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$2.8 billion in total commitments. The ManCo is a Delaware limited liability company and a registered investment adviser with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the \"SEC\") under CRD #298417. The Fund\'s sole general partner is Ardent Capital GP III LLC (the \"General Partner\"), a Delaware limited liability company.

The engagement encompasses the formation of new holding entities, the negotiation of separation arrangements with departing principals, the realignment of carried interest and management fee economics among continuing and next-generation principals, the solicitation of necessary limited partner consents, compliance with existing side-letter obligations, and related tax structuring. The scope of the representation, the personnel assigned to the engagement, the fee arrangement, and other terms and conditions governing this engagement are set forth in the sections that follow.
**[2. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**

The engagement will comprise the following principal workstreams, each of which is described in greater detail below. We understand that the scope of the engagement may evolve as the restructuring progresses; any material expansion of the scope described herein will be discussed with the Client in advance.
**2.1 Entity Restructuring**
Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the restructuring of the organizational hierarchy of the Ardent Capital platform, including:

\(a\) Advising on the formation of a new Delaware limited liability company, to be named Ardent Capital Holdings LLC (\"HoldCo\"), which will serve as a parent holding company for both the General Partner and the ManCo, thereby consolidating the principals\' economic interests and governance rights in a single vehicle at the top of the organizational structure.

\(b\) Advising on the formation of an intermediate entity, Ardent GP Intermediate LLC (\"GP Intermediate\"), as a wholly owned subsidiary of HoldCo and the sole member of the General Partner. GP Intermediate will serve as an interposing entity between HoldCo and the General Partner, facilitating the allocation of carried interest economics and providing structural flexibility for the admission of future principals and the potential establishment of successor funds.

\(c\) Drafting and negotiating limited liability company agreements for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including provisions governing capital contributions, profit and loss allocations, distribution waterfalls, governance (including voting and consent requirements), transfer restrictions, withdrawal and removal mechanics, non-compete and non-solicitation covenants, and such other provisions as may be appropriate.

\(d\) Preparing amended and restated limited liability company agreements for the General Partner and the ManCo to reflect the new holding-company structure, including modifications to membership interest provisions, management and officer provisions, and capital account and allocation provisions necessitated by the interposition of HoldCo and GP Intermediate.

\(e\) Preparing and filing Certificates of Formation with the Delaware Secretary of State for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, together with any ancillary filings or registrations required in connection with the formation and qualification of such entities.

\(f\) Preparing Amendment No. 1 to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund (the \"LPA\") to reflect the structural changes to the General Partner, including any required modifications to the definitions, representations, and governance provisions of the LPA necessitated by the interposition of GP Intermediate and HoldCo above the General Partner.
**2.2 Economics Realignment**
Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the reallocation and documentation of the economic arrangements among the principals of the Fund, including:

\(a\) Advising on the reallocation of carried interest percentages and management fee profit-share allocations among the remaining and next-generation principals, taking into account the departure of the principals described in Section 2.3 below, the contributions of continuing principals, and the Firm\'s understanding of the Client\'s objectives with respect to the incentivization and retention of key personnel.

\(b\) Drafting an amended and restated Carried Interest Allocation Agreement reflecting the revised carried interest percentages applicable to each principal, including vesting schedules, forfeiture and clawback provisions, and mechanics for the allocation of carried interest among HoldCo members through the GP Intermediate and General Partner chain.

\(c\) Drafting a Management Fee Sharing and Profit Allocation Agreement at the HoldCo level, setting forth the allocation of management fee revenue among HoldCo members, including base compensation allocations, discretionary bonus pools, and distribution priorities.
\(d\) Revising the co-investment allocation policy to reflect the revised principal group and to address any changes in co-investment rights and priorities resulting from the restructuring.
**2.3 Departing Principal Separation**
Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the negotiation and documentation of separation arrangements for two departing principals:
\(a\) **David Kellner** (Senior Partner), who is retiring from the Ardent Capital platform; and
\(b\) **Joanna Trask** (Partner), who is departing voluntarily.
In connection with each departing principal, the Firm will:

> \(i\) Draft comprehensive separation and release agreements, addressing, among other things, the departing principal\'s resignation from all positions with the ManCo, the General Partner, HoldCo (if applicable), and all affiliated entities; mutual releases of claims; confidentiality, non-disparagement, non-solicitation, and (as applicable) non-competition covenants; cooperation obligations; and any ongoing compensation or benefits arrangements.

> \(ii\) Draft carry retention and clawback side letters, specifying the portion of carried interest to be retained by each departing principal with respect to investments made during his or her tenure, the clawback obligations applicable thereto, and the mechanics for the calculation and payment of any retained carry distributions.

> \(iii\) As applicable, draft a senior advisor agreement in favor of Mr. Kellner, setting forth the terms of any ongoing advisory role, including the scope of services, compensation, expense reimbursement, and termination provisions.

> \(iv\) Coordinate, as necessary and appropriate, with Whitford & Chase LLP, counsel to the departing principals, led by Richard Beaulieu, Esq., in connection with the negotiation and finalization of all separation documentation.
**2.4 LP Consent and Side-Letter Compliance**
Calderwood & Harkness will advise on all limited partner notification, consent, and compliance matters arising from the restructuring, including:

\(a\) Preparing materials for notification to, and solicitation of consent from, the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA, including a detailed memorandum describing the restructuring and its implications for the Fund and its limited partners.

\(b\) Analyzing compliance with the Fund\'s fourteen (14) existing side letters, with particular attention to key-person provisions under Section 5.2 of the LPA and any expanded or supplemental key-person provisions contained in certain side letters, to determine whether the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask or the structural changes contemplated by the restructuring trigger key-person events, consent requirements, or notification obligations under any such side letter.

\(c\) Preparing LP notification letters to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund, describing the restructuring, the changes to the General Partner structure, the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, and any other information required to be disclosed under the LPA or the applicable side letters.

\(d\) Advising on the preparation and filing of an amended SEC Form ADV (Parts 1 and 2) to reflect the restructuring, and advising on any other regulatory filings or notifications required in connection with the restructuring, including any applicable state regulatory filings.
**2.5 Tax Structuring**
Calderwood & Harkness will provide tax analysis and structuring advice in connection with the restructuring, including:

\(a\) Federal income tax analysis of the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including the tax treatment of the contribution or transfer of interests in the General Partner and the ManCo to HoldCo.
\(b\) Delaware tax analysis of the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including any applicable Delaware franchise taxes, formation taxes, or annual reporting obligations.

\(c\) Federal income tax analysis of the reallocation of carried interest among the principals, including the application of Section 1061 of the Internal Revenue Code and any implications arising from the modification of existing partnership interests.

\(d\) Tax analysis of the economic arrangements with departing principals, including the characterization of carry retention payments and the tax treatment of any consideration paid in connection with the separation arrangements.

\(e\) Section 704(b) and Section 704(c) analysis of built-in gain allocations with respect to existing Fund investments, including the impact of the restructuring on the allocation of built-in gains and losses among the principals and the mechanics for tracking and allocating such amounts through the revised entity structure.

\(f\) All tax structuring advice under this engagement will be provided by Sylvia Hartwell, Specialist Partner (Tax), who will coordinate as necessary with the Client\'s independent accountants at Heathrow Whitman & Co.
**2.6 Limitations on Scope**

The scope of this engagement is limited to the matters described in Sections 2.1 through 2.5 above. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the following matters are expressly excluded from the scope of this engagement:

\(a\) Routine fund operations, portfolio company transactions, and ongoing limited partner communications unrelated to the restructuring described herein. We understand that such matters will continue to be handled by Pemberton Hale LLP (Victoria Langford, Partner), which serves as the Fund\'s existing fund formation and operations counsel.

\(b\) Accounting, auditing, and valuation services, which we understand are provided by Heathrow Whitman & Co. (accountants and auditors) and Broadleaf Consulting Group (valuation), respectively. Nothing in this engagement shall be construed as the provision of accounting, auditing, or valuation advice by Calderwood & Harkness.

\(c\) Representation of any departing principal, including David Kellner and Joanna Trask, in connection with the restructuring or any other matter. Each departing principal is separately represented by Whitford & Chase LLP.
\(d\) Representation of any limited partner of the Fund in connection with the restructuring or any other matter.

To the extent matters arise during the course of this engagement that fall outside the scope described herein but that may benefit from our involvement, we will discuss with the Client whether and on what terms such matters should be added to the scope of this engagement or addressed through a separate engagement.

Fees for services rendered in connection with this engagement will be charged on an hourly basis at the following standard rates:

Partner                             \$1,650
Specialist Partner                  \$1,750
Senior Associate                    \$950
Associate                           \$750

The foregoing rates are subject to annual adjustment, typically effective January 1 of each year. In the event of any rate adjustment during the term of this engagement, the Firm will communicate such adjustment to the Client in advance. Adjusted rates will apply to services rendered on or after the effective date of the adjustment.
**4.2 Estimated Fee Range**

Based on the anticipated scope and complexity of the engagement as described in Section 2 above, and taking into account the number of workstreams, the anticipated volume of document drafting and negotiation, and the extent of LP consent and regulatory compliance work expected to be required, we estimate that total professional fees for this engagement will fall within the range of **\$850,000 to \$1,100,000**.

Actual fees may vary from this estimate based on a number of factors, including (without limitation) the ultimate scope and complexity of the work, the nature and duration of negotiations with Whitford & Chase LLP on behalf of the departing principals, the extent and complexity of LP consent solicitation and side-letter compliance matters, the number and complexity of tax structuring issues that arise, and any expansion of the scope of the engagement beyond the matters described herein. 10: 
11: **Reflecting comments of Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC received May 16, 2025, and Calderwood & Harkness LLP revisions dated May 22, 2025**
12: 
13: **Prepared by Calderwood & Harkness LLP**
14: 
15: CONFIDENTIAL --- For Discussion Purposes Only --- Subject to Revision
16: 
17: This document is a preliminary draft prepared for discussion purposes and is subject to further revision and negotiation. This draft does not constitute a binding offer or agreement by any party. Distribution of this document is restricted to intended recipients and their legal and financial advisors. All rights reserved.
18: 
19: **AGREEMENT OF LIMITED PARTNERSHIP**
20: 
21: **OF**
22: 
23: **HARROWGATE PRIVATE EQUITY FUND V LP**
24: 
25: This Agreement of Limited Partnership (this **\"Agreement\"**) of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the **\"Partnership\"** or the **\"Fund\"**), is entered into as of the date of the First Close (as defined below) by and among Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, as the general partner (the **\"General Partner\"** or **\"GP\"**), and each Person who is admitted as a limited partner of the Partnership (each, a **\"Limited Partner\"** or **\"LP\"** and, collectively, the **\"Limited Partners\"**), in each case in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth herein. The General Partner and the Limited Partners are sometimes referred to herein individually as a **\"Partner\"** and collectively as the **\"Partners.\"**
26: 
27: **RECITALS**
28: 
29: **WHEREAS**, the General Partner has caused a Certificate of Limited Partnership to be filed (or to be filed on or prior to the date hereof) with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, forming the Partnership as a limited partnership under and pursuant to the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act, 6 Del. C. § 17-101 *et seq.*, as amended from time to time (the **\"Act\"**);
30: 
31: **WHEREAS**, the General Partner desires to establish the Fund as a private equity investment vehicle for the purpose of making equity and equity-related investments, directly or indirectly, primarily in North American mid-market and upper-mid-market companies in the industrials, business services, healthcare services, and technology-enabled services sectors;
32: 
33: **WHEREAS**, the General Partner is the sole general partner of the Partnership and is a Delaware limited liability company, the sole member of which is Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the **\"Sponsor\"**);
34: 
35: **WHEREAS**, the Sponsor has sponsored and managed four predecessor private equity funds (Harrowgate Private Equity Fund I LP through Harrowgate Private Equity Fund IV LP) and manages approximately \$5.8 billion in aggregate assets under management as of the date hereof;
36: 
37: **WHEREAS**, each Limited Partner desires to make a capital commitment to the Partnership on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement and in the Subscription Agreement executed by such Limited Partner; and
38: 
39: **WHEREAS**, the Partners desire to set forth their respective rights, obligations, and duties with respect to the Partnership.
40: 
41: **NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Partners hereby agree as follows:
42: 
43: **[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**
44: 
45: **[Section 1.1 --- Defined Terms]{.underline}**
46: 
47: As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:
48: 
49: **\"Act\"** means the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act, 6 Del. C. § 17-101 *et seq.*, as it may be amended from time to time, and any successor statute thereto.
50: 
51: **\"Adjusted Capital Account\"** means, with respect to each Partner, such Partner\'s Capital Account as of the end of the relevant Fiscal Year or other applicable period, as adjusted in accordance with Treasury Regulation Sections 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(4), (5), and (6), after giving effect to the following adjustments: (a) credit to such Capital Account any amounts that such Partner is obligated to restore or is treated as obligated to restore pursuant to Treasury Regulation Sections 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(c), 1.704-2(g)(1), and 1.704-2(i)(5); and (b) debit to such Capital Account the items described in Treasury Regulation Sections 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(4), (5), and (6). The foregoing definition is intended to comply with the provisions of Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d) and shall be interpreted consistently therewith.
52: 
53: **\"Affiliate\"** means, with respect to any Person, any other Person that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with, such Person. For purposes of this definition, **\"control\"** (including the correlative terms \"controlling,\" \"controlled by,\" and \"under common control with\") means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of a Person, whether through ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise, and shall be deemed to exist when a Person owns, directly or indirectly, fifty percent (50%) or more of the outstanding voting securities or equity interests of the applicable entity. Notwithstanding the foregoing, no Limited Partner shall be deemed to be an Affiliate of the General Partner, the Sponsor, or any other Limited Partner solely by reason of such Limited Partner\'s investment in the Fund.
54: 
55: **\"Aggregate Commitments\"** means the aggregate Capital Commitments of all Partners (including the GP Commitment), as set forth in the Schedule of Partners, as the same may be updated from time to time. At the hard cap, Aggregate Commitments shall not exceed Two Billion Dollars (\$2,000,000,000).
56: 
57: **\"Associate\"** means any member, partner, managing director, principal, officer, director, employee, or agent of the General Partner, the Sponsor, or any of their respective Affiliates.
58: 
59: **\"Benefit Plan Investor\"** means a \"benefit plan investor\" as defined in 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101(f)(2), as modified by Section 3(42) of ERISA, including (a) any \"employee benefit plan\" as defined in Section 3(3) of ERISA that is subject to Part 4 of Subtitle B of Title I of ERISA, (b) any \"plan\" as defined in Section 4975(e)(1) of the Code that is subject to Section 4975 of the Code, and (c) any entity whose underlying assets include \"plan assets\" by reason of a plan\'s investment in such entity.
60: 
61: **\"Blocker Entity\"** means HGF V blocker Corp., a Delaware C corporation formed for the benefit of certain tax-exempt or non-U.S. Limited Partners to mitigate UBTI or effectively connected income concerns, as the General Partner may determine to be appropriate in connection with the Fund\'s investment program.
62: 
63: **\"Bridge Financing\"** means any short-term Fund-level borrowing (whether under the Subscription Credit Facility or otherwise) used to fund Portfolio Investments or other Partnership obligations in advance of or in lieu of issuing Capital Calls, which borrowing shall not remain outstanding for more than one hundred eighty (180) consecutive days from the date of the applicable borrowing.
64: 
65: **\"Business Day\"** means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or a day on which commercial banks in New York, New York or Wilmington, Delaware are authorized or required by law or executive order to remain closed.
66: 
67: **\"Capital Account\"** means, with respect to each Partner, the capital account established and maintained for such Partner in accordance with Section 704(b) of the Code and Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv), as further described in Section 6.1 of this Agreement.
68: 
69: **\"Capital Call\"** or **\"Drawdown Notice\"** means a written notice issued by the General Partner to the Partners requiring such Partners to fund all or a portion of their unfunded Capital Commitments, specifying the aggregate amount of such capital contribution, the purpose thereof, and the date on which such funds are due, in accordance with Section 4.2 of this Agreement.
70: 
71: **\"Capital Commitment\"** means, with respect to each Partner, the aggregate amount that such Partner has committed to contribute to the Partnership as capital contributions, as set forth in such Partner\'s Subscription Agreement and reflected in the Schedule of Partners, as the same may be updated from time to time.
72: 
73: **\"Carried Interest\"** means the General Partner\'s right to receive twenty percent (20%) of Net Profits distributed in excess of the Preferred Return, as more fully described in Section 8.2 of this Agreement (Tiers 3 and 4 of the distribution waterfall).
74: 
75: **\"Carry Distribution\"** means any Distribution of Carried Interest to the General Partner pursuant to Tier 3 or Tier 4 of the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 8.2.
76: 
77: **\"Catch-Up\"** or **\"GP Catch-Up\"** means the distribution priority described in Tier 3 of Section 8.2, pursuant to which eighty percent (80%) of distributable amounts are allocated to the General Partner and twenty percent (20%) to the Limited Partners until the cumulative distributions to the General Partner under Tier 3 and Tier 4 equal twenty percent (20%) of the sum of all cumulative distributions under Tiers 2, 3, and 4.
78: 
79: **\"Cause\"** means (a) the commission of fraud or willful misconduct by the General Partner, any Key Person, or any Associate acting on behalf of the General Partner in connection with the affairs of the Partnership; (b) a material breach by the General Partner of this Agreement that is not cured within the applicable cure period set forth in Section 12.6; or (c) the voluntary or involuntary bankruptcy, insolvency, receivership, or dissolution of the General Partner.
80: 
81: **\"Clawback Amount\"** means the amount of excess Carried Interest subject to return by the General Partner to the Partnership pursuant to Article IX of this Agreement.
82: 
83: **\"Code\"** means the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended from time to time, and any successor statute thereto. References to specific sections of the Code shall be deemed to include corresponding provisions of any successor statute.
84: 
85: **\"Commitment Period\"** has the meaning ascribed to the term \"Investment Period.\"
86: 
87: **\"Concentration Limit\"** means, with respect to any single Portfolio Investment, twenty percent (20%) of Aggregate Commitments, measured at the time of the initial commitment to such Portfolio Investment (i.e., a maximum of Four Hundred Million Dollars (\$400,000,000) at the hard cap of Two Billion Dollars (\$2,000,000,000)), as more fully described in Section 5.3(a).
88: 
89: **\"Defaulting Partner\"** means any Partner that fails to fund its share of a Capital Call by the applicable funding date, as set forth in Section 4.9 of this Agreement, and that has not cured such failure within five (5) Business Days of the funding date.
90: 
91: **\"Distribution\"** means any distribution of cash, securities, or other property by the Partnership to one or more Partners, whether as a return of capital, a share of income or gain, or otherwise, as determined by the General Partner in accordance with this Agreement.
92: 
93: **\"Early Close discount\"** means the ten (10) basis point reduction in the Management Fee rate applicable to Limited Partners admitted to the Partnership at the First Close, as described in Section 7.1(c) of this Agreement (resulting in a Management Fee rate of 1.65% per annum on Capital Commitments during the Investment Period, in lieu of 1.75%).
94: 
95: **\"ERISA\"** means the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended from time to time, and any successor statute thereto, together with all rules and regulations promulgated thereunder.
96: 
97: **\"Excess Organizational Expenses\"** means Organizational Expenses incurred by the Partnership in excess of Three Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$3,500,000), which Excess Organizational Expenses shall be borne solely by the Sponsor and shall not be charged to the Partnership or any Partner.
98: 
99: **\"Excluded Co-Investment\"** means a co-investment opportunity offered alongside the Fund to one or more Limited Partners or third parties in accordance with Section 5.4, which co-investment is made through a separate co-investment vehicle or on a direct basis and is not treated as a Portfolio Investment of the Fund for purposes of this Agreement.
100: 
101: **\"Final Close\"** means the last date on which Limited Partners may be admitted to the Partnership and Capital Commitments accepted, which date shall be no later than the Final Close Deadline.
102: 
103: **\"Final Close Deadline\"** means February 15, 2027, being eighteen (18) months after the target date of the First Close.
104: 
105: **\"First Close\"** means the initial closing of Capital Commitments to the Partnership, targeted for August 15, 2025, at which the General Partner shall have accepted Capital Commitments aggregating at least Seven Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$750,000,000) (or such lesser amount as the General Partner may determine in its sole discretion).
106: 
107: **\"Fiscal Year\"** means the calendar year commencing on January 1 and ending on December 31 of each year; *provided*, that the first Fiscal Year of the Partnership shall commence on the date of the First Close and shall end on December 31 of such calendar year, and the final Fiscal Year of the Partnership shall end on the date of the final distribution of all Partnership assets and cancellation of the Certificate of Limited Partnership.
108: 
109: **\"For-Cause Removal\"** means the removal of the General Partner for Cause by a vote of a majority in interest of the Limited Partners (excluding GP-affiliated Capital Commitments) in accordance with Section 12.6(b).
110: 
111: **\"Fund\"** means Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, a Delaware limited partnership formed pursuant to this Agreement.
112: 
113: **\"Fund Expenses\"** means the ordinary and recurring expenses of the Partnership borne by the Partnership, as more fully described in Section 7.4 of this Agreement.
114: 
115: **\"General Partner\"** or **\"GP\"** means Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, the sole member of which is Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, in its capacity as the sole general partner of the Partnership, and any successor general partner admitted to the Partnership in accordance with this Agreement.
116: 
117: **\"GP Catch-Up\"** has the meaning set forth in the definition of \"Catch-Up\" above.
118: 
119: **\"GP Commitment\"** means the Capital Commitment of the General Partner (or its Affiliates) to the Partnership, which shall be equal to two and one-half percent (2.5%) of Aggregate Commitments (equal to Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000) at the hard cap of Two Billion Dollars (\$2,000,000,000)). The GP Commitment shall be funded pari passu with Capital Calls to the Limited Partners and on the same terms and conditions as the Capital Commitments of the Limited Partners, except that no Management Fee shall be charged with respect to the GP Commitment.

**AGREEMENT OF LIMITED PARTNERSHIP**
**HARROWGATE PRIVATE EQUITY FUND V LP**

This Agreement of Limited Partnership (this **\"Agreement\"**) of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the **\"Partnership\"** or the **\"Fund\"**), is entered into as of the date of the First Close (as defined below) by and among Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, as the general partner (the **\"General Partner\"** or **\"GP\"**), and each Person who is admitted as a limited partner of the Partnership (each, a **\"Limited Partner\"** or **\"LP\"** and, collectively, the **\"Limited Partners\"**), in each case in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth herein. The General Partner and the Limited Partners are sometimes referred to herein individually as a **\"Partner\"** and collectively as the **\"Partners.\"**
**RECITALS**

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner has caused a Certificate of Limited Partnership to be filed (or to be filed on or prior to the date hereof) with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, forming the Partnership as a limited partnership under and pursuant to the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act, 6 Del. C. § 17-101 *et seq.*, as amended from time to time (the **\"Act\"**);

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner desires to establish the Fund as a private equity investment vehicle for the purpose of making equity and equity-related investments, directly or indirectly, primarily in North American mid-market and upper-mid-market companies in the industrials, business services, healthcare services, and technology-enabled services sectors;

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner is the sole general partner of the Partnership and is a Delaware limited liability company, the sole member of which is Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the **\"Sponsor\"**);

**WHEREAS**, the Sponsor has sponsored and managed four predecessor private equity funds (Harrowgate Private Equity Fund I LP through Harrowgate Private Equity Fund IV LP) and manages approximately \$5.8 billion in aggregate assets under management as of the date hereof;

**WHEREAS**, each Limited Partner desires to make a capital commitment to the Partnership on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement and in the Subscription Agreement executed by such Limited Partner; and
**WHEREAS**, the Partners desire to set forth their respective rights, obligations, and duties with respect to the Partnership.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Partners hereby agree as follows:
**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**
**[Section 1.1 --- Defined Terms]{.underline}**
As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:
**\"Act\"** means the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act, 6 Del. C. § 17-101 *et seq.*, as it may be amended from time to time, and any successor statute thereto.

**\"Adjusted Capital Account\"** means, with respect to each Partner, such Partner\'s Capital Account as of the end of the relevant Fiscal Year or other applicable period, as adjusted in accordance with Treasury Regulation Sections 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(4), (5), and (6), after giving effect to the following adjustments: (a) credit to such Capital Account any amounts that such Partner is obligated to restore or is treated as obligated to restore pursuant to Treasury Regulation Sections 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(c), 1.704-2(g)(1), and 1.704-2(i)(5); and (b) debit to such Capital Account the items described in Treasury Regulation Sections 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(4), (5), and (6). The foregoing definition is intended to comply with the provisions of Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d) and shall be interpreted consistently therewith.

**\"Affiliate\"** means, with respect to any Person, any other Person that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with, such Person. For purposes of this definition, **\"control\"** (including the correlative terms \"controlling,\" \"controlled by,\" and \"under common control with\") means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of a Person, whether through ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise, and shall be deemed to exist when a Person owns, directly or indirectly, fifty percent (50%) or more of the outstanding voting securities or equity interests of the applicable entity. Notwithstanding the foregoing, no Limited Partner shall be deemed to be an Affiliate of the General Partner, the Sponsor, or any other Limited Partner solely by reason of such Limited Partner\'s investment in the Fund.

**\"Aggregate Commitments\"** means the aggregate Capital Commitments of all Partners (including the GP Commitment), as set forth in the Schedule of Partners, as the same may be updated from time to time. At the hard cap, Aggregate Commitments shall not exceed Two Billion Dollars (\$2,000,000,000).
**\"Associate\"** means any member, partner, managing director, principal, officer, director, employee, or agent of the General Partner, the Sponsor, or any of their respective Affiliates.

**\"Benefit Plan Investor\"** means a \"benefit plan investor\" as defined in 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101(f)(2), as modified by Section 3(42) of ERISA, including (a) any \"employee benefit plan\" as defined in Section 3(3) of ERISA that is subject to Part 4 of Subtitle B of Title I of ERISA, (b) any \"plan\" as defined in Section 4975(e)(1) of the Code that is subject to Section 4975 of the Code, and (c) any entity whose underlying assets include \"plan assets\" by reason of a plan\'s investment in such entity.

**\"Blocker Entity\"** means HGF V blocker Corp., a Delaware C corporation formed for the benefit of certain tax-exempt or non-U.S. Limited Partners to mitigate UBTI or effectively connected income concerns, as the General Partner may determine to be appropriate in connection with the Fund\'s investment program.

**\"Bridge Financing\"** means any short-term Fund-level borrowing (whether under the Subscription Credit Facility or otherwise) used to fund Portfolio Investments or other Partnership obligations in advance of or in lieu of issuing Capital Calls, which borrowing shall not remain outstanding for more than one hundred eighty (180) consecutive days from the date of the applicable borrowing.

**\"Business Day\"** means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or a day on which commercial banks in New York, New York or Wilmington, Delaware are authorized or required by law or executive order to remain closed.

**\"Capital Account\"** means, with respect to each Partner, the capital account established and maintained for such Partner in accordance with Section 704(b) of the Code and Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv), as further described in Section 6.1 of this Agreement.

**\"Capital Call\"** or **\"Drawdown Notice\"** means a written notice issued by the General Partner to the Partners requiring such Partners to fund all or a portion of their unfunded Capital Commitments, specifying the aggregate amount of such capital contribution, the purpose thereof, and the date on which such funds are due, in accordance with Section 4.2 of this Agreement.

**\"Capital Commitment\"** means, with respect to each Partner, the aggregate amount that such Partner has committed to contribute to the Partnership as capital contributions, as set forth in such Partner\'s Subscription Agreement and reflected in the Schedule of Partners, as the same may be updated from time to time.

**\"Carried Interest\"** means the General Partner\'s right to receive twenty percent (20%) of Net Profits distributed in excess of the Preferred Return, as more fully described in Section 8.2 of this Agreement (Tiers 3 and 4 of the distribution waterfall).
**\"Carry Distribution\"** means any Distribution of Carried Interest to the General Partner pursuant to Tier 3 or Tier 4 of the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 8.2.

**\"Catch-Up\"** or **\"GP Catch-Up\"** means the distribution priority described in Tier 3 of Section 8.2, pursuant to which eighty percent (80%) of distributable amounts are allocated to the General Partner and twenty percent (20%) to the Limited Partners until the cumulative distributions to the General Partner under Tier 3 and Tier 4 equal twenty percent (20%) of the sum of all cumulative distributions under Tiers 2, 3, and 4.

**\"Cause\"** means (a) the commission of fraud or willful misconduct by the General Partner, any Key Person, or any Associate acting on behalf of the General Partner in connection with the affairs of the Partnership; (b) a material breach by the General Partner of this Agreement that is not cured within the applicable cure period set forth in Section 12.6; or (c) the voluntary or involuntary bankruptcy, insolvency, receivership, or dissolution of the General Partner.
**\"Clawback Amount\"** means the amount of excess Carried Interest subject to return by the General Partner to the Partnership pursuant to Article IX of this Agreement.

**\"Code\"** means the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended from time to time, and any successor statute thereto. References to specific sections of the Code shall be deemed to include corresponding provisions of any successor statute.
**\"Commitment Period\"** has the meaning ascribed to the term \"Investment Period.\"

**\"Concentration Limit\"** means, with respect to any single Portfolio Investment, twenty percent (20%) of Aggregate Commitments, measured at the time of the initial commitment to such Portfolio Investment (i.e., a maximum of Four Hundred Million Dollars (\$400,000,000) at the hard cap of Two Billion Dollars (\$2,000,000,000)), as more fully described in Section 5.3(a).

**\"Defaulting Partner\"** means any Partner that fails to fund its share of a Capital Call by the applicable funding date, as set forth in Section 4.9 of this Agreement, and that has not cured such failure within five (5) Business Days of the funding date.

**\"Distribution\"** means any distribution of cash, securities, or other property by the Partnership to one or more Partners, whether as a return of capital, a share of income or gain, or otherwise, as determined by the General Partner in accordance with this Agreement.

**\"Early Close discount\"** means the ten (10) basis point reduction in the Management Fee rate applicable to Limited Partners admitted to the Partnership at the First Close, as described in Section 7.1(c) of this Agreement (resulting in a Management Fee rate of 1.65% per annum on Capital Commitments during the Investment Period, in lieu of 1.75%).

**\"ERISA\"** means the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended from time to time, and any successor statute thereto, together with all rules and regulations promulgated thereunder.

**\"Excess Organizational Expenses\"** means Organizational Expenses incurred by the Partnership in excess of Three Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$3,500,000), which Excess Organizational Expenses shall be borne solely by the Sponsor and shall not be charged to the Partnership or any Partner.

**\"Excluded Co-Investment\"** means a co-investment opportunity offered alongside the Fund to one or more Limited Partners or third parties in accordance with Section 5.4, which co-investment is made through a separate co-investment vehicle or on a direct basis and is not treated as a Portfolio Investment of the Fund for purposes of this Agreement.
**\"Final Close\"** means the last date on which Limited Partners may be admitted to the Partnership and Capital Commitments accepted, which date shall be no later than the Final Close Deadline.
**\"Final Close Deadline\"** means February 15, 2027, being eighteen (18) months after the target date of the First Close.

**\"First Close\"** means the initial closing of Capital Commitments to the Partnership, targeted for August 15, 2025, at which the General Partner shall have accepted Capital Commitments aggregating at least Seven Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$750,000,000) (or such lesser amount as the General Partner may determine in its sole discretion).

**\"Fiscal Year\"** means the calendar year commencing on January 1 and ending on December 31 of each year; *provided*, that the first Fiscal Year of the Partnership shall commence on the date of the First Close and shall end on December 31 of such calendar year, and the final Fiscal Year of the Partnership shall end on the date of the final distribution of all Partnership assets and cancellation of the Certificate of Limited Partnership.

**\"For-Cause Removal\"** means the removal of the General Partner for Cause by a vote of a majority in interest of the Limited Partners (excluding GP-affiliated Capital Commitments) in accordance with Section 12.6(b).
**\"Fund\"** means Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, a Delaware limited partnership formed pursuant to this Agreement.
**\"Fund Expenses\"** means the ordinary and recurring expenses of the Partnership borne by the Partnership, as more fully described in Section 7.4 of this Agreement.

**\"General Partner\"** or **\"GP\"** means Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, the sole member of which is Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, in its capacity as the sole general partner of the Partnership, and any successor general partner admitted to the Partnership in accordance with this Agreement.
**\"GP Catch-Up\"** has the meaning set forth in the definition of \"Catch-Up\" above.

**\"GP Commitment\"** means the Capital Commitment of the General Partner (or its Affiliates) to the Partnership, which shall be equal to two and one-half percent (2.5%) of Aggregate Commitments (equal to Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000) at the hard cap of Two Billion Dollars (\$2,000,000,000)). The GP Commitment shall be funded pari passu with Capital Calls to the Limited Partners and on the same terms and conditions as the Capital Commitments of the Limited Partners, except that no Management Fee shall be charged with respect to the GP Commitment.
